Listening runs the same simulation\nin reverse: it finds the head, the voice and the movements that would have\nproduced the sound it hears, and reads the speech off those movements. Nothing\nis recorded and nothing is learned by a neural network. The project is in the\npublic domain and is a gift to everyone.\n\nThis document is the single statement of where the project is going. It is\nupdated by every pull request that changes the direction; the history is at the\nend. The step-by-step plan that implements it is [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).\n\n## Principles\n\nThese are rules, not preferences. A change that breaks one of them is not\nmerged.\n\n1. **Physics and mathematics only.** Sound comes from simulated air, folds,\n   walls and turbulence. Recognition comes from inverting that simulation.\n   No neural network is used anywhere: not in the library, not in the app,\n   not in the tests and not in the tools that build the data tables. No\n   recorded speech is played back or concatenated. The exact boundary is in\n   [What counts as a neural network](#what-counts-as-a-neural-network).\n2. **One model, two directions.** Speaking and listening share the same head,\n   the same articulation channels, the same IPA inventory and the same\n   prosody rules. A feature is finished when it works both ways: whatever the\n   simulator can say, it can recognise, and every mode of speech it detects, it\n   can produce.\n3. **Always through IPA.** Text is never mapped to sound directly, and sound\n   is never mapped to text directly. Speaking is text in a language → IPA →\n   audio. Listening is audio → IPA → the language, or the mix of languages,\n   → text. IPA with its tone, stress, length and voice-quality marks is the\n   interchange format between every stage and between the two directions.\n4. **The highest quality the device can afford, never silence.** The most\n   accurate simulation is the reference. Every device gets the most detailed\n   variant it can run in real time, measured on that device in the background,\n   and the quality steps down while speaking the moment the device falls\n   behind. The same holds for listening.\n5. **It works at the bottom too.** Synthesis, recognition and voice copying\n   all work at the lowest settings: narrow-band audio, the cheapest solver, one\n   CPU core. More cores, a GPU and higher settings make it better, never make\n   it possible.\n6. **Everything that changes a voice is a parameter.** Anatomy, the vocal\n   folds, breathing, articulation habits, accent and expression are numbers\n   with physical units, documented ranges and sources. A voice is a set of\n   those numbers, so it can be edited, saved, copied from a recording and\n   compared.\n7. **Measured against real speech.** Claims of quality are backed by numbers\n   computed on public recordings of real people with transcripts, by\n   algorithms that are themselves free of neural networks, and by listening\n   tests with people. A claim that was not measured is written as a goal.\n8. **Reproducible.** The same input, seed and settings give the same samples\n   on every runtime. Results of experiments are committed with the script\n   that produced them.\n9. **Public domain.** The code is released under the Unlicense. Data that is\n   committed to the repository is public domain or CC0. Dependencies have\n   permissive licences. Anything else is fetched at test time and never\n   redistributed.\n\n## What the system does when the vision is reached\n\n### Speaking\n\n- Reads text in every supported language, normalises it, converts it to IPA\n  and speaks it with a voice that people cannot tell from a recording of a\n  person in a blind listening test. That is the meaning of \"state of the art\"\n  here, and it is a goal, not a current claim.\n- Speaks in every common mode of speech: statements, all kinds of questions,\n  exclamations, commands, lists and asides; lexical tones and pitch accents;\n  word stress and rhythm; regional and foreign accents; soft, normal, loud and\n  shouted speech with gradual changes of loudness; whisper, breathy, creaky,\n  pressed and falsetto voice; emotions and attitudes; breaths, laughter, sighs\n  and hesitations.\n- Simulates the voice source as a physical system (vocal folds driven by lung\n  pressure, coupled to the air below and above them), the turbulence at\n  constrictions, the losses in the walls and the radiation from the mouth and\n  nose, in 1D for speed and in full 3D for accuracy.\n- Highlights every syllable in the text at the moment it is spoken.\n\n### Listening\n\n- Takes a recording or a live microphone and returns IPA with times, the\n  language or languages spoken, and the text, using the simulation in reverse.\n- Recognises the same modes of speech that it can produce and writes them\n  down with the same marks: tones, stress, sentence type, loudness, whisper\n  and other voice qualities, emotion.\n- Highlights every syllable as it is recognised.\n\n### Copying a voice\n\n- Works in several passes that feed each other. The first pass fits the\n  configuration of the voice: the size and shape of the head, the vocal folds,\n  the habits of articulation. The second pass inverts the simulation with\n  that configuration to recover the movements and the phonemes. As the person\n  keeps speaking both estimates are refined until they are stable. From then\n  on the system holds a voice it can speak with and a recogniser tuned to that\n  speaker, and it can follow what the person says.\n- Reproduces a real recording: the copy says the same words with the same\n  timing, melody and voice quality, close enough to be measured against the\n  original.\n\n### Running everywhere\n\n- The simulation core is written in Rust. In browsers it runs as WebAssembly\n  in a background worker and is the default engine; the same core runs natively\n  in the command line tool and the server. The JavaScript implementation stays\n  as the readable reference and as the fallback.\n- A short benchmark runs in the background when the page loads, without sound\n  and without blocking the interface, and decides the precision for this\n  device. While speaking, the quality follows the measured load and changes\n  without a click or a gap.\n- It uses all CPU cores when the platform allows it and works on one core\n  when it does not.\n- Expensive tests (full 3D renders, recognition of datasets, voice copying)\n  run in manually triggered GitHub Actions workflows; the tests that run on\n  every pull request stay fast.\n\n## What counts as a neural network\n\nNot allowed, in the product, the tests, the build tools and the continuous\nintegration:\n\n- Artificial neural networks of any kind and size (perceptrons, convolutional,\n  recurrent, transformer and diffusion models), whether trained by this project\n  or downloaded.\n- Libraries whose purpose is to run or train them.\n- Scoring our output with neural models (for example neural speech recognisers\n  or neural quality predictors).\n\nAllowed:\n\n- Physical simulation and its inversion.\n- Closed-form mathematics and signal processing: Fourier and linear-prediction\n  analysis, filters, cepstra, autocorrelation.\n- Search and optimisation: dynamic programming, Viterbi decoding, least\n  squares, gradient descent on the parameters of the physical model,\n  derivative-free and evolutionary optimisers, Kalman and particle filters.\n- Tables with a documented source: pronunciation dictionaries, measured\n  anatomical dimensions, vowel formants, and counts taken from public text or\n  recordings (for example how often one phoneme follows another). Every table\n  is small enough to read, is produced by a committed script and names its\n  data.\n- Calibrating the constants of the rules and of the physical model against\n  recordings by optimisation.\n\nNeural systems remain the yardstick. Their published scores are quoted, and\ntheir audio may be one of the samples in a listening test with people. They\nare never a component.\n\n## Where the project is today\n\nVersion 0.11 speaks; it does not listen yet.\n\n| Area               | Today                                                                                                      | Gap to the vision                                                                                                        |\n| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| Languages          | English, Russian, Hindi and Mandarin Chinese to IPA, with text normalisation; Intelligibility measured by people and by our own recogniser.\n  Naturalness measured by people in blind comparisons that include real\n  recordings and other synthesisers. Features per word, from the frames of its vowels (`analyzeFrames`, `trackPitch`, `trackFormants`, `inverseFilter`, `mode-features.js`): `alpha` (alpha ratio, dB), `pitch` (median, Hz and semitones re the baseline), `f1` (mean F1 minus the baseline F1 of the same vowel, Hz; `null` without `options.voice`), `voiced` (voiced share of the vowel frames), `h1h2` (corrected for formants, dB), `hnr` (dB), `cpp` (dB), `jitter` (%), `rate` (syllables per second of the word and its two neighbours). `d` before a name below means \"minus the baseline\".\n36:4. Effort in decibels (inverse of `EFFORT_RULES` of #52): `Etilt = dalpha / 0.2`, `Epitch = dpitch in Hz / 5`, `Ef1 = df1 / 3.5`; `E = 0.6 * Etilt + 0.2 * Epitch + 0.2 * Ef1` (without `f1`: 0.75 and 0.25); `effort = clamp(0.5 + E / 40, 0, 1)`, rounded to the nearest of 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1. `confidence = max(0, 1 - |Etilt - Epitch| / 20)`.\n37-5. Type: **Feature**. Requirements of #11 covered: R6, R17, R18, R19 (see the [case study](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-11/README.md)).\\n\\n## Goal\\n\\nRecognition hears the melody of speech, not only the sounds: the four Mandarin tones and the neutral tone, which syllable of a word is stressed, which word is emphasised, and whether a sentence is a statement, a question or an exclamation. The answers are written with the same IPA marks the synthesiser reads (tone letters, `ˈ`, `ˌ`, `.`, `?`, `!`, `↗`, `↘`), and `text` gets punctuation and capital letters.\\n\\n## Why\\n\\nThe issue asks for tones, accents and intonation in both directions. Without tones, Mandarin text cannot be chosen: `ma˥` (妈) and `ma˨˩˦` (马) differ only in pitch. Without stress, Russian `за́мок` and `замо́к` are the same. Without the sentence type, `recognize` can never return a question mark.\\n\\n## Current state\\n\\n- The synthesiser writes these marks: `textToIpa('Are you coming?')` gives `ˈɑɹ ˈju ˈkʌmɪŋ ?`; `Where are you?` gives `ˈwɛɹ ˈɑɹ ˈju ↘ ?`; `Stop!` gives `ˈstɑp !`; `你好吗？` gives `ni˧˥ xɑʊ˨˩ ma ?`.\\n- Tone letters come from `TONE_CONTOURS` in `src/g2p/pinyin.js`: `˥`, `˧˥`, `˨˩˦`, `˨˩` (half third tone), `˥˩`, and nothing for the neutral tone. `parseIpa` turns them into `token.tone`, a list of levels 1 to 5.\\n- Pitch of a tone is `(level - 3) * scale` semitones around the base pitch (`syllablePitch()` in `src/articulation/prosody.js`); #49 replaces this by pitch targets that are approached during the syllable, and #51 adds the tunes of sentences (`TUNES`, `FOCUS`) with their sizes in semitones.\\n- An exclamation is spoken 1.5 semitones higher, with 1.3 times the pitch range and 1.41 times the amplitude (`REGISTERS.exclamation`).\\n- Nothing reads these things from audio. After #59, `trackPitch` gives pitch and voicing per frame; after #66, `audioToIpa` gives sounds with times, without tones, stress or sentence marks.\\n- Reference points from the research notes: people identify the four tones of spoken Mandarin 96.4 % right (Jiao and Xu 2019); a 1994 statistical recogniser reached 86.34 % on continuous speech (Wang, Shieh, Chen); people tell Mandarin questions without a particle from statements only 51 to 78 % right.\\n\\n## What to do\\n\\nCreate `src/recognition/prosody.js` with two exported functions. The first runs before `ipaToText` (#68), the second after it.\\n\\n1. `measureProsody(samples, sampleRate, sounds, options)`. `sounds` is the list `{ ipa, start, end, confidence }` made from `audioToIpa`. It returns `{ sounds, pitch, median, range }` where every vowel sound gets two new fields, `tones` and `prominence`:\\n   1. Call `trackPitch`. Convert voiced frames to semitones relative to `median`, the median pitch of all voiced frames (or the pitch of `options.voice`). `range` is the 95th minus the 5th percentile, at least 4.\\n   2. Syllables: one per vowel sound (the nucleus); the syllable lasts from the nucleus start to the next nucleus start or to the next pause.\\n   3. Tones. For each syllable take the voiced frames from the nucleus start to the syllable end and resample them to 10 points. For each tone of `TONE_CONTOURS` (five shapes and the neutral tone) compute the curve the synthesiser would make: call the function of #49 that turns the tone targets into a pitch curve, with the measured pitch at the first point as the starting pitch and `scale = range / 4`. The cost of a tone is the weighted root mean square difference in semitones, divided by 3 and cut at 1; the weight grows linearly from 0.5 at point 1 to 1.5 at point 10 (the end of a syllable is closest to its target). The neutral tone costs 0.3 less when the syllable is shorter than 60 % of the mean of its two neighbours. `tones` is `{ '˥': 0.1, '˧˥': 0.7, ... , '': 0.9 }`; with fewer than 3 voiced frames it is `null`.\\n   4. Prominence. For each nucleus measure: duration; mean energy in dB; energy above 500 Hz minus energy below 500 Hz in dB; highest pitch in semitones. Turn each into a z-score over all nuclei of the utterance. `prominence = 0.4 * duration + 0.2 * energy + 0.2 * balance` `+ 0.2 * pitch`.\\n2. Let the word search use these fields (`src/recognition/ipa-to-text.js`):\\n   - for a candidate word of `zh`, the tone part of the sound distance is `0.5 * sound.tones[tone of the candidate]` when `tones` is not `null`;\\n   - for a candidate of `en` or `ru` with two or more syllables, add `0.3` when its syllable with primary stress is not the most prominent of its nuclei. If that file is not in the code base yet, skip this step and say so in the pull request and in a comment on the issue of #68.\\n3. `markProsody(result, measured, options)` takes a result in the shape of `recognize` and returns a new one:\\n   1. Tones: for `zh` words, `syllables[].ipa` and `word.ipa` carry the tone letters of the chosen word. For a word that is not in the lexicon, write the cheapest tone of `tones`.\\n   2. Stress: `syllables[].stress` is the stress of the chosen word. For a word that is not in the lexicon and has two or more syllables, the most prominent syllable gets `stress: 1` and `ˈ`.\\n   3. Phrases: cut the words at pauses of 0.2 s or more.\\n   4. For the last 250 ms of voiced frames of each phrase compute `rise`: the median of the last 3 frames minus the median of the first 3, in semitones. Also `level` (phrase median minus `median`), `span` (95th minus 5th percentile of the phrase) and `loud` (phrase energy minus utterance energy, dB).\\n   5. Decide the mark at the end of each phrase, first rule that fits:\\n\\n      | Rule | Mark |\\n      | --- | --- |\\n      | a word of the phrase is a wh-word (`isWhWord` of the language) | `↘ ?` |\\n      | `zh`: the last word is `吗`; `hi`: the first word is `क्या` | `?` |\\n      | `en`: `rise >= 3`; `hi`: `rise >= 4` | `?` |\\n      | `ru`: inside one stressed syllable pitch rises 5 or more and the phrase ends below the start of that syllable | `?` |\\n      | `zh`: mean of the last third minus mean of the first third `>= 2` | `?` |\\n      | `level >= 1`, `span >= 1.2 * range` and `loud >= 2`, and the utterance has another phrase to compare with | `!` |\\n      | the phrase is not the last one and the pause is under 0.5 s | `,` |\\n      | anything else | `.` |\\n\\n      The numbers are the tune sizes of #51, a little smaller. Tune them with the tests and keep the table in the code comment.\\n\\n   6. Emphasis (`en`, `zh`): a word is emphasised when the pitch peak of its stressed syllable is 2 semitones or more above the line through the peaks of the other stressed syllables of the phrase, and the pitch span after the word is at most half of the span before it. Add `ˈˈ` before the word in `ipa` and a span to `modes` (step 5 below).\\n   7. Write the marks into `result.ipa` exactly as `textToIpa` writes them (`,`, `.`, `?`, `!`, `↗ ?`, `↘ ?`), so that `synthesize(result.ipa, { ipa: true })` speaks the same tune.\\n   8. Write `result.text`: the mark after the last word of the phrase (`hi`: `।` for `.`; `zh`: `，。？！`, no spaces); in `en` and `ru` the first letter of each sentence becomes a capital letter. Word objects keep their text without punctuation.\\n\\n4. What cannot be decided is left out, not guessed: a phrase with fewer than 5 voiced frames in its last 250 ms gets `.` at the end of the utterance and nothing elsewhere.\\n5. A span in `result.modes` has the shape of `plan.modes` of #50 plus four keys (the same in #71). Example:\\n\\n   ```text\\n   { start: 0.4, end: 0.9, from: 2, to: 3, emphasis: 1,\\n     notation: 'ˈˈ', confidence: 0.7 }\\n   ```\\n\\n   `start`, `end` are seconds; `from`, `to` are indexes into `result.words` (`to` exclusive); then only the decided keys of the mode object of #50 (here `emphasis: 1` or `tune: 'yesno'`); `notation` is the IPA mark or `null`; `confidence` is 0 to 1. Requirements of #11 covered: R6, R7, R11, R13, R18 (see the [case study](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-11/README.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\nA fixed list of 80 sentences (20 each for English, Russian, Hindi and Mandarin) is spoken by the simulator and recognised by `recognize`. The suite `roundtrip` of the heavy workflow measures how much of the text, the IPA, the syllable times and the language comes back, per audio tier and per preset voice, fails when a threshold is missed, and writes `docs/reports/roundtrip.md`. Three sentences run in every `npm test`.\n\n## Why\n\nRecognition is the simulation in reverse, so the simulator's own speech is the one input for which the right answer is known exactly: text, IPA and the time of every syllable. This is the regression baseline for every later change of the recogniser, and the proof that both directions work at 8000 Hz.\n\n## Current state\n\n- `synthesize(text, options)` returns an object with the keys `lang`, `accent`, `ipa`, `words`, `head`, `plan`, `timeline`, `sampleRate`, `samples` and `duration`. `timeline.words[].syllables[]` holds `ipa`, `stress`, `start`, `end` (seconds) and `text`.\n- Measured on this branch: the three smoke sentences below take 0.11 to 0.27 s each to synthesise at tier `minimal` (22050 Hz, 1.9 to 2.3 s of audio).\n- The 80 sentences were checked with the current text-to-IPA code. They give about 214 s of speech and contain 40 different phone symbols in English, 47 in Russian, 50 in Hindi and 40 in Mandarin, all four Mandarin tones, the half-third tone and the neutral tone, and statements, yes/no questions, question-word questions, exclamations and one-word sentences in each language. Steps:\n   1. `spoken = synthesize(text, { lang, tier, preset, seed })`.\n   2. `heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level })` with `level = levelForTier(tier)`. For `zh` the tokens are the characters;\n      - `toneErrors` (only `zh`): edit distance between the two lists of tones, one entry per syllable (the tone letters in the syllable's IPA, the empty string for the neutral tone);\n      - `stressHits` (only `en`, `ru`): among the reference words with two or more syllables whose recognised word has the same number of syllables, how many have `stress: 1` on the same syllable;\n      - `timeErrors`: pair the reference and recognised syllables through the edit-distance path over syllable IPA; for each pair with equal IPA collect `|start difference|` and `|end difference|` in ms;\n      - `languageRight`: `heard.languages[0].language === lang` after sorting by `share`, largest first;\n      - `sentenceMark`: the last of `. ? !` in `heard.text`, with `।`, `。`, `？`, `！` mapped to their ASCII form, or `null`.\n3. Create `tests/helpers/roundtrip.js` exporting `roundTrip(text, options)` with `options = { lang, tier, preset, seed }`. Steps:\n   1. `spoken = synthesize(text, { lang, tier, preset, seed })`.\n   2. `heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level })` with `level = levelForTier(tier)`. Do not pass the language: it must be found.\n   3. Return `{ spoken, heard, seconds }` plus these numbers, computed with `errorRate` and `editDistance` of #18:\n      - `per`: `errorRate(spoken.ipa, heard.ipa, 'phone')`;\n      - `wer` (not for `zh`) and `cer`: `errorRate(text, heard.text, unit)` with `'word'` and `'char'`;\n      - `soundWer`: the same as `wer`, but each word of both texts is first replaced by its IPA from `textToIpa(...).words[].ipa`, so that a word which sounds the same (`sea` and `see`, 他 and 她) is not an error. For `zh` the tokens are the characters;\n      - `toneErrors` (only `zh`): edit distance between the two lists of tones, one entry per syllable (the tone letters in the syllable's IPA, the empty string for the neutral tone);\n      - `stressHits` (only `en`, `ru`): among the reference words with two or more syllables whose recognised word has the same number of syllables, how many have `stress: 1` on the same syllable;\n      - `timeErrors`: pair the reference and recognised syllables through the edit-distance path over syllable IPA; for each pair with equal IPA collect `|start difference|` and `|end difference|` in ms;\n      - `languageRight`: `heard.languages[0].language === lang` after sorting by `share`, largest first;\n      - `sentenceMark`: the last of `. ? !` in `heard.text`, with `।`, `。`, `？`, `！` mapped to their ASCII form, or `null`.\n3. Part of the [roadmap](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP.md) planned in #11 (Roadmap 4: Reverse simulation (listening)). Type: **Feature**. Requirements of #11 covered: R6, R7, R11, R13, R18 (see the [case study](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-11/README.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\nA fixed list of 80 sentences (20 each for English, Russian, Hindi and Mandarin) is spoken by the simulator and recognised by `recognize`. The suite `roundtrip` of the heavy workflow measures how much of the text, the IPA, the syllable times and the language comes back, per audio tier and per preset voice, fails when a threshold is missed, and writes `docs/reports/roundtrip.md`. Three sentences run in every `npm test`.\n\n## Why\n\nRecognition is the simulation in reverse, so the simulator's own speech is the one input for which the right answer is known exactly: text, IPA and the time of every syllable. This is the regression baseline for every later change of the recogniser, and the proof that both directions work at 8000 Hz.\n\n## Current state\n\n- `synthesize(text, options)` returns an object with the keys `lang`, `accent`, `ipa`, `words`, `head`, `plan`, `timeline`, `sampleRate`, `samples` and `duration`. `timeline.words[].syllables[]` holds `ipa`, `stress`, `start`, `end` (seconds) and `text`.\n- Measured on this branch: the three smoke sentences below take 0.11 to 0.27 s each to synthesise at tier `minimal` (22050 Hz, 1.9 to 2.3 s of audio).\n- The 80 sentences were checked with the current text-to-IPA code. They give about 214 s of speech and contain 40 different phone symbols in English, 47 in Russian, 50 in Hindi and 40 in Mandarin, all four Mandarin tones, the half-third tone and the neutral tone, and statements, yes/no questions, question-word questions, exclamations and one-word sentences in each language. There are no digits and no erhua (see #46 and #43).\n- `HEAD_PRESET_NAMES` is `['any', 'male', 'female', 'child']`. Tiers today: `minimal`, `low`, `medium` (waveguide), `high`, `ultra`, `studio`, `reference` (3D). #26 adds `telephone`, `narrowband` and `wideband`.\n- There is no recogniser, so no round-trip test exists: `ls tests/heavy` and `grep -rn roundtrip tests` find nothing.\n\n## What to do\n\n1. Create `tests/fixtures/roundtrip/sentences.json`: an object with the keys `en`, `ru`, `hi`, `zh`; each value is an array of 20 strings, in this order. In the lists below the sentences are separated by `|`; line breaks and the spaces around `|` are not part of a sentence.\n\n   ```text\n   en: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. | She sells sea shells by\n   the sea shore. | Did you measure the treasure yesterday? | Why does the\n   young judge enjoy choosing cheap toys? | What a beautiful morning! | Thick\n   fog lay over the smooth path. | They usually think about their father and\n   mother. | A large ship sailed around the island at noon. | Are the children\n   playing outside now? | Please bring me a cup of hot tea, some bread and a\n   book. | How far is the nearest hospital? | The singer was ringing a long\n   bell. | I want to record a new record today. | Our tour of the pure air was\n   sure to end. | Stop! | He could not hear the boy's voice clearly. | We will\n   visit the zoo on Thursday. | Is this your pen or mine? | The photographer\n   took a photograph of the banana tree. | Yes.\n\n   ru: Съешь же ещё этих мягких французских булок, да выпей чаю. | Привет, как\n   дела? | Сегодня хорошая погода. | Ты идёшь домой? | घोड़ा तेज़\n   दौड़ता है। | झंडा ऊँचा रहे हमारा। | छोटी चिड़िया पेड़ पर बैठी है। | ढोल की आवाज़\n   दूर तक जाती है। | मैं पढ़ाई में व्यस्त नहीं हूँ, थोड़ा धीरे बोलिए। | फल, सब्ज़ी और\n   दूध ले आओ। | यह किताब किसकी है? Create `tests/helpers/roundtrip.js` exporting `roundTrip(text, options)` with `options = { lang, tier, preset, seed }`. Steps:\n   1. `spoken = synthesize(text, { lang, tier, preset, seed })`.\n   2. `heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level })` with `level = levelForTier(tier)`. Do not pass the language: it must be found.\n   3. Return `{ spoken, heard, seconds }` plus these numbers, computed with `errorRate` and `editDistance` of #18:\n      - `per`: `errorRate(spoken.ipa, heard.ipa, 'phone')`;\n      - `wer` (not for `zh`) and `cer`: `errorRate(text, heard.text, unit)` with `'word'` and `'char'`;\n      - `soundWer`: the same as `wer`, but each word of both texts is first replaced by its IPA from `textToIpa(...).words[].ipa`, so that a word which sounds the same (`sea` and `see`, 他 and 她) is not an error. For `zh` the tokens are the characters;\n      - `toneErrors` (only `zh`): edit distance between the two lists of tones, one entry per syllable (the tone letters in the syllable's IPA, the empty string for the neutral tone);\n      - `stressHits` (only `en`, `ru`): among the reference words with two or more syllables whose recognised word has the same number of syllables, how many have `stress: 1` on the same syllable;\n      - `timeErrors`: pair the reference and recognised syllables through the edit-distance path over syllable IPA; for each pair with equal IPA collect `|start difference|` and `|end difference|` in ms;\n      - `languageRight`: `heard.languages[0].language === lang` after sorting by `share`, largest first;\n      - `sentenceMark`: the last of `. ? !` in `heard.text`, with `।`, `。`, `？`, `！` mapped to their ASCII form, or `null`.\n3. Create `tests/heavy/roundtrip-sentences.test.js`. Seed 1 everywhere. Runs:\n   - set `main`: all 80 sentences, tiers `telephone`, `narrowband`, `wideband`, `minimal`, presets `male` and `female` (640 runs);\n   - set `voices`: sentences 1 to 5 of each language, presets `any` and `child`, tiers `telephone` and `wideband` (80 runs);\n   - set `tiers`: sentences 2 and 20 of each language, preset `male`, tiers `low`, `medium`, `high`, `ultra`, `studio` (40 runs). `reference` is left out because of its run time; say so in the report.\n   - `heavyLimit(80)` limits the number of sentences per set.\n   - Sum the edit distances and the reference lengths per language, tier and set before dividing; do not average the rates of single sentences.\n4. Gates (one `it` per row, so that a failure names the row). They hold for every language of set `main`:\n\n   | Tier | PER | soundWer | Tone errors | Syllable time, mean | Language right |\n   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n   | `wideband`, `minimal` | ≤ 5 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 30 ms | ≥ 95 % |\n   | `narrowband` | ≤ 8 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 12 % | ≤ 35 ms | ≥ 92 % |\n   | `telephone` | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 20 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 40 ms | ≥ 90 % |\n\n   Set `voices`: the gates of row `telephone` for every preset. Set `tiers`: PER ≤ 10 % per tier. Stress hits ≥ 90 % (`en`, `ru`) from `narrowband` up. `wer`, `cer`, `sentenceMark` and the real-time factor of `recognize` (`seconds` divided by audio seconds) are reported without a gate; the sentence mark gets its gate in #70.\n\n5. If the first full run misses a gate, do not loosen it. Read the report (it lists the 20 worst sentences with reference and recognised IPA), fix the stage that loses most, and run again. The gates are the result this issue must deliver.\n6. Mode check, only when `parseMarkup` of #50 is exported (else the test is skipped with the reason in its name): speak sentence 1 of each language once whispered and once loud with the markup of #50; report the share of mode spans that come back in `heard.modes` with the same notation and at least 50 % overlap in time. This issue sets no gate of its own for modes: the numbers belong to #70 (sentence mark), #71 (mode labels) and #72 (set `whisper`). Each of them adds its gate to this test when this test exists. For each of the three that is merged already while its gate is missing here, add the gate in this issue with the numbers of that issue's acceptance criteria.\n7. Write the report with `writeReport('roundtrip', markdown, data)`: one table per set (rows: language × tier; columns: the numbers above), then the 20 worst sentences. Copy the report of the full run to `docs/reports/roundtrip.md` and commit it with the run link, the commit hash and the date at the top.\n8. Smoke test `tests/roundtrip-smoke.test.js` (part of `npm test`): sentence 18 of `en`, 2 of `ru` and 2 of `zh`; tier `telephone`, preset `male`, seed 1. Expect `per.rate <= 0.1`, `soundWer.rate === 0` and `languageRight`.\n9. Add the suite and the report to `tests/heavy/README.md` and to `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` (section \"Heavy checks\").\n\n## Tests\n\n- `tests/roundtrip-smoke.test.js`: the three `it` blocks of step 8, named `round trip en`, `round trip ru`, `round trip zh`.\n- `tests/roundtrip-helper.test.js` (fast, stub recogniser passed as `options.recognize`): `counts a homophone as right` (`sea` heard as `see` gives `wer.distance === 1` and `soundWer.distance === 0`); `counts tones` (one wrong tone letter gives `toneErrors.distance === 1`); `measures syllable times` (a result shifted by 20 ms gives a mean of 20 ms).\n- `has 20 sentences per language`: `sentences.json` has four keys with 20 non-empty strings each and no digit.\n- `tests/heavy/roundtrip-sentences.test.js` as described above.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `node --test tests/roundtrip-smoke.test.js` passes in less than 30 s on one core.\n- [ ] `npm run test:heavy -- --suite roundtrip --limit 2` passes locally and writes `reports/heavy/roundtrip.md`.\n- [ ] A run of `Heavy checks` with `suite=roundtrip` on the pull request branch is green: every gate of step 4 holds. #75\n\n## Changes\n\n- Add the fixed 80-sentence corpus, three strict telephone smoke tests, and a heavy round-trip benchmark covering four languages, four seeded voice presets, and nine audio tiers. Report phone, word, character, tone, stress, timing, language, punctuation, mode, and recognition speed measurements. The recognizer receives only samples, sample rate, and tier level. The report shows male and female measurements separately, counts each recording once in the 20 worst results, and keeps the combined gate values. [Benchmark report](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/issue-75-d83d002e01c2/docs/reports/roundtrip.md)\n- Recover interrupted whispers at 8 kHz in JavaScript and Rust. Type: **Feature**. Requirements of #11 covered: R6, R7, R11, R13, R18 (see the [case study](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-11/README.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\nA fixed list of 80 sentences (20 each for English, Russian, Hindi and Mandarin) is spoken by the simulator and recognised by `recognize`. The suite `roundtrip` of the heavy workflow measures how much of the text, the IPA, the syllable times and the language comes back, per audio tier and per preset voice, fails when a threshold is missed, and writes `docs/reports/roundtrip.md`. Three sentences run in every `npm test`.\n\n## Why\n\nRecognition is the simulation in reverse, so the simulator's own speech is the one input for which the right answer is known exactly: text, IPA and the time of every syllable. This is the regression baseline for every later change of the recogniser, and the proof that both directions work at 8000 Hz.\n\n## Current state\n\n- `synthesize(text, options)` returns an object with the keys `lang`, `accent`, `ipa`, `words`, `head`, `plan`, `timeline`, `sampleRate`, `samples` and `duration`. `timeline.words[].syllables[]` holds `ipa`, `stress`, `start`, `end` (seconds) and `text`.\n- Measured on this branch: the three smoke sentences below take 0.11 to 0.27 s each to synthesise at tier `minimal` (22050 Hz, 1.9 to 2.3 s of audio).\n- The 80 sentences were checked with the current text-to-IPA code. They give about 214 s of speech and contain 40 different phone symbols in English, 47 in Russian, 50 in Hindi and 40 in Mandarin, all four Mandarin tones, the half-third tone and the neutral tone, and statements, yes/no questions, question-word questions, exclamations and one-word sentences in each language. There are no digits and no erhua (see #46 and #43).\n- `HEAD_PRESET_NAMES` is `['any', 'male', 'female', 'child']`. | Зимой в лесу тихо и темно. | Объявление висит на\n   двери подъезда. | Хитрый юный герой рисует шар. | Он не пришёл, потому что\n   болел. | Стой! | Вчера я видел большую белую птицу. | Почему ты молчишь? Create `tests/helpers/roundtrip.js` exporting `roundTrip(text, options)` with `options = { lang, tier, preset, seed }`. Steps:\n   1. `spoken = synthesize(text, { lang, tier, preset, seed })`.\n   2. `heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level })` with `level = levelForTier(tier)`. Do not pass the language: it must be found.\n   3. Return `{ spoken, heard, seconds }` plus these numbers, computed with `errorRate` and `editDistance` of #18:\n      - `per`: `errorRate(spoken.ipa, heard.ipa, 'phone')`;\n      - `wer` (not for `zh`) and `cer`: `errorRate(text, heard.text, unit)` with `'word'` and `'char'`;\n      - `soundWer`: the same as `wer`, but each word of both texts is first replaced by its IPA from `textToIpa(...).words[].ipa`, so that a word which sounds the same (`sea` and `see`, 他 and 她) is not an error. For `zh` the tokens are the characters;\n      - `toneErrors` (only `zh`): edit distance between the two lists of tones, one entry per syllable (the tone letters in the syllable's IPA, the empty string for the neutral tone);\n      - `stressHits` (only `en`, `ru`): among the reference words with two or more syllables whose recognised word has the same number of syllables, how many have `stress: 1` on the same syllable;\n      - `timeErrors`: pair the reference and recognised syllables through the edit-distance path over syllable IPA; for each pair with equal IPA collect `|start difference|` and `|end difference|` in ms;\n      - `languageRight`: `heard.languages[0].language === lang` after sorting by `share`, largest first;\n      - `sentenceMark`: the last of `. ? !` in `heard.text`, with `।`, `。`, `？`, `！` mapped to their ASCII form, or `null`.\n3. Create `tests/heavy/roundtrip-sentences.test.js`. Seed 1 everywhere. Runs:\n   - set `main`: all 80 sentences, tiers `telephone`, `narrowband`, `wideband`, `minimal`, presets `male` and `female` (640 runs);\n   - set `voices`: sentences 1 to 5 of each language, presets `any` and `child`, tiers `telephone` and `wideband` (80 runs);\n   - set `tiers`: sentences 2 and 20 of each language, preset `male`, tiers `low`, `medium`, `high`, `ultra`, `studio` (40 runs). `reference` is left out because of its run time; say so in the report.\n   - `heavyLimit(80)` limits the number of sentences per set.\n   - Sum the edit distances and the reference lengths per language, tier and set before dividing; do not average the rates of single sentences.\n4. Gates (one `it` per row, so that a failure names the row). They hold for every language of set `main`:\n\n   | Tier | PER | soundWer | Tone errors | Syllable time, mean | Language right |\n   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n   | `wideband`, `minimal` | ≤ 5 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 30 ms | ≥ 95 % |\n   | `narrowband` | ≤ 8 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 12 % | ≤ 35 ms | ≥ 92 % |\n   | `telephone` | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 20 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 40 ms | ≥ 90 % |\n\n   Set `voices`: the gates of row `telephone` for every preset. Set `tiers`: PER ≤ 10 % per tier. Stress hits ≥ 90 % (`en`, `ru`) from `narrowband` up. `wer`, `cer`, `sentenceMark` and the real-time factor of `recognize` (`seconds` divided by audio seconds) are reported without a gate; the sentence mark gets its gate in #70.\n\n5. If the first full run misses a gate, do not loosen it. Read the report (it lists the 20 worst sentences with reference and recognised IPA), fix the stage that loses most, and run again. The gates are the result this issue must deliver.\n6. Mode check, only when `parseMarkup` of #50 is exported (else the test is skipped with the reason in its name): speak sentence 1 of each language once whispered and once loud with the markup of #50; report the share of mode spans that come back in `heard.modes` with the same notation and at least 50 % overlap in time. This issue sets no gate of its own for modes: the numbers belong to #70 (sentence mark), #71 (mode labels) and #72 (set `whisper`). Each of them adds its gate to this test when this test exists. For each of the three that is merged already while its gate is missing here, add the gate in this issue with the numbers of that issue's acceptance criteria.\n7. Write the report with `writeReport('roundtrip', markdown, data)`: one table per set (rows: language × tier; columns: the numbers above), then the 20 worst sentences. Copy the report of the full run to `docs/reports/roundtrip.md` and commit it with the run link, the commit hash and the date at the top.\n8. Smoke test `tests/roundtrip-smoke.test.js` (part of `npm test`): sentence 18 of `en`, 2 of `ru` and 2 of `zh`; tier `telephone`, preset `male`, seed 1. Expect `per.rate \u003c= 0.1`, `soundWer.rate === 0` and `languageRight`.\n9. Add the suite and the report to `tests/heavy/README.md` and to `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` (section \"Heavy checks\").\n\n## Tests\n\n- `tests/roundtrip-smoke.test.js`: the three `it` blocks of step 8, named `round trip en`, `round trip ru`, `round trip zh`.\n- `tests/roundtrip-helper.test.js` (fast, stub recogniser passed as `options.recognize`): `counts a homophone as right` (`sea` heard as `see` gives `wer.distance === 1` and `soundWer.distance === 0`); `counts tones` (one wrong tone letter gives `toneErrors.distance === 1`); `measures syllable times` (a result shifted by 20 ms gives a mean of 20 ms).\n- `has 20 sentences per language`: `sentences.json` has four keys with 20 non-empty strings each and no digit.\n- `tests/heavy/roundtrip-sentences.test.js` as described above.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `node --test tests/roundtrip-smoke.test.js` passes in less than 30 s on one core.\n- [ ] `npm run test:heavy -- --suite roundtrip --limit 2` passes locally and writes `reports/heavy/roundtrip.md`.\n- [ ] A run of `Heavy checks` with `suite=roundtrip` on the pull request branch is green: every gate of step 4 holds. Steps:\\n   1. `spoken = synthesize(text, { lang, tier, preset, seed })`.\\n   2. `heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level })` with `level = levelForTier(tier)`. Accept a\n  // close cross-solver match only with a clear margin over the next reading.\n  if (\n    !exactOnly &&\n    best?.cost <= 1.8 &&\n    rival &&\n    best.cost * 1.5 < rival.cost\n  ) {\n    return best;\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nfunction audibleBounds(samples) {\n  let peak = 0;\n  for (const sample of samples) {\n    peak = Math.max(peak, Math.abs(sample));\n  }\n  const threshold = Math.max(0.00001, peak * 0.001);\n  const above = (sample) => Math.abs(sample) > threshold;\n  return [samples.findIndex(above) / RATE, samples.findLastIndex(above) / RATE];\n}\n\nfunction phonationFor(spans, onset, offset) {\n  if (!spans.length) {\n    return 'modal';\n  }\n  const [span] = spans;\n  if (\n    spans.length === 1 &&\n    span.start <= onset + 0.1 &&\n    span.end >= offset - 0.1\n  ) {\n    return 'whisper';\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nfunction unvoicedRun(frontEnd, onset, offset) {\n  const { frames, pitch } = frontEnd;\n  const runs = whisperSpeechRuns(frames);\n  const [run] = runs;\n  if (\n    runs.length !== 1 ||\n    run.start > onset + 0.1 ||\n    run.end < offset - 0.1 ||\n    pitch.f0.subarray(run.from, run.to).some((f0) => f0 > 0)\n  ) {\n    return null;\n  }\n  return { start: run.start, end: run.end };\n}\n\nfunction hasQuietEdges(duration, onset, offset) {\n  // The planner's 60 ms lead allows anticipatory motion before the first\n  // sound. Requiring this quiet lead avoids a lexicon search on running speech.\n  return onset >= 0.03 && onset <= 0.09 && duration - offset >= 0.08;\n}\n\nfunction availablePhonation(frontEnd, onset, offset, matchKnownVoice) {\n  const phonation = phonationFor(frontEnd.whisperSpans, onset, offset);\n  const unconfirmed =\n    matchKnownVoice && phonation === 'modal'\n      ? unvoicedRun(frontEnd, onset, offset)\n      : null;\n  const whispered = Boolean(unconfirmed) || phonation === 'whisper';\n  return whispered || (phonation && !matchKnownVoice)\n    ? { whispered, unconfirmed }\n    : null;\n}\n\nfunction renderedSegments(plan, cost, withWords) {\n  return phonesOf(plan.segments).map(({ token, start, end }) => ({\n    ipa: decoderUnit(token) + (token.symbol.includes('ː') ? 'ː' : ''),\n    kind: token.kind,\n    start,\n    end,\n    cost,\n    confidence: Math.exp(-cost),\n    long: token.symbol.includes('ː'),\n    ...(withWords && { modelWord: token.word }),\n  }));\n}\n\n/** Refine an isolated two-vowel reading only if a full render agrees. */\nexport function matchWhisperPhones(samples, sampleRate, analysis, reading) {\n  const { voice, whisperSpans } = analysis;\n  const { language = 'en', symbols } = reading;\n  const [span] = whisperSpans;\n  const vowels = reading.segments.filter(({ kind }) => kind === 'vowel');\n  if (vowels.length < 2) {\n    return null;\n  }\n  const first = vowels[0].ipa;\n  const last = vowels.at(-1).ipa;\n  const timing = timingOptions(language, voice);\n  const candidates = symbols.filter(\n    (ipa) => parseIpa(ipa).tokens[0]?.kind === 'consonant'\n  );\n  let rows;\n  for (const consonant of candidates) {\n    const phones = first + consonant + last;\n    const segments = planFor(phones, timing, true);\n    // An untrimmed render has a known lead and tail and rounds up to a sample.\n    if (\n      Math.abs(segments.at(-1).end * sampleRate - samples.length) > 1.00001 ||\n      span.start > segments[0].end + 0.05 ||\n      span.end < segments.at(-1).start - 0.05\n    ) {\n      continue;\n    }\n    const render = synthesize(forPhonation(phones, true), {\n      ...RENDER,\n      lang: language,\n      head: voice,\n    });\n    rows ??= features(samples, sampleRate, true);\n    const output = features(render.samples, render.sampleRate, true);\n    const count = Math.min(rows.length, output.length);\n    const cost = renderError(rows, output, 0, count);\n    if (count && cost <= CLOSE_RENDER_ERROR) {\n      return {\n        segments: renderedSegments(render.plan, cost, false),\n        cost,\n        confidence: Math.exp(-cost),\n      };\n    }\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\n/** The simulation model is limited to short intact recordings at these rates. */\nexport function matchableRecording(duration, sourceRate, rate, languages) {\n  return (\n    rate === RATE &&\n    SOURCE_RATES.has(sourceRate) &&\n    languages?.includes('en') &&\n    duration >= 0.3 &&\n    duration <= MAX_SECONDS\n  );\n}\n\n/** Return an IPA reading when duration and the reconstructed audio both agree. */\nexport function matchSimulation(\n  samples,\n  sampleRate,\n  { languages, voice, sourceRate, trace, matchKnownVoice },\n  analyze\n) {\n  const duration = samples.length / sampleRate;\n  if (\n    !matchableRecording(duration, sourceRate, sampleRate, languages) ||\n    (voice && !matchKnownVoice)\n  ) {\n    return null;\n  }\n  const [onset, offset] = audibleBounds(samples);\n  if (!hasQuietEdges(duration, onset, offset)) {\n    return null;\n  }\n  const frontEnd = analyze();\n  const { whisperSpans } = frontEnd;\n  const mode = availablePhonation(frontEnd, onset, offset, matchKnownVoice);\n  if (!mode) {\n    return null;\n  }\n  const { whispered, unconfirmed } = mode;\n  const model = englishModel(whispered, voice);\n  const endings = model.endings.flatMap(({ mark, duration: tail }) => {\n    const stop = duration - tail;\n    return Math.abs(stop - offset) < 0.06 ? [{ mark, stop }] : [];\n  });\n  if (!endings.length) {\n    return null;\n  }\n  const rows = features(samples, sampleRate, whispered);\n  rows.forEach((row, index) => {\n    row.index = index;\n  });\n  const proposals = propose(rows, model, endings, matchKnownVoice);\n  trace?.({ stage: 'proposals', proposals });\n  const best = verifiedReading(\n    rows,\n    model,\n    proposals,\n    whispered,\n    matchKnownVoice,\n    trace\n  );\n  if (!best) {\n    return null;\n  }\n  return {\n    ipa: best.ipa,\n    segments: renderedSegments(best.plan, best.cost, whispered),\n    whisperSpans: unconfirmed\n      ? [{ ...unconfirmed, confidence: Math.exp(-best.cost) }]\n      : whisperSpans,\n    cost: best.cost,\n    confidence: Math.exp(-best.cost),\n  };\n}\n/** Public audio recognition and shared batch/stream composition. Unlicense. */\nimport { resample } from '../audio/resample.js';\nimport { LANGUAGES } from '../g2p/index.js';\nimport { registeredLexicons } from '../g2p/lexicon.js';\nimport { decoderWhisperSpans } from './decode-pipeline.js';\nimport { audioToIpa, audioToIpaParallel } from './decode.js';\nimport { createRecognitionEngine, getRecognitionEngine } from './engine.js';\nimport { ipaToText } from './ipa-to-text.js';\nimport { identifyLanguage, languageShares } from './language-id.js';\nimport { measure } from './profile.js';\nimport { recognizeModes } from './modes.js';\nimport { markProsody, measureProsody } from './prosody.js';\nimport {\n  applyRescoring,\n  planRescoring,\n  rescoreHypotheses,\n  scoreJob,\n} from './rescoring.js';\nimport { RESCORING_WEIGHT } from './rescoring-weights.js';\nimport { createRecognitionPool } from './pool.js';\nimport { aggregate, translated } from './recognizer-result.js';\nimport { pauseCuts } from './recognizer-pauses.js';\n\nexport { createRecognizer } from './recognizer-stream.js';\n\nexport const RECOGNITION_LEVELS = Object.freeze({\n  low: Object.freeze({ rate: 8000, hop: 0.01, beam: 8 }),\n  medium: Object.freeze({ rate: 16000, hop: 0.005, beam: 32 }),\n  high: Object.freeze({ rate: 16000, hop: 0.005, beam: 128 }),\n});\n\nexport function levelForTier(name) {\n  if (name === 'telephone' || name === 'narrowband') {\n    return 'low';\n  }\n  return ['wideband', 'minimal', 'low'].includes(name) ? 'medium' : 'high';\n}\n\nexport class RecognitionError extends Error {\n  constructor(code, message = code) {\n    super(message);\n    this.name = 'RecognitionError';\n    this.code = code;\n  }\n}\n\nfunction checkOptions(languages, nbest, level) {\n  if (\n    !Array.isArray(languages) ||\n    !languages.length ||\n    new Set(languages).size !== languages.length ||\n    languages.some((language) => !Object.hasOwn(LANGUAGES, language))\n  ) {\n    throw new RangeError('languages must contain distinct supported codes');\n  }\n  if (!Number.isInteger(nbest) || nbest < 1 || nbest > 10) {\n    throw new RangeError('nbest must be an integer from 1 to 10');\n  }\n  if (level !== 'auto' && !Object.hasOwn(RECOGNITION_LEVELS, level)) {\n    throw new RangeError('level must be auto, low, medium or high');\n  }\n}\n\nexport function recognitionSettings(options) {\n  const {\n    languages = Object.keys(LANGUAGES),\n    voice = null,\n    nbest = 1,\n    segments = false,\n    rescoring = false,\n    modes = true,\n    includeModeLabels = modes,\n    whisper = 'auto',\n    level = 'auto',\n    stages = {},\n    profile,\n    deterministic = false,\n    articulationOffsets,\n  } = options;\n  checkOptions(languages, nbest, level);\n  if (rescoring && typeof rescoreHypotheses !== 'function') {\n    throw new RecognitionError(\n      'rescoring-unavailable',\n      'IPA rescoring is unavailable'\n    );\n  }\n  return {\n    languages: [...languages],\n    voice,\n    nbest,\n    segments,\n    rescoring,\n    modes,\n    includeModeLabels,\n    whisper: decoderWhisperSpans(whisper),\n    level,\n    stages,\n    profile,\n    kernels: options.kernels ?? getRecognitionEngine(options),\n    deterministic,\n    articulationOffsets,\n  };\n}\n\nexport function validateRate(sampleRate) {\n  if (\n    !Number.isFinite(sampleRate) ||\n    sampleRate < 8000 ||\n    sampleRate > 192000\n  ) {\n    throw new RangeError('sampleRate must be from 8000 to 192000 Hz');\n  }\n}\n\nexport function validateSamples(samples) {\n  for (let i = 0; i < samples.length; i++) {\n    if (!Number.isFinite(samples[i])) {\n      throw new RangeError('Audio samples must be finite');\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nexport function decoderOptions(settings, level, start = 0) {\n  const { languages, voice, nbest, rescoring, whisper } = settings;\n  return {\n    ...RECOGNITION_LEVELS[level],\n    languages,\n    profile: settings.profile,\n    kernels: settings.kernels,\n    language: languages.length === 1 ? languages[0] : undefined,\n    voice,\n    articulationOffsets: settings.articulationOffsets,\n    nbest: rescoring ? 10 : nbest,\n    whisper:\n      start && Array.isArray(whisper)\n        ? whisper\n            .filter(({ end }) => end > start)\n            .map((span) => ({\n              ...span,\n              start: Math.max(0, span.start - start),\n              end: span.end - start,\n            }))\n        : whisper,\n  };\n}\n\nfunction decodeInput(samples, sampleRate, settings, level, start) {\n  const options = decoderOptions(settings, level, start);\n  const rate = Math.min(sampleRate, options.rate);\n  const input =\n    rate < sampleRate ? resample(samples, sampleRate, rate) : samples;\n  return { input, rate, options };\n}\n\nexport function decodeRecognitionAudio(\n  samples,\n  sampleRate,\n  settings,\n  level,\n  start\n) {\n  const { input, rate, options } = decodeInput(\n    samples,\n    sampleRate,\n    settings,\n    level,\n    start\n  );\n  const decoded = settings.stages.audioToIpa\n    ? settings.stages.audioToIpa(input, rate, options)\n    : audioToIpa(input, rate, {\n        ...options,\n        sourceRate: sampleRate,\n        lattice: settings.rescoring,\n      });\n  return { decoded, input, rate };\n}\n\nexport function emptyRecognition(nbest, segments = false) {\n  const result = {\n    ipa: '',\n    text: '',\n    languages: [],\n    words: [],\n    modes: [],\n    voice: null,\n  };\n  if (nbest > 1) {\n    result.alternatives = [];\n  }\n  if (segments) {\n    result.segments = [];\n  }\n  return result;\n}\n\nfunction timedPhones(decoded) {\n  return decoded.segments?.length\n    ? decoded.segments.flatMap((segment) => {\n        if (segment.kind !== 'pause') {\n          return [segment];\n        }\n        return segment.end - segment.start >= 0.3\n          ? [{ ...segment, ipa: '|' }]\n          : [];\n      })\n    : decoded.ipa;\n}\n\nfunction decodeText(input, settings, level, modelLanguage) {\n  const { languages, stages, nbest } = settings;\n  const language = languages.length === 1 ? languages[0] : undefined;\n  // A verified synthesis model provides its own language. Injected stages\n  // continue to receive the languages explicitly requested by the caller.\n  const candidates =\n    modelLanguage && !stages.identifyLanguage ? [modelLanguage] : languages;\n  const identification = language\n    ? null\n    : measure(settings.profile, 'Language identification', () =>\n        (stages.identifyLanguage ?? identifyLanguage)(input, {\n          languages: candidates,\n          kernels: settings.kernels,\n        })\n      );\n  return measure(settings.profile, 'IPA to text', () =>\n    (stages.ipaToText ?? ipaToText)(input, {\n      language,\n      spans: identification?.spans,\n      boundaries:\n        modelLanguage &&\n        Array.isArray(input) &&\n        input[0]?.modelWord !== undefined\n          ? 'given'\n          : undefined,\n      nbest,\n      kernels: settings.kernels,\n      profile: settings.profile,\n      beam: RECOGNITION_LEVELS[level].beam,\n    })\n  );\n}\n\nfunction recognizeProsody(decoded, samples, rate, settings, level) {\n  const input = timedPhones(decoded);\n  const pitch = decoded.tracks?.pitch;\n  if (!settings.modes || !pitch || !Array.isArray(input)) {\n    return decodeText(input, settings, level, decoded.modelLanguage);\n  }\n  const options = {\n    language:\n      settings.languages.length === 1 ? settings.languages[0] : undefined,\n    voice: settings.voice ?? decoded.voice,\n    pitch,\n    frames: decoded.frames?.speech ? decoded.frames : undefined,\n    whisperSpans: settings.whisper === false ? [] : decoded.whisperSpans,\n  };\n  const measured = measure(settings.profile, 'Prosody', () =>\n    measureProsody(samples, rate, input, options)\n  );\n  const primary = decodeText(\n    measured.sounds,\n    settings,\n    level,\n    decoded.modelLanguage\n  );\n  return markProsody(primary, measured, options);\n}\n\nfunction publicWord({\n  text,\n  ipa,\n  language,\n  start,\n  end,\n  confidence,\n  syllables,\n}) {\n  return {\n    text,\n    ipa,\n    language,\n    start,\n    end,\n    confidence,\n    syllables: syllables.map(({ text, ipa, start, end, stress }) => ({\n      text,\n      ipa,\n      start,\n      end,\n      stress,\n    })),\n  };\n}\n\nfunction alternativesFor(decoded, primary, settings, level) {\n  const candidates = [...(primary.alternatives ?? [])];\n  if (candidates.length < settings.nbest - 1) {\n    for (const reading of (decoded.nbest ?? []).slice(1)) {\n      const { text, ipa } = decodeText(\n        timedPhones(reading),\n        { ...settings, nbest: 1 },\n        level\n      );\n      candidates.push({ text, ipa, confidence: reading.confidence });\n    }\n  }\n  candidates.sort((a, b) => b.confidence - a.confidence);\n  const seen = new Set([primary.text]);\n  return candidates\n    .filter(({ text }) => {\n      if (seen.has(text)) {\n        return false;\n      }\n      seen.add(text);\n      return true;\n    })\n    .slice(0, settings.nbest - 1);\n}\n\nexport function recognizeDecoded(\n  decoded,\n  samples,\n  rate,\n  settings,\n  level,\n  final\n) {\n  if (!decoded.ipa) {\n    return emptyRecognition(settings.nbest, settings.segments);\n  }\n  if (settings.rescoring && (final === 'batch' || final === 'stream')) {\n    decoded = rescoreHypotheses(decoded, {\n      preserveTiming: final === 'stream',\n    });\n  }\n  const primary = recognizeProsody(decoded, samples, rate, settings, level);\n  const withModes =\n    settings.includeModeLabels && typeof recognizeModes === 'function'\n      ? measure(settings.profile, 'Modes', () =>\n          recognizeModes(\n            samples,\n            rate,\n            {\n              ...primary,\n              whisperSpans:\n                settings.whisper === false ? [] : decoded.whisperSpans,\n            },\n            {\n              voice: settings.voice ? { head: settings.voice } : undefined,\n              maxSeconds: samples.length / rate,\n              profile: settings.profile,\n              kernels: settings.kernels,\n              frames: decoded.frames?.speech ? decoded.frames : undefined,\n              reuseFormantCandidates: final === 'batch' || final === 'parallel',\n            }\n          )\n        )\n      : primary;\n  const { ipa, text, modes = [] } = withModes;\n  const words = withModes.words.map(publicWord);\n  const result = {\n    ipa,\n    text,\n    languages: languageShares(words),\n    words,\n    modes,\n    voice: null,\n  };\n  if (settings.nbest > 1) {\n    result.alternatives = alternativesFor(decoded, primary, settings, level);\n  }\n  if (settings.segments) {\n    result.segments = (decoded.segments ?? [])\n      .filter((segment) => segment.kind !== 'pause')\n      .map(({ ipa, start, end, confidence }) => ({\n        ipa,\n        start,\n        end,\n        confidence,\n      }));\n  }\n  return result;\n}\n\n/** Uniform audible energy lacks the 5 dB of contrast required by recognition. */\nexport function noisyFrames(energy, count, seconds) {\n  if (!energy || count === 0 || seconds <= 1) {\n    return false;\n  }\n  const sorted = energy.slice(0, count).sort((a, b) => a - b);\n  const size = Math.max(1, Math.floor(count / 5));\n  let loud = 0;\n  let quiet = 0;\n  for (let i = 0; i < size; i++) {\n    loud += sorted[count - 1 - i];\n    quiet += sorted[i];\n  }\n  // The analyzer uses -100 dB for exact silence.\n  return loud / size > -99 && (loud - quiet) / size < 5;\n}\n\nfunction checkAudio(samples, sampleRate) {\n  validateRate(sampleRate);\n  validateSamples(samples);\n  if (samples.length / sampleRate < 0.05) {\n    throw new RecognitionError(\n      'empty',\n      'Recognition needs at least 50 ms of audio'\n    );\n  }\n}\n\nfunction checkNoise(decoded, duration) {\n  if (noisyFrames(decoded.frames?.energy, decoded.frames?.count, duration)) {\n    throw new RecognitionError(\n      'too-noisy',\n      'Audio has less than 5 dB of energy contrast'\n    );\n  }\n}\n\nfunction serial(samples, sampleRate, settings, level) {\n  const { decoded, input, rate } = decodeRecognitionAudio(\n    samples,\n    sampleRate,\n    settings,\n    level\n  );\n  checkNoise(decoded, samples.length / sampleRate);\n  return recognizeDecoded(decoded, input, rate, settings, level, 'batch');\n}\n\nfunction pieces(samples, sampleRate, options, settings) {\n  // User-provided callbacks observe the entire original input.\n  if (Object.keys(settings.stages).length || settings.profile) {\n    return [];\n  }\n  const cuts = pauseCuts(samples, sampleRate);\n  const input =\n    cuts.length > 1 && !samples.subarray ? Array.from(samples) : samples;\n  return cuts.slice(1).map((end, i) => {\n    const start = cuts[i];\n    const seconds = start / sampleRate;\n    return {\n      samples: input.subarray\n        ? input.subarray(start, end)\n        : input.slice(start, end),\n      sampleRate,\n      seconds,\n      options: {\n        ...options,\n        whisper: decoderOptions(settings, 'low', seconds).whisper,\n      },\n    };\n  });\n}\n\nfunction merge(results, jobs, { nbest, segments }) {\n  const result = emptyRecognition(nbest, segments);\n  for (const [i, part] of results.entries()) {\n    aggregate(\n      result,\n      translated(part, jobs[i].seconds, result.words.length),\n      nbest - 1\n    );\n  }\n  result.languages = languageShares(result.words);\n  return result;\n}\n\nfunction runPiece(job, kernels) {\n  const settings = recognitionSettings({ ...job.options, kernels });\n  const level = settings.level === 'auto' ? 'medium' : settings.level;\n  return serial(job.samples, job.sampleRate, settings, level);\n}\n\nexport function recognize(samples, sampleRate, options = {}) {\n  if (options.threads === 'auto' || options.threads > 1) {\n    return recognizeAsync(samples, sampleRate, options);\n  }\n  checkAudio(samples, sampleRate);\n  const settings = recognitionSettings(options);\n  const level = settings.level === 'auto' ? 'medium' : settings.level;\n  const jobs = options.unsplit\n    ? []\n    : pieces(samples, sampleRate, options, settings);\n  return jobs.length\n    ? merge(\n        jobs.map((job) => runPiece(job, settings.kernels)),\n        jobs,\n        settings\n      )\n    : serial(samples, sampleRate, settings, level);\n}\n\nasync function parallelDecode(samples, sampleRate, settings, level, pool) {\n  const { input, rate, options } = decodeInput(\n    samples,\n    sampleRate,\n    settings,\n    level\n  );\n  let decoded = await audioToIpaParallel(\n    input,\n    rate,\n    { ...options, sourceRate: sampleRate, lattice: settings.rescoring },\n    pool\n  );\n  checkNoise(decoded, samples.length / sampleRate);\n  if (settings.rescoring && decoded.ipa) {\n    const preparation = planRescoring(decoded);\n    const scores = await pool.run('rescore', preparation.jobs, scoreJob);\n    decoded = applyRescoring(decoded, preparation, scores, RESCORING_WEIGHT);\n  }\n  return recognizeDecoded(decoded, input, rate, settings, level, 'parallel');\n}\n\nexport async function recognizeAsync(samples, sampleRate, options = {}) {\n  checkAudio(samples, sampleRate);\n  const kernels = options.kernels ?? (await createRecognitionEngine(options));\n  const settings = recognitionSettings({ ...options, kernels });\n  const level = settings.level === 'auto' ? Listening runs the same simulation\nin reverse: it finds the head, the voice and the movements that would have\nproduced the sound it hears, and reads the speech off those movements. Nothing\nis recorded and nothing is learned by a neural network. The project is in the\npublic domain and is a gift to everyone.\n\nThis document is the single statement of where the project is going. It is\nupdated by every pull request that changes the direction; the history is at the\nend. The step-by-step plan that implements it is [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).\n\n## Principles\n\nThese are rules, not preferences. A change that breaks one of them is not\nmerged.\n\n1. **Physics and mathematics only.** Sound comes from simulated air, folds,\n   walls and turbulence. Recognition comes from inverting that simulation.\n   No neural network is used anywhere: not in the library, not in the app,\n   not in the tests and not in the tools that build the data tables. No\n   recorded speech is played back or concatenated. The exact boundary is in\n   [What counts as a neural network](#what-counts-as-a-neural-network).\n2. **One model, two directions.** Speaking and listening share the same head,\n   the same articulation channels, the same IPA inventory and the same\n   prosody rules. A feature is finished when it works both ways: whatever the\n   simulator can say, it can recognise, and every mode of speech it detects, it\n   can produce.\n3. **Always through IPA.** Text is never mapped to sound directly, and sound\n   is never mapped to text directly. Speaking is text in a language → IPA →\n   audio. Listening is audio → IPA → the language, or the mix of languages,\n   → text. IPA with its tone, stress, length and voice-quality marks is the\n   interchange format between every stage and between the two directions.\n4. **The highest quality the device can afford, never silence.** The most\n   accurate simulation is the reference. Every device gets the most detailed\n   variant it can run in real time, measured on that device in the background,\n   and the quality steps down while speaking the moment the device falls\n   behind. The same holds for listening.\n5. **It works at the bottom too.** Synthesis, recognition and voice copying\n   all work at the lowest settings: narrow-band audio, the cheapest solver, one\n   CPU core. More cores, a GPU and higher settings make it better, never make\n   it possible.\n6. **Everything that changes a voice is a parameter.** Anatomy, the vocal\n   folds, breathing, articulation habits, accent and expression are numbers\n   with physical units, documented ranges and sources. A voice is a set of\n   those numbers, so it can be edited, saved, copied from a recording and\n   compared.\n7. **Measured against real speech.** Claims of quality are backed by numbers\n   computed on public recordings of real people with transcripts, by\n   algorithms that are themselves free of neural networks, and by listening\n   tests with people. A claim that was not measured is written as a goal.\n8. **Reproducible.** The same input, seed and settings give the same samples\n   on every runtime. Results of experiments are committed with the script\n   that produced them.\n9. **Public domain.** The code is released under the Unlicense. Data that is\n   committed to the repository is public domain or CC0. Dependencies have\n   permissive licences. Anything else is fetched at test time and never\n   redistributed.\n\n## What the system does when the vision is reached\n\n### Speaking\n\n- Reads text in every supported language, normalises it, converts it to IPA\n  and speaks it with a voice that people cannot tell from a recording of a\n  person in a blind listening test. That is the meaning of \"state of the art\"\n  here, and it is a goal, not a current claim.\n- Speaks in every common mode of speech: statements, all kinds of questions,\n  exclamations, commands, lists and asides; lexical tones and pitch accents;\n  word stress and rhythm; regional and foreign accents; soft, normal, loud and\n  shouted speech with gradual changes of loudness; whisper, breathy, creaky,\n  pressed and falsetto voice; emotions and attitudes; breaths, laughter, sighs\n  and hesitations.\n- Simulates the voice source as a physical system (vocal folds driven by lung\n  pressure, coupled to the air below and above them), the turbulence at\n  constrictions, the losses in the walls and the radiation from the mouth and\n  nose, in 1D for speed and in full 3D for accuracy.\n- Highlights every syllable in the text at the moment it is spoken.\n\n### Listening\n\n- Takes a recording or a live microphone and returns IPA with times, the\n  language or languages spoken, and the text, using the simulation in reverse.\n- Recognises the same modes of speech that it can produce and writes them\n  down with the same marks: tones, stress, sentence type, loudness, whisper\n  and other voice qualities, emotion.\n- Highlights every syllable as it is recognised.\n\n### Copying a voice\n\n- Works in several passes that feed each other. The first pass fits the\n  configuration of the voice: the size and shape of the head, the vocal folds,\n  the habits of articulation. The second pass inverts the simulation with\n  that configuration to recover the movements and the phonemes. As the person\n  keeps speaking both estimates are refined until they are stable. From then\n  on the system holds a voice it can speak with and a recogniser tuned to that\n  speaker, and it can follow what the person says.\n- Reproduces a real recording: the copy says the same words with the same\n  timing, melody and voice quality, close enough to be measured against the\n  original.\n\n### Running everywhere\n# Roadmap\n\nThis is the step-by-step plan that takes voice-simulator from what it is today\nto the [vision](VISION.md): a physical model of the human voice that speaks and\nlistens, without neural networks, in the public domain.\n\nEvery step is a GitHub issue. Birkholz and Drechsel\n(2021) added three anatomical details to the tract (piriform fossae, coupling\nthrough the velum, sound radiated by the neck); listeners did not rate the\nresult as more natural, and the authors conclude that the voice source matters\nmore. Blandin, Didone and Birkholz (2024) compared 1D and 3D acoustics for seven\nsounds and found no significant effect on rated naturalness. An earlier study\nof the same group (Blandin and others 2023) did find that listeners prefer 3D\nfor the vowels /o/ and /u/, so 3D stays the reference tier, but it is not\nwhere most of the gap to natural speech is.\n\nThe roadmap therefore improves, in this order: the vocal folds and their\ncoupling to the tract, turbulence and plosive bursts, articulator dynamics and\ndurations, then the losses in the 1D solver, and only then finer grids. **Create a Pull Request**\n\n## Code Standards\n\n### File Size Limits\n\n**Maximum 1500 lines per file** (enforced via ESLint `max-lines` rule and CI `check-file-line-limits` job).\n\nThis benefits both AI and human developers by ensuring files remain readable and maintainable.\n\n### Formatting and Linting\n\nAll code must pass:\n\n```bash\n# Check formatting\nbun run format:check\n\n# Check linting\nbun run lint\n\n# Run all checks\nbun run check\n```\n\nThe pre-commit hook runs automatically, but you can also manually format and fix:\n\n```bash\n# Auto-fix formatting\nbun run format\n\n# Auto-fix lint issues\nbun run lint:fix\n```\n\n### Testing Requirements\n\nTests should:\n\n- Cover critical paths\n- Work across all runtimes (Node.js, Bun, Deno)\n- Use the [test-anywhere](https://github.com/link-foundation/test-anywhere) framework\n\n```bash\n# Run tests\nbun test --timeout 30000\nnpm test\ndeno test -A --parallel\n```\n\nTests that need more than about 10 seconds or a download do not belong in\n`tests/*.test.js`; put them into `tests/heavy/` (see \"Heavy checks\" below).\n\n### Heavy checks\n\nSlow tests (full 3D renders, quality reports against recordings, recognition\nof datasets, round trips, voice copying) live in `tests/heavy/` and are named\n`<suite>-<topic>.test.js`, where the suite is `quality`, `recognition`,\n`roundtrip`, `copy`, workflow `Heavy checks`\n([.github/workflows/heavy.yml](../.github/workflows/heavy.yml)), which is only\nstarted by hand:\n\n- in the **Actions** tab: choose **Heavy checks**, then **Run workflow**, pick\n  the branch, the suite, optionally a `ref` (a branch or tag of this\n  repository, or a commit already on `main` or on the branch picked; empty\n  means the branch picked)\n  and a `limit` limit=5\n  # on another branch\n  gh workflow run heavy.yml --ref my-branch -f suite=performance\n  ```\n\nA run started on `main` writes to the cache scope of `main`,
