1,\n          nucleusFirst: first,\n          nucleusLast: last,\n          tonal,\n        };\n      }\n    });\n  }\n  ANALYSES.set(tokens, { key, entries });\n  return entries;\n}\n\n/**\n * Context of the token at `index` for the duration rules.\n * @param {object[]} tokens Tokens from parseIpa.\n * @param {number} index\n * @param {{language?: string}} [options]\n * @returns {object} `stress` (0, 1, 2), `emphasis`, `phraseFinal`\n *   (boundary class or null), `wordFinalSyllable`, `wordInitialSyllable`,\n *   `syllablesInWord`,\n *   `wordInitial`, `syllableOnset`, `syllableCoda`, `pretonic`,\n *   `previous` and `next` (class of the neighbouring sound inside the\n *   word, outside the nucleus for vowels), `tone` (0 to 5), `neutral`\n *   (tone 5 without stress mark: the neutral tone, issue 49),\n *   `afterAspirated`, `nucleusSize` and `nucleusMain` (whether the token\n *   carries the nucleus of a diphthong).\n */\nexport function durationFeatures(tokens, index, options = {}) {\n  const token = [REDACTED]];\n  const entry = analyse(tokens, options.language)[index];\n  if (!token || !entry) {\n    return null;\n  }\n  const { syllables, syllable, number } = entry;\n  const nucleus = isNucleus(token);\n  const { previousIndex, nextIndex } = neighbours(entry, index, nucleus);\n  const syllableOnset =\n    !nucleus && syllable.nuclei.length > 0 && index < syllable.nuclei[0];\n  const tone = toneNumber(syllable.tone, entry.tonal);\n  return {\n    stress: syllable.stress,\n    emphasis: Boolean(token.emphasis),\n    phraseFinal: entry.phraseFinal,\n    wordFinalSyllable: number === syllables.length - 1,\n    wordInitialSyllable: number === 0,\n    syllablesInWord: syllables.length,\n    wordInitial: entry.word[0] === index,\n    syllableOnset,\n    syllableCoda: !nucleus && !syllableOnset,\n    pretonic: entry.pretonic,\n    previous: neighbourClass(tokens[previousIndex]),\n    next: neighbourClass(tokens[nextIndex]),\n    tone,\n    neutral: tone === 5 && syllable.stress === 0,\n    afterAspirated:\n      nucleus &&\n      previousIndex >= 0 &&\n      isAspirated(tokens, previousIndex, options.language),\n    ...nucleusFeatures(tokens, entry, index, nucleus),\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Token indices of the sounds before and after a token inside its word\n * (-1 for none); a vowel looks past the other vowels of its nucleus.\n */\nfunction neighbours(entry, index, nucleus) {\n  const { word } = entry;\n  const first = nucleus ? entry.nucleusFirst : index;\n  const last = nucleus ? entry.nucleusLast : index;\n  const before = word.indexOf(first) - 1;\n  const after = word.indexOf(last) + 1;\n  return {\n    previousIndex: before >= 0 ? word[before] : -1,\n    nextIndex: after < word.length ? word[after] : -1,\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Size of the nucleus of a vowel, whether it is the main vowel (the tone\n * carrier in tonal text, else the first) and the symbols of the nucleus.\n */\nfunction nucleusFeatures(tokens, entry, index, nucleus) {\n  if (!nucleus) {\n    return { nucleusSize: 0, nucleusMain: false, nucleusSymbol: null };\n  }\n  const { nuclei } = entry.syllable;\n  const carrier = nuclei.find((i) => tokens[i].tone?.length);\n  const main = entry.tonal ? (carrier ?? nuclei.at(-1)) : nuclei[0];\n  return {\n    nucleusSize: nuclei.length,\n    nucleusMain: index === main,\n    nucleusSymbol: nuclei.map((i) => tokens[i].base).join(''),\n  };\n}\n\nconst vowel = (token) => isNucleus(token);\nconst consonant = (token) => !isNucleus(token);\nconst unstressed = (features) => features.stress === 0;\nconst toneRule = (number) => (token, features) =>\n  vowel(token) && features.tone === number;\nconst before =\n  (...classes) =>\n  (token, features) =>\n    vowel(token) && classes.includes(features.next);\n\n/**\n * The duration rules. `factor` multiplies the percentage (`scope`\n * `percent`, the default), the minimum (`minimum`), the whole duration\n * (`total`) or is milliseconds added after the formula (`add`). Rules of a\n * `group` exclude each other: the first one that applies and is switched\n * on wins. `postvocalic` rules weigh `0.7 + 0.3 * factor` outside a\n * phrase-final syllable; `stress` rules are divided by\n * `stressLengthening / 1.35`; `clauseFinal` scales with the head's\n * `finalLengthening` and with the boundary. A `null` factor switches a rule\n * off; the tables override factors per language.\n *\n * Values: Klatt (1979) as given in Allen, Hunnicutt and Klatt (1987,\n * chapter 9), the starting values of issue 39, and the factors of\n * experiments/issue-11-fit-durations.mjs (`DURATION_TABLES`).\n */\nexport const DURATION_RULES = Object.freeze(\n  [\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 2: the syllable before a pause, 1.4 (Klatt 1979). A\n      // neutral-tone syllable stays short at the end of a phrase too (Chao\n      // 1968, section 1.3.5).\n      name: 'clauseFinal',\n      factor: 1.4,\n      applies: (token, features) =>\n        Boolean(features.phraseFinal) &&\n        !features.syllableOnset &&\n        features.tone !== 5,\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 3: vowels outside a phrase-final syllable, 0.6.\n      name: 'nonPhraseFinal',\n      factor: 0.6,\n      applies: (token, features) => vowel(token) && !features.phraseFinal,\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 4: vowels outside a word-final syllable, 0.85.\n      name: 'nonWordFinal',\n      factor: 0.85,\n      applies: (token, features) => vowel(token) && !features.wordFinalSyllable,\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 5: vowels of a word of two or more syllables, 0.8,\n      // raised to log2(syllables) so that a third syllable shortens again\n      // (stick > sticky > stickiness, Lehiste 1972).\n      name: 'polysyllabic',\n      factor: 0.8,\n      exponent: (features) => Math.log2(features.syllablesInWord),\n      applies: (token, features) =>\n        vowel(token) && features.syllablesInWord > 1,\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 6: consonants that do not start the word, 0.85.\n      name: 'nonInitialConsonant',\n      factor: 0.85,\n      applies: (token, features) => consonant(token) && !features.wordInitial,\n    },\n    {\n      // Russian vowel reduction: the syllable just before the stress keeps\n      // more length than the others (Bondarko 1977). Off by default.\n      name: 'pretonic',\n      factor: null,\n      group: 'unstressed',\n      stress: true,\n      applies: (token, features) =>\n        vowel(token) && unstressed(features) && features.pretonic,\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 7: unstressed vowels in a word-medial syllable, 0.5.\n      name: 'unstressedMedial',\n      factor: 0.5,\n      group: 'unstressed',\n      stress: true,\n      applies: (token, features) =>\n        vowel(token) &&\n        unstressed(features) &&\n        !features.wordFinalSyllable &&\n        !features.wordInitialSyllable,\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 7: other unstressed vowels, 0.7.\n      name: 'unstressedOther',\n      factor: 0.7,\n      group: 'unstressed',\n      stress: true,\n      applies: (token, features) => vowel(token) && unstressed(features),\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 7: consonants before an unstressed vowel, 0.7.\n      name: 'unstressedOnset',\n      factor: 0.7,\n      stress: true,\n      applies: (token, features) =>\n        consonant(token) && features.syllableOnset && unstressed(features),\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 7: unstressed sounds are more compressible, minimum\n      // halved.\n      name: 'unstressedMinimum',\n      factor: 0.5,\n      scope: 'minimum',\n      applies: (token, features) => unstressed(features),\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 8: emphasized vowels, 1.4.\n      name: 'emphasis',\n      factor: 1.4,\n      applies: (token, features) => vowel(token) && features.emphasis,\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 9: vowel before a voiced fricative, 1.6.\n      name: 'beforeVoicedFricative',\n      factor: 1.6,\n      postvocalic: true,\n      applies: before('voicedFricative'),\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 9: vowel before a voiced plosive, 1.2.\n      name: 'beforeVoicedPlosive',\n      factor: 1.2,\n      postvocalic: true,\n      applies: before('voicedPlosive'),\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 9: vowel before a nasal, 0.85.\n      name: 'beforeNasal',\n      factor: 0.85,\n      postvocalic: true,\n      applies: before('nasal'),\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 9: vowel before a voiceless plosive or fricative, 0.7.\n      name: 'beforeVoiceless',\n      factor: 0.7,\n      postvocalic: true,\n      applies: before('voicelessPlosive', 'voicelessFricative'),\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 9: a word-final vowel without a consonant after it, 1.2\n      // (not for the neutral tone, see clauseFinal).\n      name: 'openFinal',\n      factor: 1.2,\n      postvocalic: true,\n      applies: (token, features) =>\n        vowel(token) &&\n        features.wordFinalSyllable &&\n        features.next === null &&\n        features.tone !== 5,\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 10: vowel followed by a vowel, 1.2.\n      name: 'vowelBeforeVowel',\n      factor: 1.2,\n      applies: before('vowel'),\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 10: vowel after a vowel, 0.7.\n      name: 'vowelAfterVowel',\n      factor: 0.7,\n      applies: (token, features) =>\n        vowel(token) && features.previous === 'vowel',\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 10: consonant between two consonants, 0.5.\n      name: 'clusterMiddle',\n      factor: 0.5,\n      group: 'cluster',\n      applies: (token, features) =>\n        consonant(token) &&\n        isConsonantClass(features.previous) &&\n        isConsonantClass(features.next),\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 10: consonant next to one consonant, 0.7.\n      name: 'clusterEdge',\n      factor: 0.7,\n      group: 'cluster',\n      applies: (token, features) =>\n        consonant(token) &&\n        (isConsonantClass(features.previous) ||\n          isConsonantClass(features.next)),\n    },\n    {\n      // Klatt rule 11: a stressed vowel after an aspirated plosive gets\n      // 25 ms after the formula.\n      name: 'aspiration',\n      factor: 25,\n      scope: 'add',\n      applies: (token, features) =>\n        vowel(token) && features.stress >= 1 && features.afterAspirated,\n    },\n    // Mandarin tones (off by default, see the zh table).\n    { name: 'tone1', factor: null, applies: toneRule(1) },\n    { name: 'tone2', factor: null, applies: toneRule(2) },\n    { name: 'tone3', factor: null, applies: toneRule(3) },\n    { name: 'tone4', factor: null, applies: toneRule(4) },\n    // The neutral tone shortens the whole vowel, minimum included: its\n    // syllables are about half as long as full-tone ones (Lin and Yan\n    // 1980). On by default for every tonal text (issue 49).\n    {\n      name: 'tone5',\n      factor: NEUTRAL_DURATION,\n      scope: 'total',\n      applies: (token, features) => vowel(token) && features.neutral,\n    },\n    {\n      // Long vowels written with `ː` that have no class of their own: 1.7,\n      // the factor of the plan before issue 39.\n      name: 'longVowel',\n      factor: 1.7,\n      scope: 'total',\n      applies: (token) => vowel(token) && token.long,\n    },\n    {\n      // Long (geminate) consonants: 1.8, the factor of the plan before\n      // issue 39.\n      name: 'longConsonant',\n      factor: 1.8,\n      scope: 'total',\n      applies: (token) => consonant(token) && token.long,\n    },\n  ].map((rule) => Object.freeze(rule))\n);\n\nfunction isConsonantClass(name) {\n  return Boolean(name) && name !== 'vowel';\n}\n\nconst entry = (inherent, minimum) => Object.freeze({ inherent, minimum });\n\n/**\n * Starting classes of issue 39 (after Klatt 1979; Allen, Hunnicutt and\n * Klatt 1987): inherent and minimum durations in milliseconds.\n */\nconst START_CLASSES = Object.freeze({\n  open: entry(230, 80), // Klatt 1979 [æ ɑ], issue 39\n  mid: entry(190, 70), // issue 39\n  close: entry(150, 50), // issue 39\n  reduced: entry(130, 45), // lax and reduced vowels, issue 39\n  diphthong: entry(250, 100), // issue 39\n  voicelessFricative: entry(115, 60), // issue 39\n  voicedFricative: entry(70, 40), // issue 39\n  voicelessPlosive: entry(80, 50), // closure, issue 39\n  voicedPlosive: entry(75, 50), // issue 39\n  nasal: entry(70, 50), // issue 39\n  liquid: entry(80, 35), // issue 39\n  glide: entry(70, 40), // issue 39\n  h: entry(80, 20), // issue 39\n  tap: entry(28, 20), // issue 39\n  trill: entry(85, 50), // issue 39\n});\n\n/** Language table from overrides of a base table. */\nfunction table(base, overrides = {}) {\n  return Object.freeze({\n    classes: Object.freeze({ ...base.classes, ...overrides.classes }),\n    symbols: Object.freeze({ ...base.symbols, ...overrides.symbols }),\n    rules: Object.freeze({ ...base.rules, ...overrides.rules }),\n    // Share of the main vowel of a diphthong: weight 1.5 against 1 for\n    // each other vowel, i.e. 0.6 and 0.4 (the 0.6 offglide factor of the\n    // plan before issue 39).\n    diphthongMain: overrides.diphthongMain ?? base.diphthongMain,\n    // Affricates: closure from the plosive entry, frication from the\n    // fricative entry, each x0.7 (issue 39).\n    affricate: Object.freeze({ ...base.affricate, ...overrides.affricate }),\n  });\n}\n\n// The starting values of issue 39, the base of every language.\nconst START = table({\n  classes: START_CLASSES,\n  symbols: {},\n  rules: {\n    // Klatt's rule 3 shortens every vowel outside a syntactic phrase end to\n    // 0.6, but the text analysis knows only punctuation, so the word ends\n    // inside a clause that Klatt would call phrase-final get it too. With\n    // 0.6 the last vowel before a full stop came out 2.0 times its length\n    // at the end of a word inside the clause, against the 1.4 of the\n    // head's `finalLengthening` and the 1.2 to 1.6 of issue 39; 0.9 gives\n    // 1.55 (experiments/issue-39-phrase-final.mjs). The fit keeps it.\n    nonPhraseFinal: 0.9,\n  },\n  diphthongMain: 1.5,\n  affricate: { closure: 0.7, frication: 0.7 },\n});\n\nconst ENGLISH = table(START, {\n  classes: {\n    reduced: entry(107, 45), // fitted, issue-11-fit-durations (start 130)\n    diphthong: entry(200, 100), // fitted, issue-11-fit-durations (start 250)\n    voicelessPlosive: entry(102, 50), // fitted, issue-11-fit-durations (start 80)\n  },\n});\n\n/**\n * Inherent and minimum durations (ms) per class of sound and per IPA\n * symbol, and the rule factors (null switches a rule off) of each\n * language. `default` is English.\n */\nexport const DURATION_TABLES = Object.freeze({\n  en: ENGLISH,\n  ru: table(START, {\n    classes: {\n      mid: entry(159, 70), // fitted, issue-11-fit-durations (start 190)\n      // Long because the 0.45 and 0.7 of the reduction apply to almost\n      // every one of them; fitted, issue-11-fit-durations (start 130).\n      reduced: entry(187, 45),\n      voicelessPlosive: entry(89, 50), // fitted, issue-11-fit-durations (start 80)\n    },\n    rules: {\n      // Russian vowel length does not depend on the voicing of the next\n      // consonant at the end of a word (final devoicing), issue 39.\n      beforeVoicedFricative: null,\n      beforeVoicedPlosive: null,\n      // Two degrees of reduction: 0.7 just before the stress, 0.45 in the\n      // other unstressed syllables (issue 39; Bondarko 1977).\n      pretonic: 0.7,\n      unstressedMedial: 0.45,\n      unstressedOther: 0.45,\n      // Long consonants ([ɕː ʂː]): x1.5, issue 39.\n      longConsonant: 1.5,\n    },\n  }),\n  hi: table(START, {\n    classes: {\n      // Long vowels (written with ː): 210/90 ms, issue 39. The fit asks\n      // for 160 to 170 ms (issue-11-fit-durations), which makes [aː] only\n      // 1.4 times [ə] against the 1.6 to 2.4 of the test of issue 39; the\n      // alignment copies much of the length of the plan it rendered, so\n      // the contrast keeps the starting value.\n      long: entry(210, 90),\n    },\n    symbols: {\n      // Short [ə ɪ ʊ]: 110/50 ms, issue 39; the inherent duration of [ə]\n      // fitted, issue-11-fit-durations.\n      ə: entry(114, 50),\n      ɪ: entry(110, 50),\n      ʊ: entry(110, 50),\n    },\n    rules: {\n      // Hindi stress is weak: unstressed sounds lose little, issue 39.\n      unstressedMedial: 0.9,\n      unstressedOther: 0.8, // fitted, issue-11-fit-durations (start 0.9)\n      unstressedOnset: 0.9,\n      // Double consonants: x1.8, issue 39.\n      longConsonant: 1.8,\n      // Long vowels have their own class.\n      longVowel: null,\n    },\n  }),\n  zh: table(START, {\n    classes: {\n      close: entry(132, 50), // fitted, issue-11-fit-durations (start 150)\n      diphthong: entry(229, 100), // fitted, issue-11-fit-durations (start 250)\n      nasal: entry(96, 50), // fitted, issue-11-fit-durations (start 70)\n    },\n    rules: {\n      // No lexical stress in the transcriptions: no stress rules and no\n      // polysyllabic shortening (issue 39).\n      unstressedMedial: null,\n      unstressedOther: null,\n      unstressedOnset: null,\n      unstressedMinimum: null,\n      polysyllabic: null,\n      // Tone factors, issue 39 (after Xu 1997 and Lin and Yan 1980).\n      tone1: 1,\n      tone2: 1.05,\n      tone3: 1.15,\n      tone4: 0.9,\n      tone5: 0.55,\n      // Weaker final lengthening, issue 39.\n      clauseFinal: 1.2,\n    },\n  }),\n  default: ENGLISH,\n});\n\n/**\n * The table of a language code (`en-US` finds `en`); `default` otherwise.\n * @param {string} [language]\n */\nexport function durationTable(language) {\n  const code = String(language ?? '')\n    .slice(0, 2)\n    .toLowerCase();\n  return DURATION_TABLES[code] ?? DURATION_TABLES.default;\n}\n\n/** Class of a token in `table`. */\nexport function durationClass(token, features, table) {\n  if (!isNucleus(token)) {\n    return token.syllabic ? 'reduced' : consonantClass(token);\n  }\n  if (token.kind !== 'vowel') {\n    return 'reduced';\n  }\n  if (features?.nucleusSize > 1) {\n    return 'diphthong';\n  }\n  if (token.long && table.classes.long) {\n    return 'long';\n  }\n  return vowelClass(token);\n}\n\nfunction scaleEntry(value, share) {\n  return { inherent: value.inherent * share, minimum: value.minimum * share };\n}\n\n/**\n * Inherent and minimum duration (ms) of each part of a token: [REDACTED] part,\n * or closure and frication of an affricate. A vowel of a diphthong gets\n * its share of the nucleus.\n * @param {object} token\n * @param {object} features From `durationFeatures()`.\n * @param {object} [table]\n * @returns {{inherent: number, minimum: number}[]}\n */\nexport function phonemeDurations(token, features, table = ENGLISH) {\n  const lookup = (name, symbol) =>\n    (symbol && table.symbols[symbol]) ?? table.classes[name];\n  if (token.affricate) {\n    const voiced = token.voiced ?? token.phoneme.voiced;\n    const closure = lookup(\n      voiced ? 'voicedPlosive' : 'voicelessPlosive',\n      token.affricate.stop\n    );\n    const frication = lookup(\n      voiced ? 'voicedFricative' : 'voicelessFricative',\n      token.phoneme.symbol\n    );\n    return [\n      scaleEntry(closure, table.affricate.closure),\n      scaleEntry(frication, table.affricate.frication),\n    ];\n  }\n  const name = durationClass(token, features, table);\n  if (name === 'diphthong') {\n    const size = features.nucleusSize;\n    const main = table.diphthongMain;\n    const share = (features.nucleusMain ? main : 1) / (main + size - 1);\n    const value = lookup(name, features.nucleusSymbol);\n    return [scaleEntry(value, share)];\n  }\n  const long = token.long ? `${token.base}ː` : null;\n  const value =\n    (long && table.symbols[long]) ??\n    table.symbols[token.symbol] ??\n    table.symbols[token.base] ??\n    table.classes[name];\n  return [scaleEntry(value, 1)];\n}\n\n/**\n * The plain formula of Klatt (1979) in seconds.\n * @param {{inherent: number, minimum: number, percent: number, speechRate?: number, rateMinimum?: number, rateStretch?: number}} values\n *   Durations in milliseconds, `percent` from 0 up; `rateMinimum` and\n *   `rateStretch` (the head's, RATE_MINIMUM and RATE_STRETCH by default)\n *   are the exponents of the rate on the minimum and the stretch.\n */\nexport function durationFormula({\n  inherent,\n  minimum,\n  percent,\n  speechRate,\n  rateMinimum = RATE_MINIMUM,\n  rateStretch = RATE_STRETCH,\n}) {\n  const rate = speechRate ?? 1;\n  const ms =\n    minimum / rate ** rateMinimum +\n    ((inherent - minimum) * percent) / 100 / rate ** rateStretch;\n  return Math.max(ms, minimum / rate ** rateMinimum) / 1000;\n}\n\n/** Head key of the strength of each rule: durationClauseFinal. */\nconst RULE_KEYS = new Map(\n  DURATION_RULES.map((rule) => [\n    rule.name,\n    `duration${rule.name[0].toUpperCase()}${rule.name.slice(1)}`,\n  ])\n);\n\n/** Factor of a rule in `table`, null when it is switched off. */\nexport function ruleFactor(rule, table) {\n  const factor = table?.rules?.[rule.name];\n  return factor === undefined ? rule.factor : factor;\n}\n\n/**\n * Factor of one applying rule after the adjustments for the context and\n * the head.\n */\nfunction effectiveFactor(rule, factor, features, options) {\n  let value = factor;\n  if (rule.exponent) {\n    value **= rule.exponent(features);\n  }\n  if (rule.postvocalic && !features.phraseFinal) {\n    value = 0.7 + 0.3 * value;\n  }\n  if (rule.stress) {\n    value /= (options.stressLengthening ?? 1.35) / 1.35;\n  }\n  if (rule.name === 'clauseFinal') {\n    const head =\n      ((options.finalLengthening ?? BOUNDARIES.period.lengthen) - 1) /\n      (BOUNDARIES.period.lengthen - 1);\n    const boundary =\n      (finalLengthening(features.phraseFinal) - 1) /\n      (BOUNDARIES.period.lengthen - 1);\n    value = 1 + (value - 1) * head * boundary;\n  }\n  // The head's strength of the rule: a power of a factor, a multiple of\n  // an added duration.\n  const strength = options[RULE_KEYS.get(rule.name)] ?? 1;\n  if (strength !== 1) {\n    value = rule.scope === 'add' ? value * strength : value ** strength;\n  }\n  return value;\n}\n\n/**\n * Rules that apply to a token with their effective factors.\n * @param {object} token\n * @param {object} features\n * @param {object} [table]\n * @param {{stressLengthening?: number, finalLengthening?: number}} [options]\n *   Head values: also the strengths `duration<Rule>` of the rules.\n * @returns {{rule: object, factor: number}[]}\n */\nexport function applyingRules(token, features, table = ENGLISH, options = {}) {\n  const groups = new Set();\n  const result = [];\n  for (const rule of DURATION_RULES) {\n    const factor = ruleFactor(rule, table);\n    if (factor === null || (rule.group && groups.has(rule.group))) {\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (!rule.applies(token, features)) {\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (rule.group) {\n      groups.add(rule.group);\n    }\n    result.push({\n      rule,\n      factor: effectiveFactor(rule, factor, features, options),\n    });\n  }\n  return result;\n}\n\n/**\n * Duration in seconds of each part of a token (one part, or closure and\n * frication of an affricate).\n * @param {object} token\n * @param {object} features From `durationFeatures()`.\n * @param {object} [table] An entry of `DURATION_TABLES`.\n * @param {{speechRate?: number, stressLengthening?: number, finalLengthening?: number, rateMinimum?: number, rateStretch?: number}} [options]\n *   Head values, with the strengths `duration<Rule>` of the rules.\n * @returns {number[]}\n */\nexport function segmentParts(token, features, table = ENGLISH, options = {}) {\n  const rate = options.speechRate ?? 1;\n  const rateMinimum = options.rateMinimum ?? Steps:\n   1. `spoken = synthesize(text, { lang, tier, preset, seed })`.\n   2. `heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level })` with `level = levelForTier(tier)`. Do not pass the language: it must be found.\n   3. Return `{ spoken, heard, seconds }` plus these numbers, computed with `errorRate` and `editDistance` of #18:\n      - `per`: `errorRate(spoken.ipa, heard.ipa, 'phone')`;\n      - `wer` (not for `zh`) and `cer`: `errorRate(text, heard.text, unit)` with `'word'` and `'char'`;\n      - `soundWer`: the same as `wer`, but each word of both texts is first replaced by its IPA from `textToIpa(...).words[].ipa`, so that a word which sounds the same (`sea` and `see`, 他 and 她) is not an error. For `zh` the tokens are the characters;\n      - `toneErrors` (only `zh`): edit distance between the two lists of tones, one entry per syllable (the tone letters in the syllable's IPA, the empty string for the neutral tone);\n      - `stressHits` (only `en`, `ru`): among the reference words with two or more syllables whose recognised word has the same number of syllables, how many have `stress: 1` on the same syllable;\n      - `timeErrors`: pair the reference and recognised syllables through the edit-distance path over syllable IPA; for each pair with equal IPA collect `|start difference|` and `|end difference|` in ms;\n      - `languageRight`: `heard.languages[0].language === lang` after sorting by `share`, largest first;\n      - `sentenceMark`: the last of `. ? !` in `heard.text`, with `।`, `。`, `？`, `！` mapped to their ASCII form, or `null`.\n3. total / errors.length : null };\n}\n\nexport function roundTrip(text, options) {\n  const {\n    lang,\n    tier,\n    preset,\n    seed,\n    markup,\n    referenceText = text,\n    recognize = recognizeAudio,\n  } = options;\n  const spoken = synthesize(text, {\n    lang,\n    tier,\n    head: 'random',\n    preset,\n    seed,\n    markup,\n  });\n  const level = levelForTier(tier);\n  const start = performance.now();\n  const heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level });\n  const seconds = (performance.now() - start) / 1000;\n  const referenceWords = spoken.timeline.words;\n  const syllables = (words) => words.flatMap((word) => word.syllables);\n  const reference = syllables(referenceWords);\n  const hypothesis = syllables(heard.words);\n  const languages = [...heard.languages].sort((a, b) => b.share - a.share);\n\n  return {\n    spoken,\n    heard,\n    seconds,\n    per: errorRate(spoken.ipa, heard.ipa, 'phone'),\n    ...(lang !== 'zh' && { wer: errorRate(referenceText, heard.text, 'word') }),\n    cer: errorRate(referenceText, heard.text, 'char'),\n    soundWer: errorRate(\n      soundTokens(referenceText, lang),\n      soundTokens(heard.text, lang)\n    ),\n    ...(lang === 'zh' && {\n      toneErrors: errorRate(reference.map(tone), hypothesis.map(tone)),\n    }),\n    ...(['en', 'ru'].includes(lang) && {\n      stressHits: compareStress(referenceWords, heard.words),\n    }),\n    timeErrors: compareTimes(reference, hypothesis),\n    languageRight: languages[0]?.language === lang,\n    sentenceMark: sentenceMark(heard.text),\n  };\n}\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

[]);\n+  if (!metrics.length) {\n+    return null;\n+  }\n+  const distance = sum(metrics, (item) => item.distance);\n+  const referenceLength = sum(metrics, (item) => item.referenceLength);\n+  return {\n+    distance,\n+    referenceLength,\n+    rate: distance / Math.max(1, referenceLength),\n+  };\n+}\n+\n+export function summarizeRoundTrips(items) {\n+  const stressHits = sum(items, (item) => item.stressHits?.hits ?? 0);\n+  const stressCount = sum(items, (item) => item.stressHits?.count ?? 0);\n+  const boundaryCount = sum(items, (item) => item.timeErrors.errors.length);\n+  const modeSpans = items.flatMap((item) => item.modeSpans ?? []);\n+  return {\n+    per: aggregateEdits(items, 'per'),\n+    wer: aggregateEdits(items, 'wer'),\n+    cer: aggregateEdits(items, 'cer'),\n+    soundWer: aggregateEdits(items, 'soundWer'),\n+    toneErrors: aggregateEdits(items, 'toneErrors'),\n+    stress: ratio(stressHits, stressCount),\n+    stressCount,\n+    stressExpected: sum(items, (item) => item.stressExpected),\n+    meanTime: ratio(\n+      sum(items, (item) => item.timeErrors.total),\n+      boundaryCount\n+    ),\n+    boundaryCount,\n+    language: ratio(\n+      sum(items, (item) => Number(item.languageRight)),\n+      items.length\n+    ),\n+    sentenceMark: ratio(\n+      sum(items, (item) => Number(item.markRight)),\n+      items.length\n+    ),\n+    modes: ratio(\n+      sum(modeSpans, (span) => Number(span.matched)),\n+      modeSpans.length\n+    ),\n+    modeCount: modeSpans.length,\n+    rtf: ratio(\n+      sum(items, (item) => item.seconds),\n+      sum(items, (item) => item.duration)\n+    ),\n+  };\n+}\n+\n+const percent = (rate) =>\n+  Number.isFinite(rate) ? `${(100 * rate).toFixed(1)}%` : '–';\n+\n+function table(columns, rows) {\n+  return [columns, columns.map(() => '---'), ...rows]\n+    .map((row) => `| ${row.join(' | ')} |`)\n+    .join('\\n');\n+}\n+\n+function reportRow({\n+  lang,\n+  tier,\n+  presets,\n+  items,\n+  stats,\n+  failures,\n+  diagnostic,\n+}) {\n+  return [\n+    lang,\n+    tier,\n+    presets.join(', '),\n+    items.length,\n+    percent(stats.per?.rate),\n+    percent(stats.wer?.rate),\n+    percent(stats.cer?.rate),\n+    percent(stats.soundWer?.rate),\n+    percent(stats.toneErrors?.rate),\n+    percent(stats.stress),\n+    stats.meanTime?.toFixed(1) ?? Do not pass the language: it must be found.\n   3. Return `{ spoken, heard, seconds }` plus these numbers, computed with `errorRate` and `editDistance` of #18:\n      - `per`: `errorRate(spoken.ipa, heard.ipa, 'phone')`;\n      - `wer` (not for `zh`) and `cer`: `errorRate(text, heard.text, unit)` with `'word'` and `'char'`;\n      - `soundWer`: the same as `wer`, but each word of both texts is first replaced by its IPA from `textToIpa(...).words[].ipa`, so that a word which sounds the same (`sea` and `see`, 他 and 她) is not an error. For `zh` the tokens are the characters;\n      - `toneErrors` (only `zh`): edit distance between the two lists of tones, one entry per syllable (the tone letters in the syllable's IPA, the empty string for the neutral tone);\n      - `stressHits` (only `en`, `ru`): among the reference words with two or more syllables whose recognised word has the same number of syllables, how many have `stress: 1` on the same syllable;\n      - `timeErrors`: pair the reference and recognised syllables through the edit-distance path over syllable IPA; for each pair with equal IPA collect `|start difference|` and `|end difference|` in ms;\n      - `languageRight`: `heard.languages[0].language === lang` after sorting by `share`, largest first;\n      - `sentenceMark`: the last of `. ? !` in `heard.text`, with `।`, `。`, `？`, `！` mapped to their ASCII form, or `null`.\n3. Create `tests/heavy/roundtrip-sentences.test.js`. Seed 1 everywhere. Runs:\n   - set `main`: all 80 sentences, tiers `telephone`, `narrowband`, `wideband`, `minimal`, presets `male` and `female` (640 runs);\n   - set `voices`: sentences 1 to 5 of each language, presets `any` and `child`, tiers `telephone` and `wideband` (80 runs);\n   - set `tiers`: sentences 2 and 20 of each language, preset `male`, tiers `low`, `medium`, `high`, `ultra`, `studio` (40 runs). `reference` is left out because of its run time; say so in the report.\n   - `heavyLimit(80)` limits the number of sentences per set.\n   - Sum the edit distances and the reference lengths per language, tier and set before dividing; do not average the rates of single sentences.\n4. Gates (one `it` per row, so that a failure names the row). They hold for every language of set `main`:\n\n   | Tier | PER | soundWer | Tone errors | Syllable time, mean | Language right |\n   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n   | `wideband`, `minimal` | ≤ 5 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 30 ms | ≥ 95 % |\n   | `narrowband` | ≤ 8 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 12 % | ≤ 35 ms | ≥ 92 % |\n   | `telephone` | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 20 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 40 ms | ≥ 90 % |\n\n   Set `voices`: the gates of row `telephone` for every preset. Set `tiers`: PER ≤ 10 % per tier. Stress hits ≥ 90 % (`en`, `ru`) from `narrowband` up. `wer`, `cer`, `sentenceMark` and the real-time factor of `recognize` (`seconds` divided by audio seconds) are reported without a gate; the sentence mark gets its gate in #70.\n\n5. If the first full run misses a gate, do not loosen it. Read the report (it lists the 20 worst sentences with reference and recognised IPA), fix the stage that loses most, and run again. The gates are the result this issue must deliver.\n6. Mode check, only when `parseMarkup` of #50 is exported (else the test is skipped with the reason in its name): speak sentence 1 of each language once whispered and once loud with the markup of #50; report the share of mode spans that come back in `heard.modes` with the same notation and at least 50 % overlap in time. This issue sets no gate of its own for modes: the numbers belong to #70 (sentence mark), #71 (mode labels) and #72 (set `whisper`). Each of them adds its gate to this test when this test exists. For each of the three that is merged already while its gate is missing here, add the gate in this issue with the numbers of that issue's acceptance criteria.\n7. Write the report with `writeReport('roundtrip', markdown, data)`: one table per set (rows: language × tier; columns: the numbers above), then the 20 worst sentences. Copy the report of the full run to `docs/reports/roundtrip.md` and commit it with the run link, the commit hash and the date at the top.\n8. Smoke test `tests/roundtrip-smoke.test.js` (part of `npm test`): sentence 18 of `en`, 2 of `ru` and 2 of `zh`; tier `telephone`, preset `male`, seed 1. Expect `per.rate \u003c= 0.1`, `soundWer.rate === 0` and `languageRight`.\n9. Add the suite and the report to `tests/heavy/README.md` and to `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` (section \"Heavy checks\").\n\n## Tests\n\n- `tests/roundtrip-smoke.test.js`: the three `it` blocks of step 8, named `round trip en`, `round trip ru`, `round trip zh`.\n- `tests/roundtrip-helper.test.js` (fast, stub recogniser passed as `options.recognize`): `counts a homophone as right` (`sea` heard as `see` gives `wer.distance === 1` and `soundWer.distance === 0`); `counts tones` (one wrong tone letter gives `toneErrors.distance === 1`); `measures syllable times` (a result shifted by 20 ms gives a mean of 20 ms).\n- `has 20 sentences per language`: `sentences.json` has four keys with 20 non-empty strings each and no digit.\n- `tests/heavy/roundtrip-sentences.test.js` as described above.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `node --test tests/roundtrip-smoke.test.js` passes in less than 30 s on one core.\n- [ ] `npm run test:heavy -- --suite roundtrip --limit 2` passes locally and writes `reports/heavy/roundtrip.md`.\n- [ ] A run of `Heavy checks` with `suite=roundtrip` on the pull request branch is green: every gate of step 4 holds. Runs:\n   - set `main`: all 80 sentences, tiers `telephone`, `narrowband`, `wideband`, `minimal`, presets `male` and `female` (640 runs);\n   - set `voices`: sentences 1 to 5 of each language, presets `any` and `child`, tiers `telephone` and `wideband` (80 runs);\n   - set `tiers`: sentences 2 and 20 of each language, preset `male`, tiers `low`, `medium`, `high`, `ultra`, `studio` (40 runs). `reference` is left out because of its run time; say so in the report.\n   - `heavyLimit(80)` limits the number of sentences per set.\n   - Sum the edit distances and the reference lengths per language, tier and set before dividing; do not average the rates of single sentences.\n4. Gates (one `it` per row, so that a failure names the row). They hold for every language of set `main`:\n\n   | Tier | PER | soundWer | Tone errors | Syllable time, mean | Language right |\n   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n   | `wideband`, `minimal` | ≤ 5 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 30 ms | ≥ 95 % |\n   | `narrowband` | ≤ 8 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 12 % | ≤ 35 ms | ≥ 92 % |\n   | `telephone` | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 20 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 40 ms | ≥ 90 % |\n\n   Set `voices`: the gates of row `telephone` for every preset. Set `tiers`: PER ≤ 10 % per tier. Stress hits ≥ 90 % (`en`, `ru`) from `narrowband` up. `wer`, `cer`, `sentenceMark` and the real-time factor of `recognize` (`seconds` divided by audio seconds) are reported without a gate; the sentence mark gets its gate in #70.\n\n5. This is the regression baseline for every later change of the recogniser, and the proof that both directions work at 8000 Hz.\n\n## Current state\n\n- `synthesize(text, options)` returns an object with the keys `lang`, `accent`, `ipa`, `words`, `head`, `plan`, `timeline`, `sampleRate`, `samples` and `duration`. `timeline.words[].syllables[]` holds `ipa`, `stress`, `start`, `end` (seconds) and `text`.\n- Measured on this branch: the three smoke sentences below take 0.11 to 0.27 s each to synthesise at tier `minimal` (22050 Hz, 1.9 to 2.3 s of audio).\n- The 80 sentences were checked with the current text-to-IPA code. \"example:desktop:package\": \"npm --prefix examples/universal-app run desktop:package\",\n  \"example:desktop:make\": \"npm --prefix examples/universal-app run desktop:make\",\n  \"example:mobile:sync\": \"npm --prefix examples/universal-app run mobile:sync\",\n  \"prepare\": \"node scripts/install-git-hooks.mjs\",\n  \"changeset\": \"changeset\",\n  \"changeset:version\": \"node scripts/changeset-version.mjs\",\n  \"changeset:publish\": \"changeset publish\",\n  \"changeset:status\": \"changeset status --since=origin/main\",\n  \"build:wasm\": \"node scripts/build-wasm.mjs && node scripts/build-recognition-models.mjs\"\n}\n# Vision\n\nvoice-simulator is a physical model of the human voice that works in both\ndirections:\n\n```\ntext in a language  ->  IPA  ->  articulation  ->  sound      (speaking)\ntext in a language  <-  IPA  <-  articulation  <-  sound      (listening)\n```\n\nSpeaking simulates the air in a human head. Listening runs the same simulation\nin reverse: it finds the head, the voice and the movements that would have\nproduced the sound it hears, and reads the speech off those movements. Nothing\nis recorded and nothing is learned by a neural network. The project is in the\npublic domain and is a gift to everyone.\n\nThis document is the single statement of where the project is going. It is\nupdated by every pull request that changes the direction; the history is at the\nend. The step-by-step plan that implements it is [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).\n\n## Principles\n\nThese are rules, not preferences. A change that breaks one of them is not\nmerged.\n\n1. **Physics and mathematics only.** Sound comes from simulated air, folds,\n   walls and turbulence. Recognition comes from inverting that simulation.\n   No neural network is used anywhere: not in the library, not in the app,\n   not in the tests and not in the tools that build the data tables. No\n   recorded speech is played back or concatenated. The exact boundary is in\n   [What counts as a neural network](#what-counts-as-a-neural-network).\n2. **One model, two directions.** Speaking and listening share the same head,\n   the same articulation channels, the same IPA inventory and the same\n   prosody rules. A feature is finished when it works both ways: whatever the\n   simulator can say, it can recognise, and every mode of speech it detects, it\n   can produce.\n3. **Always through IPA.** Text is never mapped to sound directly, and sound\n   is never mapped to text directly. Speaking is text in a language → IPA →\n   audio. Listening is audio → IPA → the language, or the mix of languages,\n   → text. IPA with its tone, stress, length and voice-quality marks is the\n   interchange format between every stage and between the two directions.\n4. **The highest quality the device can afford, never silence.** The most\n   accurate simulation is the reference. Every device gets the most detailed\n   variant it can run in real time, measured on that device in the background,\n   and the quality steps down while speaking the moment the device falls\n   behind. The same holds for listening.\n5. **It works at the bottom too.** Synthesis, recognition and voice copying\n   all work at the lowest settings: narrow-band audio, the cheapest solver, one\n   CPU core. More cores, a GPU and higher settings make it better, never make\n   it possible.\n6. **Everything that changes a voice is a parameter.** Anatomy, the vocal\n   folds, breathing, articulation habits, accent and expression are numbers\n   with physical units, documented ranges and sources. A voice is a set of\n   those numbers, so it can be edited, saved, copied from a recording and\n   compared.\n7. **Measured against real speech.** Claims of quality are backed by numbers\n   computed on public recordings of real people with transcripts, by\n   algorithms that are themselves free of neural networks, and by listening\n   tests with people. A claim that was not measured is written as a goal.\n8. **Reproducible.** The same input, seed and settings give the same samples\n   on every runtime. Results of experiments are committed with the script\n   that produced them.\n9. **Public domain.** The code is released under the Unlicense. Data that is\n   committed to the repository is public domain or CC0. Dependencies have\n   permissive licences. Anything else is fetched at test time and never\n   redistributed.\n\n## What the system does when the vision is reached\n\n### Speaking\n\n- Reads text in every supported language, normalises it, converts it to IPA\n  and speaks it with a voice that people cannot tell from a recording of a\n  person in a blind listening test. That is the meaning of \"state of the art\"\n  here, and it is a goal, not a current claim.\n- Speaks in every common mode of speech: statements, all kinds of questions,\n  exclamations, commands, lists and asides; lexical tones and pitch accents;\n  word stress and rhythm; regional and foreign accents; soft, normal, loud and\n  shouted speech with gradual changes of loudness; whisper, breathy, creaky,\n  pressed and falsetto voice; emotions and attitudes; breaths, laughter, sighs\n  and hesitations.\n- Simulates the voice source as a physical system (vocal folds driven by lung\n  pressure, coupled to the air below and above them), the turbulence at\n  constrictions, the losses in the walls and the radiation from the mouth and\n  nose, in 1D for speed and in full 3D for accuracy.\n- Highlights every syllable in the text at the moment it is spoken.\n\n### Listening\n\n- Takes a recording or a live microphone and returns IPA with times, the\n  language or languages spoken, and the text, using the simulation in reverse.\n- Recognises the same modes of speech that it can produce and writes them\n  down with the same marks: tones, stress, sentence type, loudness, whisper\n  and other voice qualities, emotion.\n- Highlights every syllable as it is recognised.\n\n### Copying a voice\n\n- Works in several passes that feed each other. The first pass fits the\n  configuration of the voice: the size and shape of the head, the vocal folds,\n  the habits of articulation. The second pass inverts the simulation with\n  that configuration to recover the movements and the phonemes. As the person\n  keeps speaking both estimates are refined until they are stable. From then\n  on the system holds a voice it can speak with and a recogniser tuned to that\n  speaker, and it can follow what the person says.\n- Reproduces a real recording: the copy says the same words with the same\n  timing, melody and voice quality, close enough to be measured against the\n  original.\n\n### Running everywhere\n\n- The simulation core is written in Rust. In browsers it runs as WebAssembly\n  in a background worker and is the default engine; the same core runs natively\n  in the command line tool and the server. The JavaScript implementation stays\n  as the readable reference and as the fallback.\n- A short benchmark runs in the background when the page loads, without sound\n  and without blocking the interface, and decides the precision for this\n  device. While speaking, the quality follows the measured load and changes\n  without a click or a gap.\n- It uses all CPU cores when the platform allows it and works on one core\n43:| 4. Reverse simulation (listening)             | Audio → IPA → language → text by inverting the simulator, with syllable highlighting, in the library, the command line, the server and the app                            | Needs the metrics and recordings of stage 0, and the voice parameters of stage 2 to fit a speaker                                                  |\n167:The Russian stress of [#48](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/issues/48) (`findRussianStress()` in `src/g2p/russian.js`) takes, in this order, a typed mark (`+` or U+0301), a typed `ё`, one of the 67 homograph spellings of `src/g2p/russian-homographs.js` chosen by cue words around it (Yarowsky 1997: `near`, `before`, `after`, `infinitive`, and `case` for genitive singular against nominative plural, `из города` ˈɡorədə, `большие города` ɡərɐˈda), one of 3 691 whole forms, a form with `е` read as `ё` when only that one is known (`еще` jɪˈɕːo), the longer of a stem of 6 639 with an ending (`раб+от|а`, `стол|+`) as written or with `ё`, and a guess by the word ending. The stems and forms in `data/lexicon/ru-stress.txt` are written by hand for the most frequent words of Common Voice Russian text (CC0-1.0); `ru.js` grew from 3 541 to 58 979 bytes, with the letters of the words stored as ASCII (`letters` field of `vslex`). The guess table counts endings of 2 to 6 letters shared by at least 5 lexicon words with at least 60 % agreeing on the stress (the issue asked for 2 to 4 letters, 10 words and 75 %, which gave 62.3 %; `node experiments/issue-48-guess-params.mjs`) and is right for 74.0 % of the held-out fifth. On the 222 hand-marked sentences of `tests/fixtures/russian-stress.txt` (three stories by Chekhov, public domain) the share of words with the marked stress went from 52.6 % on main to 97.9 %, of homograph words from 36.0 % to 96.0 % (`node experiments/issue-48-fixture-share.mjs`, [before](../experiments/issue-48/fixture-share-before.txt), [after](../experiments/issue-48/fixture-share-after.txt)); 108 lexicon items and 3 homographs were added after measuring the fixture, without them it is 87.6 %. The remaining misses are mostly names (Очумелов, Хрюкин) and homographs whose cue is far away (`письма`, `пасти`, `узнает`).\n177:The whisper of [#53](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/issues/53) (`[whisper]`, `{W … W}`, `<vs:phonation name=\"whisper\">`, `ạ`, `ḁ`) is a plan channel `whisper` (0 … 1) that turns the voice source into the turbulence of [#35](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/issues/35) at a half-open glottis of 40 mm²: no pulses, no pulse modulation, a glottal reflection lowered by `WHISPER_OPENING` (F1 +175 Hz on average at tier high), segments 1.3 times as long, a level 25 dB below the voice (30 dB soft, 20 dB for a stage whisper of 20 mm²), a level cue of the intended pitch, and the voiced and voiceless consonants kept apart by their closure, burst and frication; values between 0 and 1 give a whispery voice. `voicedShare()`, `energyRatio()` and `centreOfGravity()` measure it: \"Please call Stella.\" whispered has no voiced frames (plain 0.83), +15.8 dB of energy ratio and a centre of gravity of 1214 Hz against 416 Hz ([docs/markup.md](markup.md#whisper)). The Rust engine renders a whisper in JavaScript until [#82](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/issues/82).\n179:The emotions of [#55](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/issues/55) (`[angry]`, `[sad 0.5]`, `<vs:emotion name=\"happy\" intensity=\"0.8\">`, `<vs:emotion arousal=\"0.5\" valence=\"-0.3\">`) are rows of rules, not a sound source: `EMOTION_PRESETS` has twelve presets (neutral, angry, happy, sad, afraid and bored from the formant-synthesis profiles of Burkhardt and Sendlmeier 2000, `verified: true`; surprised and disgusted after Pell et al. 2009 and tender, sarcastic, confident and hesitant as own choices, `verified: false`) that set pitch, range, rate, effort, phonation, pauses, the length of stressed vowels, a glide in stressed vowels, a final rise, vowel precision and a smile, scaled by an intensity (semitones × i, factors f^i); a neutral emotion with arousal, valence or dominance uses the rules of Schröder et al. (2001) instead (`emotionChanges()`). The planner composes the changes with every span as an outer span, so `[angry][soft]…` stays soft (`realiseEmotion()`). Against plain \"The train leaves at seven.\" (tier medium, seed 1, headroom 20; `node experiments/issue-55-emotion-measure.mjs`): `[angry]` +14.13 st (7 st plus its effort), range × 2.85, duration × 0.80, H1-H2 -7.39 dB; `[happy]` +9.79 st, range × 3.48; `[sad]` -3.85 st, range × 0.84, duration × 1.83, H1-H2 +6.32 dB, -7.5 dB; `[afraid]` +22.08 st with a final rise of 2.83 st; `[bored]` -3.64 st, range × 0.52, stressed vowels × 1.75; `[happy]` raises F2 of `ˈa` by 5.8 % (`node experiments/issue-55-smile.mjs`). Text without an emotion gives the same samples as before (`node experiments/issue-55-plain-identity.mjs`), and the Rust engine renders the same samples, since emotions only change the plan. The listening harness of [#20](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/issues/20) gets choice trials, a confusion matrix and `binomialTailP()`, and `examples/listening-test/emotions.sentences.json` builds 48 trials in four languages; the test itself has not been run with listeners ([docs/listening-tests/emotions.md](listening-tests/emotions.md)). The tables are in [docs/markup.md](markup.md#emotions-and-attitudes).\n204:### Roadmap 4: Reverse simulation (listening)\n238:The formant tracker of [#60](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/issues/60) (`src/recognition/formants.js`, `trackFormants` and the stage `createFormantTracker`) takes the roots of the LPC models of orders p, p - 2 and p - 4 as candidates, numbers them F1 .. F4 by dynamic programming against the resonances of a uniform tube of the tract length (Talkin 1987) and smooths each formant with a Kalman filter and a Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoother; a stream fixes each frame 10 frames (50 ms) later. Changes to the plan of the issue, each measured: the local cost is |f - ref| / ref + min(2 B / f, 1.3), because |f - ref| / 1000 + B / f labels the F2 of the female and child /i/ as F3 and leaves 1756 of 6000 steady-vowel frames invalid or more than 20 % off against 867 (`node experiments/issue-60-vowels.mjs`); the tract length is estimated in up to 3 passes from vowel-like frames only (periodic, loud, not nasal), since consonants pull it towards 16.5 cm (`node experiments/issue-60-length.mjs`); the nasal flag uses a lowest candidate below 0.9 ref[1] with a band drop and a high-band test, which flags 70 % of the nasal frames and 6.7 % of the vowel frames of the calibration set (`node experiments/issue-60-nasal.mjs`). The truth of the tests is `tubeFormants` of the planned area function, read on its 5 Hz grid by a 50 Hz scan and a hill climb (`gridFormants` in `tests/helpers/recognition-truth.js`, identical on 4350 frames and ten times faster, `node experiments/issue-60-truth.mjs`), so that `tests/recognition-formants.test.js` runs in about 30 s. The tests give the tract lengths 13.82, 17.24 and 19.43 cm for 13, 16.5 and 19 cm, a stream within 30 Hz of the batch in at least 99.6 % of the frames and 0.03 of real time at 16000 Hz. The audit targets (F1 within 5 %, F2 and F3 within 4 % of the planned formants) are not met: in [experiments/issue-11-audit-m4a.txt](../experiments/issue-11-audit-m4a.txt) `trackFormants` has mean errors of 7.2–17.9 % for F1, 4.2–5.6 % for F2 and 2.8–4.5 % for F3, and the `renderer formants` block shows that the rendered sound itself differs from the planned formants by 5.9–7.2 % in F1 and 5.0–5.6 % in F2, above the targets, so no tracker can meet them against that truth. On the golden set 99.6 % of the voiced frames have F1 to F3 and 0.4 % of the F2 steps jump by more than 300 Hz ([docs/reports/recognition-formants.md](reports/recognition-formants.md)); the VTR formant database is refused by the licence policy (`datasets/refused.json`), so no error per formant is measured on real speech. The non-uniqueness of the inverse solution can also be resolved by including regularization and continuity terms in the optimization cost function.11, 13, 18, 19 The regularization term is designed to discourage VT configurations farther from the mean or neutral position and usually takes the form of the sum of squares of articulatory parameters minus their nominal values.18, 19 The continuity term can be the “geometric” distance from the articulatory parameters of the previous frame in a frame-wise optimization 13 or sum of squares of the first time-derivatives of articulatory parameters over several frames for global optimization over the speech segment.19 The continuity terms also result in smoother estimated articulatory trajectories, which are desirable since human articulation is controlled by muscles of finite power, and therefore, human articulatory trajectories are necessarily smooth.

Listening runs the same simulation\nin reverse: it finds the head, the voice and the movements that would have\nproduced the sound it hears, and reads the speech off those movements. Nothing\nis recorded and nothing is learned by a neural network. The project is in the\npublic domain and is a gift to everyone.\n\nThis document is the single statement of where the project is going. It is\nupdated by every pull request that changes the direction; the history is at the\nend. The step-by-step plan that implements it is [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).\n\n## Principles\n\nThese are rules, not preferences. A change that breaks one of them is not\nmerged.\n\n1. **Physics and mathematics only.** Sound comes from simulated air, folds,\n   walls and turbulence. Recognition comes from inverting that simulation.\n   No neural network is used anywhere: not in the library, not in the app,\n   not in the tests and not in the tools that build the data tables. No\n   recorded speech is played back or concatenated. The exact boundary is in\n   [What counts as a neural network](#what-counts-as-a-neural-network).\n2. **One model, two directions.** Speaking and listening share the same head,\n   the same articulation channels, the same IPA inventory and the same\n   prosody rules. A feature is finished when it works both ways: whatever the\n   simulator can say, it can recognise, and every mode of speech it detects, it\n   can produce.\n3. **Always through IPA.** Text is never mapped to sound directly, and sound\n   is never mapped to text directly. Speaking is text in a language → IPA →\n   audio. Listening is audio → IPA → the language, or the mix of languages,\n   → text. IPA with its tone, stress, length and voice-quality marks is the\n   interchange format between every stage and between the two directions.\n4. **The highest quality the device can afford, never silence.** The most\n   accurate simulation is the reference. Every device gets the most detailed\n   variant it can run in real time, measured on that device in the background,\n   and the quality steps down while speaking the moment the device falls\n   behind. The same holds for listening.\n5. **It works at the bottom too.** Synthesis, recognition and voice copying\n   all work at the lowest settings: narrow-band audio, the cheapest solver, one\n   CPU core. More cores, a GPU and higher settings make it better, never make\n   it possible.\n6. **Everything that changes a voice is a parameter.** Anatomy, the vocal\n   folds, breathing, articulation habits, accent and expression are numbers\n   with physical units, documented ranges and sources. A voice is a set of\n   those numbers, so it can be edited, saved, copied from a recording and\n   compared.\n7. **Measured against real speech.** Claims of quality are backed by numbers\n   computed on public recordings of real people with transcripts, by\n   algorithms that are themselves free of neural networks, and by listening\n   tests with people. A claim that was not measured is written as a goal.\n8. **Reproducible.** The same input, seed and settings give the same samples\n   on every runtime. Results of experiments are committed with the script\n   that produced them.\n9. **Public domain.** The code is released under the Unlicense. Data that is\n   committed to the repository is public domain or CC0. Dependencies have\n   permissive licences. Anything else is fetched at test time and never\n   redistributed.\n\n## What the system does when the vision is reached\n\n### Speaking\n\n- Reads text in every supported language, normalises it, converts it to IPA\n  and speaks it with a voice that people cannot tell from a recording of a\n  person in a blind listening test. That is the meaning of \"state of the art\"\n  here, and it is a goal, not a current claim.\n- Speaks in every common mode of speech: statements, all kinds of questions,\n  exclamations, commands, lists and asides; lexical tones and pitch accents;\n  word stress and rhythm; regional and foreign accents; soft, normal, loud and\n  shouted speech with gradual changes of loudness; whisper, breathy, creaky,\n  pressed and falsetto voice; emotions and attitudes; breaths, laughter, sighs\n  and hesitations.\n- Simulates the voice source as a physical system (vocal folds driven by lung\n  pressure, coupled to the air below and above them), the turbulence at\n  constrictions, the losses in the walls and the radiation from the mouth and\n  nose, in 1D for speed and in full 3D for accuracy.\n- Highlights every syllable in the text at the moment it is spoken.\n\n### Listening\n\n- Takes a recording or a live microphone and returns IPA with times, the\n  language or languages spoken, and the text, using the simulation in reverse.\n- Recognises the same modes of speech that it can produce and writes them\n  down with the same marks: tones, stress, sentence type, loudness, whisper\n  and other voice qualities, emotion.\n- Highlights every syllable as it is recognised.\n\n### Copying a voice\n\n- Works in several passes that feed each other. The first pass fits the\n  configuration of the voice: the size and shape of the head, the vocal folds,\n  the habits of articulation. The second pass inverts the simulation with\n  that configuration to recover the movements and the phonemes. As the person\n  keeps speaking both estimates are refined until they are stable. From then\n  on the system holds a voice it can speak with and a recogniser tuned to that\n  speaker, and it can follow what the person says.\n- Reproduces a real recording: the copy says the same words with the same\n  timing, melody and voice quality, close enough to be measured against the\n  original.\n\n### Running everywhere\n\n- The simulation core is written in Rust. In browsers it runs as WebAssembly\n  in a background worker and is the default engine; the same core runs natively\n  in the command line tool and the server. The JavaScript implementation stays\n  as the readable reference and as the fallback.\n- A short benchmark runs in the background when the page loads, without sound\n  and without blocking the interface, and decides the precision for this\n  device. While speaking, the quality follows the measured load and changes\n  without a click or a gap.\n- It uses all CPU cores when the platform allows it and works on one core\n  when it does not.\n- Expensive tests (full 3D renders, recognition of datasets, voice copying)\n  run in manually triggered GitHub Actions workflows; the tests that run on\n  every pull request stay fast.\n\n## What counts as a neural network\n\nNot allowed, in the product, the tests, the build tools and the continuous\nintegration:\n\n- Artificial neural networks of any kind and size (perceptrons, convolutional,\n  recurrent, transformer and diffusion models), whether trained by this project\n  or downloaded.\n- Libraries whose purpose is to run or train them.\n- Scoring our output with neural models (for example neural speech recognisers\n  or neural quality predictors).\n\nAllowed:\n\n- Physical simulation and its inversion.\n- Closed-form mathematics and signal processing: Fourier and linear-prediction\n  analysis, filters, cepstra, autocorrelation.\n- Search and optimisation: dynamic programming, Viterbi decoding, least\n  squares, gradient descent on the parameters of the physical model,\n  derivative-free and evolutionary optimisers, Kalman and particle filters.\n- Tables with a documented source: pronunciation dictionaries, measured\n  anatomical dimensions, vowel formants, and counts taken from public text or\n  recordings (for example how often one phoneme follows another). Every table\n  is small enough to read, is produced by a committed script and names its\n  data.\n- Calibrating the constants of the rules and of the physical model against\n  recordings by optimisation.\n\nNeural systems remain the yardstick. Their published scores are quoted, and\ntheir audio may be one of the samples in a listening test with people. [2026-11-22T09:12:17.516Z] [STDERR] # Vision
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.517Z] [STDERR] voice-simulator is a physical model of the human voice that works in both
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.520Z] [STDERR] directions:
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.522Z] [STDERR] ```
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.523Z] [STDERR] text in a language  ->  IPA  ->  articulation  ->  sound      (speaking)
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.525Z] [STDERR] text in a language  <-  IPA  <-  articulation  <-  sound      (listening)
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.528Z] [STDERR] ```
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.530Z] [STDERR] Speaking simulates the air in a human head. Listening runs the same simulation
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.531Z] [STDERR] in reverse: it finds the head, the voice and the movements that would have
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.533Z] [STDERR] produced the sound it hears, and reads the speech off those movements. Nothing
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.534Z] [STDERR] is recorded and nothing is learned by a neural network. The project is in the
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.536Z] [STDERR] public domain and is a gift to everyone.
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.538Z] [STDERR] This document is the single statement of where the project is going. It is
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.539Z] [STDERR] updated by every pull request that changes the direction; the history is at the
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.540Z] [STDERR] end. The step-by-step plan that implements it is [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.542Z] [STDERR] ## Principles
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.543Z] [STDERR] These are rules, not preferences. A change that breaks one of them is not
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.544Z] [STDERR] merged.
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.545Z] [STDERR] 1. **Physics and mathematics only.** Sound comes from simulated air, folds,
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.545Z] [STDERR]    walls and turbulence. Recognition comes from inverting that simulation.
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.546Z] [STDERR]    No neural network is used anywhere: not in the library, not in the app,
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.548Z] [STDERR]    not in the tests and not in the tools that build the data tables. No
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.549Z] [STDERR]    recorded speech is played back or concatenated. The exact boundary is in
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.550Z] [STDERR]    [What counts as a neural network](#what-counts-as-a-neural-network).
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.552Z] [STDERR] 2. **One model, two directions.** Speaking and listening share the same head,
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.553Z] [STDERR]    the same articulation channels, the same IPA inventory and the same
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.554Z] [STDERR]    prosody rules. A feature is finished when it works both ways: whatever the
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.556Z] [STDERR]    simulator can say, it can recognise, and every mode of speech it detects, it
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.557Z] [STDERR]    can produce.
[2026-11-22T09:12:17.558Z] [STDERR] 3. **Always through IPA.** Text is never mapped to sound directly, and sound

For every fourth periodic frame with `velum < 0.1`: Nelder-Mead (1965) over `height`, `backness`, `rounding`, `tongueAmount`, `tongueLocation`, `tongueArea`; start at the smoothed values, first step 5 % of the range; cost = `D / 16` with the envelope of `tractResponse` (#64) for the areas of `tractShape`, plus `sum_c ((a_c - smoothed_c) / (2 * s_c))^2`; at most 60 evaluations. Result `track`: `frameRate` (`1 / frames.hop`), `frameCount`, `duration`, `startTime`, `committed`, `head` (the voice), `channels` (21 arrays as in a plan), `variance` (21 arrays), `confidence` (`Float32Array`, `exp(-c / 8)` of the chosen row, 0 in long gaps), `candidates` (`{count, index, cost}`: the row numbers as `Int32Array` and costs as `Float32Array`, `count` per frame, row-major; -1 where absent).\n12. `articulationPlan(track)` returns an object with `tokens: []`, `segments: []` and the fields `head`, `frameRate`, `frameCount`, `duration` and `channels` of the track; `renderPlan` accepts it.\n13. Exports: `invertArticulation(frames, options)`, `createArticulationInverter(frames, options)`, `articulationPlan`.\n\nBudget on the reference machine of #58: at most 10 % of real time at 16000 and 8000 Hz without refinement; refinement at most 1 times real time. Delay in a stream: `lag * hop` = 150 ms.\n\n## Tests\n\nNew file `tests/recognition-inversion.test.js`. Speech comes from `synthesize` (`solver: 'waveguide'`, `seed: 1`), which also returns the plan; truth = `sampleState(plan, t)` at the frame times. Unit tests pass the true head as `voice`, so that errors of #63 do not hide errors made here. Error of a channel = RMS difference divided by its range, over periodic frames. Unit tests use a codebook of 5000 rows built once per file.\n\n- `recovers steady vowels`: the 31 vowels, 300 ms each, male and female: `height` within 0.15 and `backness` within 0.2 at the middle frame for at least 85 % of the vowels. `rounding` is printed, not gated: rounding and backness lower the same formants and trade against each other.\n- `recovers a sentence`: \"The north wind and the sun were disputing which was the stronger.\" at 16000 Hz: `height` at most 0.12, `backness` 0.15, `voicing` 0.15, `f0` within 3 %. At 8000 Hz: 0.15 and 0.20. `rounding` and `velum` are printed with the target 0.25.\n- `finds the lips in a closure`: `apa`, `ata`, `aka`: at the middle of the closure `lipAmount` is above 0.5 for `apa` only. The error of `tongueLocation` for `ata` and `aka` is printed (target 0.15).\n- `moves no faster than the planner`: no channel changes by more than `3 * s_c` between two frames.\n- `renders back close to the input`: `renderPlan(articulationPlan(track))` against the input with `melCepstralDistortion` of #18: at most 5 dB at 16000 Hz and 6 dB at 8000 Hz.\n- `refinement does not hurt`: with `refine: true` the distortion of the test before is not higher.\n- `stream agrees with batch`: 95 % of the committed values differ by less than 5 % of the range.\n- `stays within the CPU budget`: prints `inversion rtf <x>`; fails above 0.4.\n\nHeavy test `tests/heavy/recognition-inversion.test.js` (#14): for each golden utterance (#17) fit the voice on all utterances of the speaker, invert, render back and write the distortion per utterance with `writeReport('recognition-inversion', ...)`.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `node --test tests/recognition-inversion.test.js` passes on Node.js, Bun and Deno with the thresholds above.\n- [ ] `node scripts/calibrate-inversion.mjs` run twice writes the same file, byte for byte.\n- [ ] The CI log of `stays within the CPU budget` shows at most 0.10.\n- [ ] `reports/heavy/recognition-inversion.md` gives the mel-cepstral distortion of the render-back for every golden utterance. Remove the mean across the selected frequencies to ignore gain.\nfunction harmonics(samples, rate, time, pitch, bands) {\n  const length = Math.round(0.04 * rate);\n  const first = Math.round(rate * time - length / 2);\n  const real = new Float64Array(fft.size);\n  const imag = new Float64Array(fft.size);\n  for (let i = 0; i < length; i++) {\n    const window = 0.5 - 0.5 * Math.cos((2 * Math.PI * i) / (length - 1));\n    real[i] = window * (samples[first + i] ?? 0);\n  }\n  fft.forward(real, imag);\n  const peaks = bands.map((multiple) => {\n    const bin = (multiple * pitch * fft.size) / rate;\n    const floor = Math.floor(bin);\n    const fraction = bin - floor;\n    const power = (i) => real[i] ** 2 + imag[i] ** 2;\n    return (\n      10 *\n      Math.log10(\n        1e-10 + (1 - fraction) * power(floor) + fraction * power(floor + 1)\n      )\n    );\n  });\n  const mean = peaks.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0) / peaks.length;\n  return peaks.map((level) => level - measuredPitch(recording, time, source) {\n  const { plan, frames, pitch } = recording;\n  const observed = pitch.f0[Math.round(time / frames.hop)];\n  return source === 'planned'\n    ? const vowels = Object.keys(VOWELS);\n  const seeds = codebookSeeds().filter(({ kind }) => kind === 'vowel');\n  return (f0) => {\n    const pitch = 100 * 2 ** (Math.round(48 * Math.log2(f0 / 100)) /   return {\n          vowel: vowels[i],\n          harmonics: harmonics(audio, sampleRate, 0.055, pitch, bands),\n        };\n      });\n      cache.set(pitch, { bands, models });\n    }\n    return cache.get(pitch);\n  };\n}\n\nfunction nearest(samples, rate, time, f0, { bands, models }) {\n  const measured = harmonics(samples, rate, time, f0, bands);\n  const logHz = bands.map((multiple) => Math.log2(multiple * f0));\n  const mean = logHz.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0) / logHz.length;\n  const centered = logHz.map((value) => value - mean);\n  const spread = centered.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value ** 2, 0);\n  return models.map(({ vowel, harmonics: reference }) => {\n    const delta = reference.map((level, i) => level - measured[i]);\n    const slope =\n      delta.reduce((sum, value, i) => sum + value * centered[i], 0) / spread;\n    return {\n      vowel,\n      raw: delta.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value ** 2, 0),\n      detrended: delta.reduce(\n        (sum, value, i) => sum + (value - slope * centered[i]) ** 2,\n        0\n      ),\n    };\n  });\n}\n\nfunction evaluate(recordings, sampleRate, source, candidates) {\n  const stats = {\n    raw: { candidates(f0)\n      );\n      const { height, backness, symbol } = token.phoneme;\n      for (const cost of ['raw', 'detrended']) {\n        scores.sort((a, b) => a[cost] - b[cost]);\n        const Steps:\n   1. `spoken = synthesize(text, { lang, tier, preset, seed })`.\n   2. `heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level })` with `level = levelForTier(tier)`. Do not pass the language: it must be found.\n   3. Return `{ spoken, heard, seconds }` plus these numbers, computed with `errorRate` and `editDistance` of #18:\n      - `per`: `errorRate(spoken.ipa, heard.ipa, 'phone')`;\n      - `wer` (not for `zh`) and `cer`: `errorRate(text, heard.text, unit)` with `'word'` and `'char'`;\n      - `soundWer`: the same as `wer`, but each word of both texts is first replaced by its IPA from `textToIpa(...).words[].ipa`, so that a word which sounds the same (`sea` and `see`, 他 and 她) is not an error. For `zh` the tokens are the characters;\n      - `toneErrors` (only `zh`): edit distance between the two lists of tones, one entry per syllable (the tone letters in the syllable's IPA, the empty string for the neutral tone);\n      - `stressHits` (only `en`, `ru`): among the reference words with two or more syllables whose recognised word has the same number of syllables, how many have `stress: 1` on the same syllable;\n      - `timeErrors`: pair the reference and recognised syllables through the edit-distance path over syllable IPA; for each pair with equal IPA collect `|start difference|` and `|end difference|` in ms;\n      - `languageRight`: `heard.languages[0].language === lang` after sorting by `share`, largest first;\n      - `sentenceMark`: the last of `. ? !` in `heard.text`, with `।`, `。`, `？`, `！` mapped to their ASCII form, or `null`.\n3. Example:\n\n   ```text\n   { start: 0.4, end: 1.9, from: 1, to: 5, effort: 0.75,\n     notation: 'f', confidence: 0.8 }\n   ```\n\n   `start`, `end` in seconds; `from`, `to` are indexes into `result.words` (`to` exclusive); then only the decided keys of the mode object of #50; `notation` is the brace label or `null` when IPA has none (emotion); `confidence` is 0 to 1.\n\n2. Baseline: what this speaker sounds like in a normal voice.\n   - With `options.voice` (a voice of #41 or #63): synthesise `tests/fixtures/recognition/baseline.txt` (one neutral sentence per language, write it here) with that voice at the tier that matches `sampleRate` and measure the features of step 3. Cache by voice.\n   - Without it: the median of each feature over the utterance. Then only changes inside the utterance and the signs that need no baseline (whisper, creak, falsetto) can be reported. Do not guess the rest.\n3. Features per word, from the frames of its vowels (`analyzeFrames`, `trackPitch`, `trackFormants`, `inverseFilter`, `mode-features.js`): `alpha` (alpha ratio, dB), `pitch` (median, Hz and semitones re the baseline), `f1` (mean F1 minus the baseline F1 of the same vowel, Hz; `null` without `options.voice`), `voiced` (voiced share of the vowel frames), `h1h2` (corrected for formants, dB), `hnr` (dB), `cpp` (dB), `jitter` (%), `rate` (syllables per second of the word and its two neighbours). `d` before a name below means \"minus the baseline\".\n4. Effort in decibels (inverse of `EFFORT_RULES` of #52): `Etilt = dalpha / 0.2`, `Epitch = dpitch in Hz / 5`, `Ef1 = df1 / 3.5`; `E = 0.6 * Etilt + 0.2 * Epitch + 0.2 * Ef1` (without `f1`: 0.75 and 0.25); `effort = clamp(0.5 + E / 40, 0, 1)`, rounded to the nearest of 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1. `confidence = max(0, 1 - |Etilt - Epitch| / 20)`.\n5. Label per word, first rule that fits (start values; tune with the tests):\n\n   | Rule | Keys | Label |\n   | --- | --- | --- |\n   | `voiced < 0.05` and energy ratio 6 dB above the baseline | `phonation.whisper: 1` | `W` |\n   | median pitch below 70 Hz | `phonation.creaky: 1` | `C` |\n   | `dpitch >= 10` st and `h1h2 >= 8` | `phonation.falsetto: 1` | `F` |\n   | `h1h2 < 0`, `dhnr <= -3`, `jitter >= 3` | `phonation.harsh: 1` | `V!` |\n   | `jitter >= 5`, and `h1h2 < 0` or `dpitch <= -8` st | `phonation.creaky` | `V̰` |\n   | `dh1h2 <= -3` and `dhnr >= -2` | `phonation.tension: 1` | `V͈` |\n   | `dh1h2 >= 1` and (`dcpp <= -1` or `dhnr <= -3`) | `phonation.breathy` | `V̤` |\n   | voiced, `hnr < 10`, `dhnr <= -4` | `phonation.whisper: 0.5` | `Ṿ` |\n   | `dh1h2` between 2 and 5, `dhnr` between -2 and 2 | `phonation.tension: -1` | `V͉` |\n   | `effort` of step 4 is not 0.5 and no row above fits | `effort` | `pp`, `p`, `f`, `ff` |\n   | `rate / baseline rate >= 1.2` (may be added to any row) | `rate: 1.3` | `allegro` |\n   | `rate / baseline rate <= 0.83` (may be added to any row) | `rate: 0.75` | `lento` |\n\n   Degree of breathy and creaky voice: `d = clamp(dh1h2 / 3.2, 0, 1)` (breathy) or `clamp(jitter / 5, 0, 1)` (creaky), rounded to 0.33, 0.67 or 1 and written as `{1V̤`, `{V̤`, `{3V̤`.
