Requirements of #11 covered: R6, R17, R18, R19 (see the [case study](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-11/README.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\nRecognition says how something was spoken, not only what: soft or loud, whispered, breathy, creaky, pressed, falsetto, harsh, fast or slow, and with which emotion. The answer is a list of spans in `result.modes` and the same ExtIPA/VoQS brace marks in `result.ipa` that the synthesiser reads (`{f … f}`, `{W … W}`, `{V̤ … V̤}`), so that speaking the result again gives the same manner of speech.\n\n## Why\n\nThe issue asks for volume, whisper, emotions and \"all common modes of speech\" for input as well as output. #52 to #55 make the synthesiser speak these modes; each of them lists the measurable signs of its mode. This issue reads those signs back. Copying a recording (#79) needs them.\n\n## Current state\n\n- After #73, `recognize` returns `modes: []`. #70 (if merged) adds spans for emphasis and sentence tunes and fixes the span shape.\n- `analyzeVoice` in `src/analysis/voice-features.js` gives one value per recording for `f0`, `h1h2`, `hnr` and others. It gives nothing over time.\n- After #52, #53 and #54, `src/analysis/mode-features.js` has `levelDb`, `alphaRatio`, `voicedShare`, `energyRatio`, `centreOfGravity`, `cpp` and `jitterPercent`, and each of those issues has a table \"How the mode is written and recognised\" with target values. After #61, `inverseFilter` gives the measures of the voice source per frame.\n- The absolute level of a recording says nothing about effort: it depends on the microphone and its distance. The research notes (file 4) give the usable signs: [REDACTED]\n- Emotion: the same notes say that activation (calm or excited) can be heard from prosody, that people name one of 7 emotions from prosody alone about 58 % right (Pell et al. 2009), and that pleasant or unpleasant is hard to hear. No public-domain recordings of emotions or whisper exist.\n\n## What to do\n\nCreate `src/recognition/modes.js` exporting `recognizeModes(samples, sampleRate, result, options)`. It returns a copy of `result` (shape of `recognize`) with `modes` and `ipa` filled in.\n\n1. Span shape, as in #70: the shape of `plan.modes` of #50 plus four keys. Example:\n\n   ```text\n   { start: 0.4, end: 1.9, from: 1, to: 5, effort: 0.75,\n     notation: 'f', confidence: 0.8 }\n   ```\n\n   `start`, `end` in seconds; `from`, `to` are indexes into `result.words` (`to` exclusive); then only the decided keys of the mode object of #50; `notation` is the brace label or `null` when IPA has none (emotion); `confidence` is 0 to 1.\n\n2. Baseline: what this speaker sounds like in a normal voice.\n   - With `options.voice` (a voice of #41 or #63): synthesise `tests/fixtures/recognition/baseline.txt` (one neutral sentence per language, write it here) with that voice at the tier that matches `sampleRate` and measure the features of step 3. Cache by voice.\n   - Without it: the median of each feature over the utterance. Then only changes inside the utterance and the signs that need no baseline (whisper, creak, falsetto) can be reported. Do not guess the rest.\n3. Features per word, from the frames of its vowels (`analyzeFrames`, `trackPitch`, `trackFormants`, `inverseFilter`, `mode-features.js`): `alpha` (alpha ratio, dB), `pitch` (median, Hz and semitones re the baseline), `f1` (mean F1 minus the baseline F1 of the same vowel, Hz; `null` without `options.voice`), `voiced` (voiced share of the vowel frames), `h1h2` (corrected for formants, dB), `hnr` (dB), `cpp` (dB), `jitter` (%), `rate` (syllables per second of the word and its two neighbours). `d` before a name below means \"minus the baseline\".\n4. Effort in decibels (inverse of `EFFORT_RULES` of #52): `Etilt = dalpha / 0.2`, `Epitch = dpitch in Hz / 5`, `Ef1 = df1 / 3.5`; `E = 0.6 * Etilt + 0.2 * Epitch + 0.2 * Ef1` (without `f1`: 0.75 and 0.25); `effort = clamp(0.5 + E / 40, 0, 1)`, rounded to the nearest of 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1. `confidence = max(0, 1 - |Etilt - Epitch| / 20)`.\n5. Label per word, first rule that fits (start values; tune with the tests):\n\n   | Rule | Keys | Label |\n   | --- | --- | --- |\n   | `voiced < 0.05` and energy ratio 6 dB above the baseline | `phonation.whisper: 1` | `W` |\n   | median pitch below 70 Hz | `phonation.creaky: 1` | `C` |\n   | `dpitch >= 10` st and `h1h2 >= 8` | `phonation.falsetto: 1` | `F` |\n   | `h1h2 < 0`, `dhnr <= -3`, `jitter >= 3` | `phonation.harsh: 1` | `V!` |\n   | `jitter >= 5`, and `h1h2 < 0` or `dpitch <= -8` st | `phonation.creaky` | `V̰` |\n   | `dh1h2 <= -3` and `dhnr >= -2` | `phonation.tension: 1` | `V͈` |\n   | `dh1h2 >= 1` and (`dcpp <= -1` or `dhnr <= -3`) | `phonation.breathy` | `V̤` |\n   | voiced, `hnr < 10`, `dhnr <= -4` | `phonation.whisper: 0.5` | `Ṿ` |\n   | `dh1h2` between 2 and 5, `dhnr` between -2 and 2 | `phonation.tension: -1` | `V͉` |\n   | `effort` of step 4 is not 0.5 and no row above fits | `effort` | `pp`, `p`, `f`, `ff` |\n   | `rate / baseline rate >= 1.2` (may be added to any row) | `rate: 1.3` | `allegro` |\n   | `rate / baseline rate <= 0.83` (may be added to any row) | `rate: 0.75` | `lento` |\n\n   Degree of breathy and creaky voice: `d = clamp(dh1h2 / 3.2, 0, 1)` (breathy) or `clamp(jitter / 5, 0, 1)` (creaky), rounded to 0.33, 0.67 or 1 and written as `{1V̤`, `{V̤`, `{3V̤`. Use the key names and signs that #54 really has; this table uses those of #50.\n\n6. From words to spans: join neighbouring words with the same label. One word between two words with the same label takes their label. A span shorter than 0.3 s is dropped, except whisper. Inside a span of 4 words or more with a label of effort, fit a line to `E` over time: a change of 8 dB or more gives `crescendo` (rising) or `diminuendo` instead.\n7. Whisper spans: use `findWhisper` of `src/recognition/whisper.js` when that file exists (#72); otherwise the first row of the table.\n8. Emotion, per phrase (words between pauses of 0.2 s or more):\n   1. Vector: pitch level (st), pitch span (95th minus 5th percentile, st), `rate` ratio, `E`, `dh1h2`, `dhnr`; each minus the baseline and divided by its scale: 2 st, 2 st, 0.15, 5 dB, 3 dB, 3 dB.\n   2. Reference vectors: on first use, synthesise the baseline sentence once per emotion name of #55 at intensity 1 with the baseline voice and measure the same vector. No trained model is used.\n   3. `activation` = mean of the first four components divided by 2, cut to -1…1. Always reported when `|activation| >= 0.3`, as `emotion: { arousal: activation }`.\n   4. Name: the nearest reference by Euclidean distance `near`; `next` is the second nearest. Report `emotion.name` only when `near <= 0.6 * (length of the vector)` and `near <= 0.8 * next`; `intensity` = length of the vector divided by the length of the reference, cut to 0…1; `confidence = 1 - near / next`.\n   5. When a name is reported, drop the effort, rate and phonation spans of that phrase which the emotion preset of #55 itself produces (same key, value within one step), so that speaking the result again does not apply them twice. `notation` is `null`.\n9. Sounds, only when #56 is merged: a noise of 0.3 to 0.7 s inside a pause is `⸨inhale⸩`; 3 or more bursts of voice at 4 to 6 per second are `⸨laugh⸩`; a steady `ə`-like vowel longer than 0.2 s next to a pause is `⸨filler⸩`. Add the token to `ipa`, and to `modes` a span `{ start, end, sound, notation, confidence }`.\n10. Write `ipa`: wrap the words of every span that has a label in `{label … label}`, with `formatIpa` of #50. Export `toPlanModes(modes)`: it returns `[{ from, to, mode }]` for `planUtterance(ipa, { modes })`, including the spans without a label.\n11. What cannot be decided is left out. [2026-11-22T09:43:12.046Z] [STDERR] L12: We present a framework for speech recognition that accounts for hidden articulatory information. We model the articulatory space using a codebook of articulatory configurations geometrically derived from EMA measurements available in the MOCHA database. The articulatory parameter set we derive is in the form of Maeda parameters. In turn, these parameters are used in a physiologically-motivated articulatory speech synthesizer based on the model by Sondhi and Schroeter.

Improvements are achieved when combining the probability scores generated using the distortion features with the scores using acoustic features.

Create `tests/helpers/roundtrip.js` exporting `roundTrip(text, options)` with `options = { lang, tier, preset, seed }`. Steps:\n   1. `spoken = synthesize(text, { lang, tier, preset, seed })`.\n   2. `heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level })` with `level = levelForTier(tier)`. Do not pass the language: it must be found.\n   3. Return `{ spoken, heard, seconds }` plus these numbers, computed with `errorRate` and `editDistance` of #18:\n      - `per`: `errorRate(spoken.ipa, heard.ipa, 'phone')`;\n      - `wer` (not for `zh`) and `cer`: `errorRate(text, heard.text, unit)` with `'word'` and `'char'`;\n      - `soundWer`: the same as `wer`, but each word of both texts is first replaced by its IPA from `textToIpa(...).words[].ipa`, so that a word which sounds the same (`sea` and `see`, 他 and 她) is not an error. For `zh` the tokens are the characters;\n      - `toneErrors` (only `zh`): edit distance between the two lists of tones, one entry per syllable (the tone letters in the syllable's IPA, the empty string for the neutral tone);\n      - `stressHits` (only `en`, `ru`): among the reference words with two or more syllables whose recognised word has the same number of syllables, how many have `stress: 1` on the same syllable;\n      - `timeErrors`: pair the reference and recognised syllables through the edit-distance path over syllable IPA; for each pair with equal IPA collect `|start difference|` and `|end difference|` in ms;\n      - `languageRight`: `heard.languages[0].language === lang` after sorting by `share`, largest first;\n      - `sentenceMark`: the last of `. ? !` in `heard.text`, with `।`, `。`, `？`, `！` mapped to their ASCII form, or `null`.\n3. Requirements of #11 covered: R6, R7, R11, R13, R18 (see the [case study](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-11/README.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\nA fixed list of 80 sentences (20 each for English, Russian, Hindi and Mandarin) is spoken by the simulator and recognised by `recognize`. The suite `roundtrip` of the heavy workflow measures how much of the text, the IPA, the syllable times and the language comes back, per audio tier and per preset voice, fails when a threshold is missed, and writes `docs/reports/roundtrip.md`. Three sentences run in every `npm test`.\n\n## Why\n\nRecognition is the simulation in reverse, so the simulator's own speech is the one input for which the right answer is known exactly: text, IPA and the time of every syllable. This is the regression baseline for every later change of the recogniser, and the proof that both directions work at 8000 Hz.\n\n## Current state\n\n- `synthesize(text, options)` returns an object with the keys `lang`, `accent`, `ipa`, `words`, `head`, `plan`, `timeline`, `sampleRate`, `samples` and `duration`. `timeline.words[].syllables[]` holds `ipa`, `stress`, `start`, `end` (seconds) and `text`.\n- Measured on this branch: the three smoke sentences below take 0.11 to 0.27 s each to synthesise at tier `minimal` (22050 Hz, 1.9 to 2.3 s of audio).\n- The 80 sentences were checked with the current text-to-IPA code. They give about 214 s of speech and contain 40 different phone symbols in English, 47 in Russian, 50 in Hindi and 40 in Mandarin, all four Mandarin tones, the half-third tone and the neutral tone, and statements, yes/no questions, question-word questions, exclamations and one-word sentences in each language. There are no digits and no erhua (see #46 and #43).\n- `HEAD_PRESET_NAMES` is `['any', 'male', 'female', 'child']`. Create `tests/helpers/roundtrip.js` exporting `roundTrip(text, options)` with `options = { lang, tier, preset, seed }`. Steps:\n   1. `spoken = synthesize(text, { lang, tier, preset, seed })`.\n   2. `heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level })` with `level = levelForTier(tier)`. Do not pass the language: it must be found.\n   3. Return `{ spoken, heard, seconds }` plus these numbers, computed with `errorRate` and `editDistance` of #18:\n      - `per`: `errorRate(spoken.ipa, heard.ipa, 'phone')`;\n      - `wer` (not for `zh`) and `cer`: `errorRate(text, heard.text, unit)` with `'word'` and `'char'`;\n      - `soundWer`: the same as `wer`, but each word of both texts is first replaced by its IPA from `textToIpa(...).words[].ipa`, so that a word which sounds the same (`sea` and `see`, 他 and 她) is not an error. For `zh` the tokens are the characters;\n      - `toneErrors` (only `zh`): edit distance between the two lists of tones, one entry per syllable (the tone letters in the syllable's IPA, the empty string for the neutral tone);\n      - `stressHits` (only `en`, `ru`): among the reference words with two or more syllables whose recognised word has the same number of syllables, how many have `stress: 1` on the same syllable;\n      - `timeErrors`: pair the reference and recognised syllables through the edit-distance path over syllable IPA; for each pair with equal IPA collect `|start difference|` and `|end difference|` in ms;\n      - `languageRight`: `heard.languages[0].language === lang` after sorting by `share`, largest first;\n      - `sentenceMark`: the last of `. ? !` in `heard.text`, with `।`, `。`, `？`, `！` mapped to their ASCII form, or `null`.\n3. Runs:\n   - set `main`: all 80 sentences, tiers `telephone`, `narrowband`, `wideband`, `minimal`, presets `male` and `female` (640 runs);\n   - set `voices`: sentences 1 to 5 of each language, presets `any` and `child`, tiers `telephone` and `wideband` (80 runs);\n   - set `tiers`: sentences 2 and 20 of each language, preset `male`, tiers `low`, `medium`, `high`, `ultra`, `studio` (40 runs). `reference` is left out because of its run time; say so in the report.\n   - `heavyLimit(80)` limits the number of sentences per set.\n   - Sum the edit distances and the reference lengths per language, tier and set before dividing; do not average the rates of single sentences.\n4. Gates (one `it` per row, so that a failure names the row). They hold for every language of set `main`:\n\n   | Tier | PER | soundWer | Tone errors | Syllable time, mean | Language right |\n   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n   | `wideband`, `minimal` | ≤ 5 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 30 ms | ≥ 95 % |\n   | `narrowband` | ≤ 8 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 12 % | ≤ 35 ms | ≥ 92 % |\n   | `telephone` | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 20 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 40 ms | ≥ 90 % |\n\n   Set `voices`: the gates of row `telephone` for every preset. Listening runs the same simulation\nin reverse: it finds the head, the voice and the movements that would have\nproduced the sound it hears, and reads the speech off those movements. Nothing\nis recorded and nothing is learned by a neural network. The project is in the\npublic domain and is a gift to everyone.\n\nThis document is the single statement of where the project is going. It is\nupdated by every pull request that changes the direction; the history is at the\nend. The step-by-step plan that implements it is [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).\n\n## Principles\n\nThese are rules, not preferences. A change that breaks one of them is not\nmerged.\n\n1. **Physics and mathematics only.** Sound comes from simulated air, folds,\n   walls and turbulence. Recognition comes from inverting that simulation.\n   No neural network is used anywhere: not in the library, not in the app,\n   not in the tests and not in the tools that build the data tables. No\n   recorded speech is played back or concatenated. The exact boundary is in\n   [What counts as a neural network](#what-counts-as-a-neural-network).\n2. **One model, two directions.** Speaking and listening share the same head,\n   the same articulation channels, the same IPA inventory and the same\n   prosody rules. A feature is finished when it works both ways: whatever the\n   simulator can say, it can recognise, and every mode of speech it detects, it\n   can produce.\n3. **Always through IPA.** Text is never mapped to sound directly, and sound\n   is never mapped to text directly. Speaking is text in a language → IPA →\n   audio. Listening is audio → IPA → the language, or the mix of languages,\n   → text. IPA with its tone, stress, length and voice-quality marks is the\n   interchange format between every stage and between the two directions.\n4. **The highest quality the device can afford, never silence.** The most\n   accurate simulation is the reference. Every device gets the most detailed\n   variant it can run in real time, measured on that device in the background,\n   and the quality steps down while speaking the moment the device falls\n   behind. The same holds for listening.\n5. **It works at the bottom too.** Synthesis, recognition and voice copying\n   all work at the lowest settings: narrow-band audio, the cheapest solver, one\n   CPU core. More cores, a GPU and higher settings make it better, never make\n   it possible.\n6. **Everything that changes a voice is a parameter.** Anatomy, the vocal\n   folds, breathing, articulation habits, accent and expression are numbers\n   with physical units, documented ranges and sources. A voice is a set of\n   those numbers, so it can be edited, saved, copied from a recording and\n   compared.\n7. **Measured against real speech.** Claims of quality are backed by numbers\n   computed on public recordings of real people with transcripts, by\n   algorithms that are themselves free of neural networks, and by listening\n   tests with people. A claim that was not measured is written as a goal.\n8. **Reproducible.** The same input, seed and settings give the same samples\n   on every runtime. Results of experiments are committed with the script\n   that produced them.\n9. **Public domain.** The code is released under the Unlicense. Data that is\n   committed to the repository is public domain or CC0. Dependencies have\n   permissive licences. Anything else is fetched at test time and never\n   redistributed.\n\n## What the system does when the vision is reached\n\n### Speaking\n\n- Reads text in every supported language, normalises it, converts it to IPA\n  and speaks it with a voice that people cannot tell from a recording of a\n  person in a blind listening test. That is the meaning of \"state of the art\"\n  here, and it is a goal, not a current claim.\n- Speaks in every common mode of speech: statements, all kinds of questions,\n  exclamations, commands, lists and asides; lexical tones and pitch accents;\n  word stress and rhythm; regional and foreign accents; soft, normal, loud and\n  shouted speech with gradual changes of loudness; whisper, breathy, creaky,\n  pressed and falsetto voice; emotions and attitudes; breaths, laughter, sighs\n  and hesitations.\n- Simulates the voice source as a physical system (vocal folds driven by lung\n  pressure, coupled to the air below and above them), the turbulence at\n  constrictions, the losses in the walls and the radiation from the mouth and\n  nose, in 1D for speed and in full 3D for accuracy.\n- Highlights every syllable in the text at the moment it is spoken.\n\n### Listening\n\n- Takes a recording or a live microphone and returns IPA with times, the\n  language or languages spoken, and the text, using the simulation in reverse.\n- Recognises the same modes of speech that it can produce and writes them\n  down with the same marks: tones, stress, sentence type, loudness, whisper\n  and other voice qualities, emotion.\n- Highlights every syllable as it is recognised.\n39:| 0. At the values the planner writes they give the shape of the vowel and consonant channels; moved, they widen the mouth (`JAW_AREA` = 0.8 per cm, 9 % more F1 of `[ɛ]` for 0.5 cm; time constant 0.02 s, so that a short `[z]` still reaches its gap), lengthen the lips or the pharynx (`stretchSections()`, the velum, the teeth and the noise source keep their distance from the lips) and scale the pharynx ([experiments/issue-40-articulators.txt](../experiments/issue-40-articulators.txt)). At telephone bandwidth, normalized autocorrelation helps distinguish periodic gaps in modal speech from whispered speech when the pitch tracker drops out.\n228:The analysis front end of [#58](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/issues/58) (`src/recognition/`) resamples the input chunk by chunk to 16000, 11025 or 8000 Hz (`createResampler`, within 3e-8 of `resample()` for 44100 to 16000 Hz) and fills one frame set of flat `Float32Array`s every 5 or 10 ms: energy, zero crossings, centre of gravity, tilt, six Liu (1996) bands, periodicity (Boersma 1993), 24 mel energies, 13 cepstra, LPC by Burg, autocorrelation or covariance, a minimum-statistics noise floor (Martin 2001) and a speech flag. One `createFft` serves the whole package. The noise floor is capped at the loudest speech frame minus 25 dB, not the loudest frame, because a recording that starts with noise would otherwise hold the floor 25 dB under the noise and call all of it speech (`node experiments/issue-58-noise-cap.mjs`: 0 of 200 noise frames are called speech instead of 200 of 200). It takes 0.0138 of real time at 16000 Hz and 0.0059 at 8000 Hz and adds at most 13.5 ms of delay (`node experiments/issue-58-rtf.mjs`, `node experiments/issue-58-delay.mjs`). Stages #59 to #66 read the frame set and follow the `createX(frames, options)` / `advance(final)` / `committed` pattern (`FrameStage` in `src/recognition/frontend.d.ts`). The Rust core has the root finder (the LPC roots of the three orders, warm-started frame by frame, the dominant cost) and the tract length (`crates/voice-simulator-core/src/formants.rs`, export `vs_formant_candidates`), the same candidates as JavaScript in `tests/rust-parity.test.js`; the numbering, the smoothing and the use of the Rust engine by the tracker are left to [#77](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/issues/77).\n232:Acoustic-to-articulatory inversion [#65](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/issues/65) reads the codebook and tracked formants, picks a Viterbi path with planner-scaled motion, and estimates tract means and variance with a random-walk Kalman filter and RTS smoother. `invertArticulation` processes a full recording, `createArticulationInverter` commits a fixed-lag prefix, and `articulationPlan` feeds the resulting 21 controls back into the renderer. Source controls use pitch, energy and three calibrated noise regressions. The two unsupported controls, lateral and glottal closure, have infinite variance. The [golden-set report](reports/recognition-inversion.md) records the current render-back error. [#150](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/issues/150) tracks it against the 9 dB research target: 60.749 dB, against 61.041 dB for a constant spectrum of the recording's mean shape and 42.622 dB for the per-frame best rendered codebook row. Two additions to the plan of the issue: f0 is that of the period starting at the frame (the path read half a period later), which keeps the fine error within the 15 cents of the issue, and the unvoiced state is cheaper in quiet frames (an energy drop or a frame near the noise floor), which ends voicing at a stop closure. Changes to the plan of the issue, each measured: the local cost is |f - ref| / ref + min(2 B / f, 1.3), because |f - ref| / 1000 + B / f labels the F2 of the female and child /i/ as F3 and leaves 1756 of 6000 steady-vowel frames invalid or more than 20 % off against 867 (`node experiments/issue-60-vowels.mjs`); the tract length is estimated in up to 3 passes from vowel-like frames only (periodic, loud, not nasal), since consonants pull it towards 16.5 cm (`node experiments/issue-60-length.mjs`); the nasal flag uses a lowest candidate below 0.9 ref[1] with a band drop and a high-band test, which flags 70 % of the nasal frames and 6.7 % of the vowel frames of the calibration set (`node experiments/issue-60-nasal.mjs`). The metric's scale makes 9 dB a very strict target\n\n`melCepstralDistortion` takes the orthonormal DCT of the natural logarithm of\n26 mel filter **powers**. The conventional mel-cepstral distortion (Kubichek\n1993, SPTK) uses cepstral coefficients of the log **amplitude** spectrum\nnormalised as a Fourier series. For the same spectral difference the\ncoefficients here are about 2 × sqrt(2 × 26) ≈ 14 times larger. The tilt\nexperiment measures 13.1 for every tilt size:\n\n| Linear spectral tilt | RMS log-spectrum difference | Conventional MCD | This metric |\n| -------------------- | --------------------------: | ---------------: | ----------: |\n| ±3 dB                |                     1.73 dB |          0.87 dB |    11.32 dB |\n| ±6 dB                |                     3.46 dB |          1.73 dB |    22.67 dB |\n| ±12 dB               |                     6.93 dB |          3.46 dB |    45.42 dB |\n\nSo 9 dB here is about 0.7 dB of conventional MCD, below the few dB that\npublished resynthesis systems usually report. A ±3 dB tilt alone fails the\ntarget. The README already says this cepstrum gives larger\nvalues than SPTK; the research notes say to compare only like with like. The\n9 dB target appears to come from conventional figures.\n\n### 2. The inversion follows almost none of the spectral changes\n\nA render whose spectrum never changes, with the mean shape of the recording,\nscores 61.041 dB. The inversion scores 60.749 dB and beats this reference on\nonly 14 of 24 utterances. The time-varying part of the render-back carries\nalmost no information about the recording on this metric. On `hi-05`\n(51.70 dB) the difference of the mean cepstra alone contributes 26.9 dB;\nremoving the mean of both cepstra leaves 43.5 dB, close to the 50.7 dB of\nthe recording against its own mean. `experiments/issue-150-diagnose.mjs`\nprints this decomposition.\n\n### 3. The codebook and source model bound the error far above 9 dB\n\nEvery one of the 5,000 codebook rows of each speaker was rendered for 85 ms\nat the speaker's pitch (`experiments/issue-150-templates.mjs`). Choosing,\nfor every recorded frame independently, the row whose steady render is\nclosest (no smoothness, no transition cost) gives 42.622 dB. A held row\nrendered through `articulationPlan` matches its stored template within 1.6\nto 6.7 dB (`experiments/issue-150-steady-check.mjs`), so this is a sound\nlower bound of any tract path through this codebook with the steady voiced\nsource. Real speech adds transitions, noise, f0 movement and spectral detail\nof the speaker that the head does not produce.\n\n### 4. Source and level contour\n\nThe rendered frame level has a standard deviation of 13 to 23 dB against 8\nto 10 dB in the recordings, with a correlation of 0.48 to 0.63, and 26 to 86\nscored frames per utterance are rendered silent, mostly where the frontend\nmarks non-speech and loudness becomes 0 (`experiments/issue-150-level.mjs`).\nIterative level fitting of the loudness channel made the subset worse (64.39\nto 65.16 and 65.67 dB on `hi-05`, `en-02`, `zh-01`, `ru-04`). The suite `roundtrip` of the heavy workflow measures how much of the text, the IPA, the syllable times and the language comes back, per audio tier and per preset voice, fails when a threshold is missed, and writes `docs/reports/roundtrip.md`. Three sentences run in every `npm test`.\\n\\n## Why\\n\\nRecognition is the simulation in reverse, so the simulator's own speech is the one input for which the right answer is known exactly: text, IPA and the time of every syllable. This is the regression baseline for every later change of the recogniser, and the proof that both directions work at 8000 Hz.\\n\\n## Current state\\n\\n- `synthesize(text, options)` returns an object with the keys `lang`, `accent`, `ipa`, `words`, `head`, `plan`, `timeline`, `sampleRate`, `samples` and `duration`. `timeline.words[].syllables[]` holds `ipa`, `stress`, `start`, `end` (seconds) and `text`.\\n- Measured on this branch: the three smoke sentences below take 0.11 to 0.27 s each to synthesise at tier `minimal` (22050 Hz, 1.9 to 2.3 s of audio).\\n- The 80 sentences were checked with the current text-to-IPA code. Type: **Feature**. Requirements of #11 covered: R6, R8, R9, R12, R13, R18, R19 (see the [case study](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-11/README.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\n`fitVoice(samples, sampleRate, options)` listens to a recording of one person and returns the head configuration of the simulator that sounds like that person, with an uncertainty for every fitted parameter. It works with and without the text that was spoken, on real speakers, at 8000 Hz, and it can be continued when more sound arrives. `matchVoice` stays and calls it.\n\n## Why\n\nThis is the first pass of the multi-pass algorithm of the issue: \"first try to fit best simulation settings to copy the voice\". The second pass (#65) asks which tongue positions explain the sound, and that question only has a good answer when the tube already has the length, the source and the pitch range of the speaker.\n\n## Current state\n\n- `matchVoice` and `matchVoiceSteps` in `src/analysis/voice-match.js` fit six parameters: `pitch`, `pitchRange`, `vocalTractLength`, `tenseness`, `breathiness`, `speechRate`. They render the transcript (or the fixed `MATCH_TEXT`) at 16000 Hz with `solver: 'waveguide'`, `seed: 1`, compare the features of `analyzeVoice`, and correct each parameter by a secant step; 4 rounds by default, at most 12. The result is `{head, preset, features, rendered, distance}`.\n- The features are utterance statistics (`f0`, `f0Range`, mean `formants`, `h1h2`, `hnr`, `syllableRate`) from frames that are each decided alone.\n- `tests/voice-match.test.js` uses only synthetic recordings (pitch, tract length and speech rate within 10 % with a transcript). No test uses a real speaker, and no uncertainty is reported.\n- `breathiness` cannot be fitted today: the measured `hnr` moves from 15.19 to 14.59 dB when `breathiness` goes from 0 to 1 (`experiments/issue-11-audit.txt`). #32 fixes the source.\n- `examples/universal-app/src/engine/match-worker.js` calls `matchVoiceSteps`, so its signature and result must keep working.\n- `HEAD_PARAMETERS` in `src/head-config.js` lists 33 parameters with `min`, `max` and `default`.\n\n## What to do\n\nCreate `src/analysis/voice-fit.js`. Symbols: `c` = 35000 cm/s; MAD = median of the absolute differences from the median.\n\n1. Options: `transcript` (text), `language`, `ipa` (the transcript is IPA), `refine` (default `true`), `maxRenders` (default 40), `seed` (default 1), `parts` (default `['tract', 'pitch', 'source', 'rate']`), `state` (a state returned earlier, to continue), `onStep` (called after each render).\n2. Stage A, statistics (no rendering). Run `analyzeFrames` (#58), `trackPitch` (#59), `trackFormants` (#60), `inverseFilter` (#61) and, if `src/recognition/landmarks.js` exists, `findLandmarks` (#62); otherwise keep the syllable rate of `analyzeVoice`. Throw `Error('No voiced speech found in the recording')` when fewer than 20 frames are voiced. Collect into histograms with fixed bins (this is the `state`; it is plain JSON and its size does not grow with the sound):\n   - `f0`: quarter-semitone bins from 50 to 800 Hz, voiced frames;\n   - `dF`: 5 Hz bins from 600 to 2000 Hz; one value per frame that is voiced, has F1 to F3 valid and is not `nasal`:\n\n     ```\n     dF = sum_k F[k] * (2k - 1) / 2  /  sum_k ((2k - 1) / 2)^2     (k = 1..3)\n     ```\n\n   - `rd` (bins of 0.05), `hnr` and `cpp` (bins of 0.5 dB), `h1h2Source` (bins of 0.5 dB): reliable frames of `inverseFilter`;\n   - numbers: voiced seconds, speech seconds, count of nuclei, the sum of `frames.mel` over voiced frames (24 values) and the jitter and shimmer sums of the pitch track.\n\n3. Parameters from the statistics. Each gets an object with `value`, `sd`, `source: 'statistics'` and `frames`. `sd` of a median = `1.4826 * MAD / sqrt(frames / 20)` (frames 5 ms apart are not independent; 20 frames count as one measurement):\n   - part `tract`: `vocalTractLength = c / (2 * median dF)`;\n   - part `pitch`: `pitch` = median f0; `pitchRange` = 95th minus 5th percentile in semitones, times the constant that maps it to the parameter (measure this constant once on rendered speech of the default head and keep it in the file);\n   - part `source`: `tenseness = 1 - median(rd) / 3`; `jitter` and `shimmer` through `jitterToHead`; `breathiness` from the median `hnr` through a table for `breathiness` 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1, measured once on renders of the default head and kept in the file (needs #32);\n   - part `rate`: `speechRate` = measured syllable rate divided by that of the default head on the same kind of text, measured the same way;\n   - every value is limited to `min`..`max` of `HEAD_PARAMETERS`; parameters that are not fitted keep the default and get `source: 'default'`.\n4. Stage B, refinement by analysis-by-synthesis (when `refine` is true). Text to render: the transcript, or `MATCH_TEXT` without one. Render with `synthesize(text, {head, seed, sampleRate: 16000, solver: 'waveguide'})` and, if the recording has a lower rate, resample the render to it. Feature vector `phi` of a sound, each with a scale `s_i`:\n   - `ln(median f0)` (0.03), f0 range in semitones (1.5), `ln(median dF)` (0.02), `ln` of the median F1, F2, F3 (0.05 each), median `rd` (0.3), median `h1h2Source` (2 dB), median `cpp` (1.5 dB), median `hnr` (2 dB), mean `tilt` of voiced frames (3 dB), `ln(syllable rate)` (0.08);\n   - 24 values: mean `mel` over voiced frames minus its own mean, in dB (3 dB each). Weight `w_i` = 1 for the first group; for these 24 it is 0.3 without a transcript and 1 with one.\n   - With a transcript one more term: `melCepstralDistortion` of #18 after time alignment of recording and render, scale 1 dB, weight 4.\n\n   ```\n   J(theta) = sqrt( sum_i w_i * ((phi_i(render) - phi_i(recording)) / s_i)^2\n                    / sum_i w_i )\n              + 0.05 * sum_j ((theta_j - theta0_j) / r_j)^2\n   ```\n\n   `theta` = the parameters being refined, each scaled to 0..1 by its `min` and `max`; `theta0` = the stage A values; `r_j` = 0.25.\n\n5. Search with the Nelder-Mead simplex (reflection 1, expansion 2, contraction 0.5, shrink 0.5), first vertex `theta0`, the others `theta0` with one coordinate moved by 0.1 (towards the middle of the range). A round stops when the highest and lowest `J` of the simplex differ by less than 0.01. Values outside 0..1 are moved to the edge. The same `seed` gives the same result. Two rounds, to keep the number of renders small:\n   1. the five parameters `vocalTractLength`, `pitch`, `pitchRange`, `tenseness`, `speechRate`: at most 60 % of `maxRenders`;\n   2. `breathiness`, `glottalChink`, `aspirationLevel` and, only with a transcript, `nasalCoupling`, `pharynxRatio` and `oralWidth`: the rest.\n6. After refinement `sd` = the larger of the stage A `sd` and the standard deviation of that coordinate over the final simplex; `source: 'refined'`. It is a rough indicator, not a confidence interval; the README says so.\n7. Result: an object with `head`, `parameters`, `preset`, `features`, `rendered`, `distance`, `renders`, `voicedDuration` and `state`. `head` is a full head configuration. `parameters` maps a key of `HEAD_PARAMETERS` to the object of step 3. `preset` is the nearest preset (as today). `features` and `rendered` have the keys `analyzeVoice` returns today plus `rd`, `cpp` and `h1h2Source`. `distance` = final `J` without the last term.\n8. `fitVoiceSteps` (same arguments) is a generator: it yields `{step, renders, distance, head}` after stage A and after each improvement, and returns the result.\n9. `createVoiceFitter(options)` returns an object with `update(samples, sampleRate)`, `result(options)` and `state`. `update` adds the statistics of a new stretch of sound to the histograms (stage A only, at most 30 % of real time). `result()` computes step 3 from the histograms; with `refine: true`, `samples` and `sampleRate` in its options it also runs stage B on that stretch. #78 uses this object.\n10. `matchVoice` and `matchVoiceSteps` keep their arguments. They call `fitVoice` / `fitVoiceSteps` with `maxRenders = 10 * rounds` and return the same five keys. `analyzeVoice` keeps its result keys; its values now come from stage A.\n11. If #33 is merged, its fold parameters join round 2 of step 5 in place of `tenseness`; if #41 is merged, the result can be saved as a voice file. Neither is required.\n\nBudget on the reference machine of #58: stage A at most 30 % of real time; with the default 40 renders at most 60 s for a 10 s recording.\n\n## Tests\n\nNew file `tests/voice-fit.test.js` (the existing `tests/voice-match.test.js` must pass unchanged). It returns a copy of `result` (shape of `recognize`) with `modes` and `ipa` filled in.\n\n1. Span shape, as in #70: the shape of `plan.modes` of #50 plus four keys. Example:\n\n   ```text\n   { start: 0.4, end: 1.9, from: 1, to: 5, effort: 0.75,\n     notation: 'f', confidence: 0.8 }\n   ```\n\n   `start`, `end` in seconds; `from`, `to` are indexes into `result.words` (`to` exclusive); then only the decided keys of the mode object of #50; `notation` is the brace label or `null` when IPA has none (emotion); `confidence` is 0 to 1.\n\n2. Baseline: what this speaker sounds like in a normal voice.\n   - With `options.voice` (a voice of #41 or #63): synthesise `tests/fixtures/recognition/baseline.txt` (one neutral sentence per language, write it here) with that voice at the tier that matches `sampleRate` and measure the features of step 3. Cache by voice.\n   - Without it: the median of each feature over the utterance. Then only changes inside the utterance and the signs that need no baseline (whisper, creak, falsetto) can be reported. Do not guess the rest.\n3. Features per word, from the frames of its vowels (`analyzeFrames`, `trackPitch`, `trackFormants`, `inverseFilter`, `mode-features.js`): `alpha` (alpha ratio, dB), `pitch` (median, Hz and semitones re the baseline), `f1` (mean F1 minus the baseline F1 of the same vowel, Hz; `null` without `options.voice`), `voiced` (voiced share of the vowel frames), `h1h2` (corrected for formants, dB), `hnr` (dB), `cpp` (dB), `jitter` (%), `rate` (syllables per second of the word and its two neighbours). `d` before a name below means \"minus the baseline\".\n4. Effort in decibels (inverse of `EFFORT_RULES` of #52): `Etilt = dalpha / 0.2`, `Epitch = dpitch in Hz / 5`, `Ef1 = df1 / 3.5`; `E = 0.6 * Etilt + 0.2 * Epitch + 0.2 * Ef1` (without `f1`: 0.75 and 0.25); `effort = clamp(0.5 + E / 40, 0, 1)`, rounded to the nearest of 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1. `confidence = max(0, 1 - |Etilt - Epitch| / 20)`.\n5. Label per word, first rule that fits (start values; tune with the tests):\n\n   | Rule | Keys | Label |\n   | --- | --- | --- |\n   | `voiced < 0.05` and energy ratio 6 dB above the baseline | `phonation.whisper: 1` | `W` |\n   | median pitch below 70 Hz | `phonation.creaky: 1` | `C` |\n   | `dpitch >= 10` st and `h1h2 >= 8` | `phonation.falsetto: 1` | `F` |\n   | `h1h2 < 0`, `dhnr <= -3`, `jitter >= 3` | `phonation.harsh: 1` | `V!` |\n   | `jitter >= 5`, and `h1h2 < 0` or `dpitch <= -8` st | `phonation.creaky` | `V̰` |\n   | `dh1h2 <= -3` and `dhnr >= -2` | `phonation.tension: 1` | `V͈` |\n   | `dh1h2 >= 1` and (`dcpp <= -1` or `dhnr <= -3`) | `phonation.breathy` | `V̤` |\n   | voiced, `hnr < 10`, `dhnr <= -4` | `phonation.whisper: 0.5` | `Ṿ` |\n   | `dh1h2` between 2 and 5, `dhnr` between -2 and 2 | `phonation.tension: -1` | `V͉` |\n   | `effort` of step 4 is not 0.5 and no row above fits | `effort` | `pp`, `p`, `f`, `ff` |\n   | `rate / baseline rate >= 1.2` (may be added to any row) | `rate: 1.3` | `allegro` |\n   | `rate / baseline rate <= 0.83` (may be added to any row) | `rate: 0.75` | `lento` |\n\n   Degree of breathy and creaky voice: `d = clamp(dh1h2 / 3.2, 0, 1)` (breathy) or `clamp(jitter / 5, 0, 1)` (creaky), rounded to 0.33, 0.67 or 1 and written as `{1V̤`, `{V̤`, `{3V̤`. Use the key names and signs that #54 really has; this table uses those of #50.\n\n6. From words to spans: join neighbouring words with the same label. One word between two words with the same label takes their label. A span shorter than 0.3 s is dropped, except whisper. Inside a span of 4 words or more with a label of effort, fit a line to `E` over time: a change of 8 dB or more gives `crescendo` (rising) or `diminuendo` instead.\n7. Whisper spans: use `findWhisper` of `src/recognition/whisper.js` when that file exists (#72); otherwise the first row of the table.\n8. Emotion, per phrase (words between pauses of 0.2 s or more):\n   1. Vector: pitch level (st), pitch span (95th minus 5th percentile, st), `rate` ratio, `E`, `dh1h2`, `dhnr`; each minus the baseline and divided by its scale: 2 st, 2 st, 0.15, 5 dB, 3 dB, 3 dB.\n   2. Reference vectors: on first use, synthesise the baseline sentence once per emotion name of #55 at intensity 1 with the baseline voice and measure the same vector. No trained model is used.\n   3. `activation` = mean of the first four components divided by 2, cut to -1…1. Always reported when `|activation| >= 0.3`, as `emotion: { arousal: activation }`.\n   4. Name: the nearest reference by Euclidean distance `near`; `next` is the second nearest. Report `emotion.name` only when `near <= 0.6 * (length of the vector)` and `near <= 0.8 * next`; `intensity` = length of the vector divided by the length of the reference, cut to 0…1; `confidence = 1 - near / next`.\n   5. When a name is reported, drop the effort, rate and phonation spans of that phrase which the emotion preset of #55 itself produces (same key, value within one step), so that speaking the result again does not apply them twice. `notation` is `null`.\n9. Sounds, only when #56 is merged: a noise of 0.3 to 0.7 s inside a pause is `⸨inhale⸩`; 3 or more bursts of voice at 4 to 6 per second are `⸨laugh⸩`; a steady `ə`-like vowel longer than 0.2 s next to a pause is `⸨filler⸩`. Add the token to `ipa`, and to `modes` a span `{ start, end, sound, notation, confidence }`.\n10. Write `ipa`: wrap the words of every span that has a label in `{label … label}`, with `formatIpa` of #50. Export `toPlanModes(modes)`: it returns `[{ from, to, mode }]` for `planUtterance(ipa, { modes })`, including the spans without a label.\n11. What cannot be decided is left out. Never report an emotion name, an effort or a voice quality for a phrase with fewer than 3 vowels.\n12. Wiring: if `src/recognition/recognizer.js` exists, call `recognizeModes` after the text step when the option `modes` is not `false`, and pass the option `voice` on; otherwise #73 adds the call. Steps:\n   1. `spoken = synthesize(text, { lang, tier, preset, seed })`.\n   2. `heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level })` with `level = levelForTier(tier)`. For `zh` the tokens are the characters;\n      - `toneErrors` (only `zh`): edit distance between the two lists of tones, one entry per syllable (the tone letters in the syllable's IPA, the empty string for the neutral tone);\n      - `stressHits` (only `en`, `ru`): among the reference words with two or more syllables whose recognised word has the same number of syllables, how many have `stress: 1` on the same syllable;\n      - `timeErrors`: pair the reference and recognised syllables through the edit-distance path over syllable IPA; for each pair with equal IPA collect `|start difference|` and `|end difference|` in ms;\n      - `languageRight`: `heard.languages[0].language === lang` after sorting by `share`, largest first;\n      - `sentenceMark`: the last of `. ? !` in `heard.text`, with `।`, `。`, `？`, `！` mapped to their ASCII form, or `null`.\n3. Type: **Feature**. Requirements of #11 covered: R6, R8, R9, R12, R13, R18, R19 (see the [case study](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-11/README.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\n`fitVoice(samples, sampleRate, options)` listens to a recording of one person and returns the head configuration of the simulator that sounds like that person, with an uncertainty for every fitted parameter. It works with and without the text that was spoken, on real speakers, at 8000 Hz, and it can be continued when more sound arrives. `matchVoice` stays and calls it.\n\n## Why\n\nThis is the first pass of the multi-pass algorithm of the issue: \"first try to fit best simulation settings to copy the voice\". The second pass (#65) asks which tongue positions explain the sound, and that question only has a good answer when the tube already has the length, the source and the pitch range of the speaker.\n\n## Current state\n\n- `matchVoice` and `matchVoiceSteps` in `src/analysis/voice-match.js` fit six parameters: `pitch`, `pitchRange`, `vocalTractLength`, `tenseness`, `breathiness`, `speechRate`. They render the transcript (or the fixed `MATCH_TEXT`) at 16000 Hz with `solver: 'waveguide'`, `seed: 1`, compare the features of `analyzeVoice`, and correct each parameter by a secant step; 4 rounds by default, at most 12. The result is `{head, preset, features, rendered, distance}`.\n- The features are utterance statistics (`f0`, `f0Range`, mean `formants`, `h1h2`, `hnr`, `syllableRate`) from frames that are each decided alone.\n- `tests/voice-match.test.js` uses only synthetic recordings (pitch, tract length and speech rate within 10 % with a transcript). No test uses a real speaker, and no uncertainty is reported.\n- `breathiness` cannot be fitted today: the measured `hnr` moves from 15.19 to 14.59 dB when `breathiness` goes from 0 to 1 (`experiments/issue-11-audit.txt`). #32 fixes the source.\n- `examples/universal-app/src/engine/match-worker.js` calls `matchVoiceSteps`, so its signature and result must keep working.\n- `HEAD_PARAMETERS` in `src/head-config.js` lists 33 parameters with `min`, `max` and `default`.\n\n## What to do\n\nCreate `src/analysis/voice-fit.js`. Symbols: `c` = 35000 cm/s; MAD = median of the absolute differences from the median.\n\n1. Options: `transcript` (text), `language`, `ipa` (the transcript is IPA), `refine` (default `true`), `maxRenders` (default 40), `seed` (default 1), `parts` (default `['tract', 'pitch', 'source', 'rate']`), `state` (a state returned earlier, to continue), `onStep` (called after each render).\n2. Stage A, statistics (no rendering). Run `analyzeFrames` (#58), `trackPitch` (#59), `trackFormants` (#60), `inverseFilter` (#61) and, if `src/recognition/landmarks.js` exists, `findLandmarks` (#62); otherwise keep the syllable rate of `analyzeVoice`. Throw `Error('No voiced speech found in the recording')` when fewer than 20 frames are voiced. Collect into histograms with fixed bins (this is the `state`; it is plain JSON and its size does not grow with the sound):\n   - `f0`: quarter-semitone bins from 50 to 800 Hz, voiced frames;\n   - `dF`: 5 Hz bins from 600 to 2000 Hz; one value per frame that is voiced, has F1 to F3 valid and is not `nasal`:\n\n     ```\n     dF = sum_k F[k] * (2k - 1) / 2  /  sum_k ((2k - 1) / 2)^2     (k = 1..3)\n     ```\n\n   - `rd` (bins of 0.05), `hnr` and `cpp` (bins of 0.5 dB), `h1h2Source` (bins of 0.5 dB): reliable frames of `inverseFilter`;\n   - numbers: voiced seconds, speech seconds, count of nuclei, the sum of `frames.mel` over voiced frames (24 values) and the jitter and shimmer sums of the pitch track.\n\n3. Parameters from the statistics. Each gets an object with `value`, `sd`, `source: 'statistics'` and `frames`. `sd` of a median = `1.4826 * MAD / sqrt(frames / 20)` (frames 5 ms apart are not independent; 20 frames count as one measurement):\n   - part `tract`: `vocalTractLength = c / (2 * median dF)`;\n   - part `pitch`: `pitch` = median f0; `pitchRange` = 95th minus 5th percentile in semitones, times the constant that maps it to the parameter (measure this constant once on rendered speech of the default head and keep it in the file);\n   - part `source`: `tenseness = 1 - median(rd) / 3`; `jitter` and `shimmer` through `jitterToHead`; `breathiness` from the median `hnr` through a table for `breathiness` 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1, measured once on renders of the default head and kept in the file (needs #32);\n   - part `rate`: `speechRate` = measured syllable rate divided by that of the default head on the same kind of text, measured the same way;\n   - every value is limited to `min`..`max` of `HEAD_PARAMETERS`; parameters that are not fitted keep the default and get `source: 'default'`.\n4. Stage B, refinement by analysis-by-synthesis (when `refine` is true). Text to render: the transcript, or `MATCH_TEXT` without one. Render with `synthesize(text, {head, seed, sampleRate: 16000, solver: 'waveguide'})` and, if the recording has a lower rate, resample the render to it. Feature vector `phi` of a sound, each with a scale `s_i`:\n   - `ln(median f0)` (0.03), f0 range in semitones (1.5), `ln(median dF)` (0.02), `ln` of the median F1, F2, F3 (0.05 each), median `rd` (0.3), median `h1h2Source` (2 dB), median `cpp` (1.5 dB), median `hnr` (2 dB), mean `tilt` of voiced frames (3 dB), `ln(syllable rate)` (0.08);\n   - 24 values: mean `mel` over voiced frames minus its own mean, in dB (3 dB each). Weight `w_i` = 1 for the first group; for these 24 it is 0.3 without a transcript and 1 with one.\n   - With a transcript one more term: `melCepstralDistortion` of #18 after time alignment of recording and render, scale 1 dB, weight 4.\n\n   ```\n   J(theta) = sqrt( sum_i w_i * ((phi_i(render) - phi_i(recording)) / s_i)^2\n                    / sum_i w_i )\n              + 0.05 * sum_j ((theta_j - theta0_j) / r_j)^2\n   ```\n\n   `theta` = the parameters being refined, each scaled to 0..1 by its `min` and `max`; `theta0` = the stage A values; `r_j` = 0.25.\n\n5. Search with the Nelder-Mead simplex (reflection 1, expansion 2, contraction 0.5, shrink 0.5), first vertex `theta0`, the others `theta0` with one coordinate moved by 0.1 (towards the middle of the range). A round stops when the highest and lowest `J` of the simplex differ by less than 0.01. Values outside 0..1 are moved to the edge. The same `seed` gives the same result. Two rounds, to keep the number of renders small:\n   1. the five parameters `vocalTractLength`, `pitch`, `pitchRange`, `tenseness`, `speechRate`: at most 60 % of `maxRenders`;\n   2. `breathiness`, `glottalChink`, `aspirationLevel` and, only with a transcript, `nasalCoupling`, `pharynxRatio` and `oralWidth`: the rest.\n6. After refinement `sd` = the larger of the stage A `sd` and the standard deviation of that coordinate over the final simplex; `source: 'refined'`. It is a rough indicator, not a confidence interval; the README says so.\n7. Result: an object with `head`, `parameters`, `preset`, `features`, `rendered`, `distance`, `renders`, `voicedDuration` and `state`. `head` is a full head configuration. `parameters` maps a key of `HEAD_PARAMETERS` to the object of step 3. `preset` is the nearest preset (as today). `features` and `rendered` have the keys `analyzeVoice` returns today plus `rd`, `cpp` and `h1h2Source`. `distance` = final `J` without the last term.\n8. `fitVoiceSteps` (same arguments) is a generator: it yields `{step, renders, distance, head}` after stage A and after each improvement, and returns the result.\n9. `createVoiceFitter(options)` returns an object with `update(samples, sampleRate)`, `result(options)` and `state`. `update` adds the statistics of a new stretch of sound to the histograms (stage A only, at most 30 % of real time). `result()` computes step 3 from the histograms; with `refine: true`, `samples` and `sampleRate` in its options it also runs stage B on that stretch. #78 uses this object.\n10. `matchVoice` and `matchVoiceSteps` keep their arguments. They call `fitVoice` / `fitVoiceSteps` with `maxRenders = 10 * rounds` and return the same five keys. `analyzeVoice` keeps its result keys; its values now come from stage A.\n11. If #33 is merged, its fold parameters join round 2 of step 5 in place of `tenseness`; if #41 is merged, the result can be saved as a voice file. Neither is required.\n\nBudget on the reference machine of #58: stage A at most 30 % of real time; with the default 40 renders at most 60 s for a 10 s recording.\n\n## Tests\n\nNew file `tests/voice-fit.test.js` (the existing `tests/voice-match.test.js` must pass unchanged). Renders are slow, so the unit tests use two heads, one sentence of about 2.5 s (\"The north wind and the sun.\") and `maxRenders: 10`. Head A: `vocalTractLength` 14, `pitch` 210, `tenseness` 0.45, `speechRate` 1.15. Head B: 18.5, 100, 0.75, 0.9.\n\n- `recovers synthetic voices with a transcript`: at 16000 Hz: tract length within 6 %, pitch 3 %, speech rate 10 %, tenseness within 0.2.\n- `recovers synthetic voices without a transcript`: `refine: false`: tract length within 8 %, pitch within 3 %.\n- `works at 8000 Hz`: head A, `refine: false`: tract length within 10 %.\n- `reports uncertainty`: every fitted parameter has a finite `sd` above 0; `sd` of `pitch` is below 5 Hz; the others have `source: 'default'`.\n- `continues from a state`: two halves through `createVoiceFitter` give the stage A values of the whole recording within 2 %.\n- `is deterministic`: two calls give equal results.\n- `keeps matchVoice working`: the result has exactly the five old keys.\n\nHeavy test `tests/heavy/copy-voice-fit.test.js` (#14), 40 renders each:\n\n- 20 heads from seeds 1 to 20 with `vocalTractLength` 12 to 19 cm, `pitch` 90 to 260 Hz, `tenseness` 0.3 to 0.9, `speechRate` 0.8 to 1.25, `breathiness` 0.1 to 0.9, each speaking a 5 s sentence. Gates on the median error: tract length 4 % (6 % without transcript; no single error above 10 %), pitch 2 %, speech rate 8 %, tenseness 0.15, breathiness 0.2. For at least 16 of the 20 heads the true tract length lies within `value +- 3 * sd`.\n- Every speaker of the golden set (#17), with and without transcript: the fitted values with `sd`, the final `distance`, that of the nearest preset, and the mel-cepstral distortion of both renders.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `node --test tests/voice-fit.test.js tests/voice-match.test.js` passes on Node.js, Bun and Deno.\n- [ ] `npm run test:heavy -- --suite copy` passes the gates on the 20 heads.\n- [ ] `reports/heavy/copy-voice-fit.md` exists. Steps:\n   1. `spoken = synthesize(text, { lang, tier, preset, seed })`.\n   2. `heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level })` with `level = levelForTier(tier)`. The second pass (#65) asks which tongue positions explain the sound, and that question only has a good answer when the tube already has the length, the source and the pitch range of the speaker.\n\n## Current state\n\n- `matchVoice` and `matchVoiceSteps` in `src/analysis/voice-match.js` fit six parameters: `pitch`, `pitchRange`, `vocalTractLength`, `tenseness`, `breathiness`, `speechRate`. They render the transcript (or the fixed `MATCH_TEXT`) at 16000 Hz with `solver: 'waveguide'`, `seed: 1`, compare the features of `analyzeVoice`, and correct each parameter by a secant step; 4 rounds by default, at most 12. The result is `{head, preset, features, rendered, distance}`.\n- The features are utterance statistics (`f0`, `f0Range`, mean `formants`, `h1h2`, `hnr`, `syllableRate`) from frames that are each decided alone.\n- `tests/voice-match.test.js` uses only synthetic recordings (pitch, tract length and speech rate within 10 % with a transcript). Symbols: `c` = 35000 cm/s; MAD = median of the absolute differences from the median.\n\n1. Options: `transcript` (text), `language`, `ipa` (the transcript is IPA), `refine` (default `true`), `maxRenders` (default 40), `seed` (default 1), `parts` (default `['tract', 'pitch', 'source', 'rate']`), `state` (a state returned earlier, to continue), `onStep` (called after each render).\n2. Stage A, statistics (no rendering). Run `analyzeFrames` (#58), `trackPitch` (#59), `trackFormants` (#60), `inverseFilter` (#61) and, if `src/recognition/landmarks.js` exists, `findLandmarks` (#62); otherwise keep the syllable rate of `analyzeVoice`. Throw `Error('No voiced speech found in the recording')` when fewer than 20 frames are voiced. Collect into histograms with fixed bins (this is the `state`; it is plain JSON and its size does not grow with the sound):\n   - `f0`: quarter-semitone bins from 50 to 800 Hz, voiced frames;\n   - `dF`: 5 Hz bins from 600 to 2000 Hz; one value per frame that is voiced, has F1 to F3 valid and is not `nasal`:\n\n     ```\n     dF = sum_k F[k] * (2k - 1) / 2  /  sum_k ((2k - 1) / 2)^2     (k = 1..3)\n     ```\n\n   - `rd` (bins of 0.05), `hnr` and `cpp` (bins of 0.5 dB), `h1h2Source` (bins of 0.5 dB): reliable frames of `inverseFilter`;\n   - numbers: voiced seconds, speech seconds, count of nuclei, the sum of `frames.mel` over voiced frames (24 values) and the jitter and shimmer sums of the pitch track.\n\n3. Parameters from the statistics. Each gets an object with `value`, `sd`, `source: 'statistics'` and `frames`. `sd` of a median = `1.4826 * MAD / sqrt(frames / 20)` (frames 5 ms apart are not independent; 20 frames count as one measurement):\n   - part `tract`: `vocalTractLength = c / (2 * median dF)`;\n   - part `pitch`: `pitch` = median f0; `pitchRange` = 95th minus 5th percentile in semitones, times the constant that maps it to the parameter (measure this constant once on rendered speech of the default head and keep it in the file);\n   - part `source`: `tenseness = 1 - median(rd) / 3`; `jitter` and `shimmer` through `jitterToHead`; `breathiness` from the median `hnr` through a table for `breathiness` 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1, measured once on renders of the default head and kept in the file (needs #32);\n   - part `rate`: `speechRate` = measured syllable rate divided by that of the default head on the same kind of text, measured the same way;\n   - every value is limited to `min`..`max` of `HEAD_PARAMETERS`; parameters that are not fitted keep the default and get `source: 'default'`.\n4. Stage B, refinement by analysis-by-synthesis (when `refine` is true). Text to render: the transcript, or `MATCH_TEXT` without one. Render with `synthesize(text, {head, seed, sampleRate: 16000, solver: 'waveguide'})` and, if the recording has a lower rate, resample the render to it. Feature vector `phi` of a sound, each with a scale `s_i`:\n   - `ln(median f0)` (0.03), f0 range in semitones (1.5), `ln(median dF)` (0.02), `ln` of the median F1, F2, F3 (0.05 each), median `rd` (0.3), median `h1h2Source` (2 dB), median `cpp` (1.5 dB), median `hnr` (2 dB), mean `tilt` of voiced frames (3 dB), `ln(syllable rate)` (0.08);\n   - 24 values: mean `mel` over voiced frames minus its own mean, in dB (3 dB each). Weight `w_i` = 1 for the first group; for these 24 it is 0.3 without a transcript and 1 with one.\n   - With a transcript one more term: `melCepstralDistortion` of #18 after time alignment of recording and render, scale 1 dB, weight 4.\n\n   ```\n   J(theta) = sqrt( sum_i w_i * ((phi_i(render) - phi_i(recording)) / s_i)^2\n                    / sum_i w_i )\n              + 0.05 * sum_j ((theta_j - theta0_j) / r_j)^2\n   ```\n\n   `theta` = the parameters being refined, each scaled to 0..1 by its `min` and `max`; `theta0` = the stage A values; `r_j` = 0.25.\n\n5. Search with the Nelder-Mead simplex (reflection 1, expansion 2, contraction 0.5, shrink 0.5), first vertex `theta0`, the others `theta0` with one coordinate moved by 0.1 (towards the middle of the range). A round stops when the highest and lowest `J` of the simplex differ by less than 0.01. Values outside 0..1 are moved to the edge. The same `seed` gives the same result. Two rounds, to keep the number of renders small:\n   1. the five parameters `vocalTractLength`, `pitch`, `pitchRange`, `tenseness`, `speechRate`: at most 60 % of `maxRenders`;\n   2. `breathiness`, `glottalChink`, `aspirationLevel` and, only with a transcript, `nasalCoupling`, `pharynxRatio` and `oralWidth`: the rest.\n6. After refinement `sd` = the larger of the stage A `sd` and the standard deviation of that coordinate over the final simplex; `source: 'refined'`. It is a rough indicator, not a confidence interval; the README says so.\n7. Result: an object with `head`, `parameters`, `preset`, `features`, `rendered`, `distance`, `renders`, `voicedDuration` and `state`. `head` is a full head configuration. `parameters` maps a key of `HEAD_PARAMETERS` to the object of step 3. `preset` is the nearest preset (as today). `features` and `rendered` have the keys `analyzeVoice` returns today plus `rd`, `cpp` and `h1h2Source`. `distance` = final `J` without the last term.\n8. `fitVoiceSteps` (same arguments) is a generator: it yields `{step, renders, distance, head}` after stage A and after each improvement, and returns the result.\n9. `createVoiceFitter(options)` returns an object with `update(samples, sampleRate)`, `result(options)` and `state`. `update` adds the statistics of a new stretch of sound to the histograms (stage A only, at most 30 % of real time). `result()` computes step 3 from the histograms; with `refine: true`, `samples` and `sampleRate` in its options it also runs stage B on that stretch. #78 uses this object.\n10. `matchVoice` and `matchVoiceSteps` keep their arguments. They call `fitVoice` / `fitVoiceSteps` with `maxRenders = 10 * rounds` and return the same five keys. `analyzeVoice` keeps its result keys; its values now come from stage A.\n11. If #33 is merged, its fold parameters join round 2 of step 5 in place of `tenseness`; if #41 is merged, the result can be saved as a voice file. Neither is required.\n\nBudget on the reference machine of #58: stage A at most 30 % of real time; with the default 40 renders at most 60 s for a 10 s recording.\n\n## Tests\n\nNew file `tests/voice-fit.test.js` (the existing `tests/voice-match.test.js` must pass unchanged). Renders are slow, so the unit tests use two heads, one sentence of about 2.5 s (\"The north wind and the sun.\") and `maxRenders: 10`. Head A: `vocalTractLength` 14, `pitch` 210, `tenseness` 0.45, `speechRate` 1.15. Head B: 18.5, 100, 0.75, 0.9.\n\n- `recovers synthetic voices with a transcript`: at 16000 Hz: tract length within 6 %, pitch 3 %, speech rate 10 %, tenseness within 0.2.\n- `recovers synthetic voices without a transcript`: `refine: false`: tract length within 8 %, pitch within 3 %.\n- `works at 8000 Hz`: head A, `refine: false`: tract length within 10 %.\n- `reports uncertainty`: every fitted parameter has a finite `sd` above 0; `sd` of `pitch` is below 5 Hz; the others have `source: 'default'`.\n- `continues from a state`: two halves through `createVoiceFitter` give the stage A values of the whole recording within 2 %.\n- `is deterministic`: two calls give equal results.\n- `keeps matchVoice working`: the result has exactly the five old keys.\n\nHeavy test `tests/heavy/copy-voice-fit.test.js` (#14), 40 renders each:\n\n- 20 heads from seeds 1 to 20 with `vocalTractLength` 12 to 19 cm, `pitch` 90 to 260 Hz, `tenseness` 0.3 to 0.9, `speechRate` 0.8 to 1.25, `breathiness` 0.1 to 0.9, each speaking a 5 s sentence. Gates on the median error: tract length 4 % (6 % without transcript; no single error above 10 %), pitch 2 %, speech rate 8 %, tenseness 0.15, breathiness 0.2. For at least 16 of the 20 heads the true tract length lies within `value +- 3 * sd`.\n- Every speaker of the golden set (#17), with and without transcript: the fitted values with `sd`, the final `distance`, that of the nearest preset, and the mel-cepstral distortion of both renders.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `node --test tests/voice-fit.test.js tests/voice-match.test.js` passes on Node.js, Bun and Deno.\n- [ ] `npm run test:heavy -- --suite copy` passes the gates on the 20 heads.\n- [ ] `reports/heavy/copy-voice-fit.md` exists. Gate: for every golden speaker the final `distance` is not above that of the nearest preset. Targets to be measured, not gates yet: it is at most half of it for 80 % of the speakers, and the mel-cepstral distortion is at least 0.5 dB better than with the nearest preset.\n- [ ] The report gives the fitted `vocalTractLength` per speaker next to `speaker.sex` of the manifest (plausible: women 14-15 cm, men 16-18 cm).\n- [ ] The example app still matches a voice (its tests pass).\n- [ ] `fitVoice`, `fitVoiceSteps` and `createVoiceFitter` are exported and typed; README section \"Voice matching\" describes the new result.\n- [ ] `npm run check` and `npm test` pass; a minor changeset is added.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Tongue positions over time: #65. Type: **Feature**. Requirements of #11 covered: R6, R7, R11, R13, R18 (see the [case study](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-11/README.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\nA fixed list of 80 sentences (20 each for English, Russian, Hindi and Mandarin) is spoken by the simulator and recognised by `recognize`. The suite `roundtrip` of the heavy workflow measures how much of the text, the IPA, the syllable times and the language comes back, per audio tier and per preset voice, fails when a threshold is missed, and writes `docs/reports/roundtrip.md`. Three sentences run in every `npm test`.\n\n## Why\n\nRecognition is the simulation in reverse, so the simulator's own speech is the one input for which the right answer is known exactly: text, IPA and the time of every syllable. This is the regression baseline for every later change of the recogniser, and the proof that both directions work at 8000 Hz.\n\n## Current state\n\n- `synthesize(text, options)` returns an object with the keys `lang`, `accent`, `ipa`, `words`, `head`, `plan`, `timeline`, `sampleRate`, `samples` and `duration`. `timeline.words[].syllables[]` holds `ipa`, `stress`, `start`, `end` (seconds) and `text`.\n- Measured on this branch: the three smoke sentences below take 0.11 to 0.27 s each to synthesise at tier `minimal` (22050 Hz, 1.9 to 2.3 s of audio).\n- The 80 sentences were checked with the current text-to-IPA code. They give about 214 s of speech and contain 40 different phone symbols in English, 47 in Russian, 50 in Hindi and 40 in Mandarin, all four Mandarin tones, the half-third tone and the neutral tone, and statements, yes/no questions, question-word questions, exclamations and one-word sentences in each language. There are no digits and no erhua (see #46 and #43).\n- `HEAD_PRESET_NAMES` is `['any', 'male', 'female', 'child']`. Tiers today: `minimal`, `low`, `medium` (waveguide), `high`, `ultra`, `studio`, `reference` (3D). #26 adds `telephone`, `narrowband` and `wideband`.\n- There is no recogniser, so no round-trip test exists: `ls tests/heavy` and `grep -rn roundtrip tests` find nothing.\n\n## What to do\n\n1. Create `tests/helpers/roundtrip.js` exporting `roundTrip(text, options)` with `options = { lang, tier, preset, seed }`. Steps:\n   1. `spoken = synthesize(text, { lang, tier, preset, seed })`.\n   2. `heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level })` with `level = levelForTier(tier)`. Do not pass the language: it must be found.\n   3. Return `{ spoken, heard, seconds }` plus these numbers, computed with `errorRate` and `editDistance` of #18:\n      - `per`: `errorRate(spoken.ipa, heard.ipa, 'phone')`;\n      - `wer` (not for `zh`) and `cer`: `errorRate(text, heard.text, unit)` with `'word'` and `'char'`;\n      - `soundWer`: the same as `wer`, but each word of both texts is first replaced by its IPA from `textToIpa(...).words[].ipa`, so that a word which sounds the same (`sea` and `see`, 他 and 她) is not an error. For `zh` the tokens are the characters;\n      - `toneErrors` (only `zh`): edit distance between the two lists of tones, one entry per syllable (the tone letters in the syllable's IPA, the empty string for the neutral tone);\n      - `stressHits` (only `en`, `ru`): among the reference words with two or more syllables whose recognised word has the same number of syllables, how many have `stress: 1` on the same syllable;\n      - `timeErrors`: pair the reference and recognised syllables through the edit-distance path over syllable IPA; for each pair with equal IPA collect `|start difference|` and `|end difference|` in ms;\n      - `languageRight`: `heard.languages[0].language === lang` after sorting by `share`, largest first;\n      - `sentenceMark`: the last of `. ? !` in `heard.text`, with `।`, `。`, `？`, `！` mapped to their ASCII form, or `null`.\n3. Create `tests/heavy/roundtrip-sentences.test.js`. Seed 1 everywhere. Runs:\n   - set `main`: all 80 sentences, tiers `telephone`, `narrowband`, `wideband`, `minimal`, presets `male` and `female` (640 runs);\n   - set `voices`: sentences 1 to 5 of each language, presets `any` and `child`, tiers `telephone` and `wideband` (80 runs);\n   - set `tiers`: sentences 2 and 20 of each language, preset `male`, tiers `low`, `medium`, `high`, `ultra`, `studio` (40 runs). `reference` is left out because of its run time; say so in the report.\n   - `heavyLimit(80)` limits the number of sentences per set.\n   - Sum the edit distances and the reference lengths per language, tier and set before dividing; do not average the rates of single sentences.\n4. Gates (one `it` per row, so that a failure names the row). They hold for every language of set `main`:\n\n   | Tier | PER | soundWer | Tone errors | Syllable time, mean | Language right |\n   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n   | `wideband`, `minimal` | ≤ 5 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 30 ms | ≥ 95 % |\n   | `narrowband` | ≤ 8 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 12 % | ≤ 35 ms | ≥ 92 % |\n   | `telephone` | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 20 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 40 ms | ≥ 90 % |\n\n   Set `voices`: the gates of row `telephone` for every preset. Set `tiers`: PER ≤ 10 % per tier. Stress hits ≥ 90 % (`en`, `ru`) from `narrowband` up. `wer`, `cer`, `sentenceMark` and the real-time factor of `recognize` (`seconds` divided by audio seconds) are reported without a gate; the sentence mark gets its gate in #70.\n\n5. If the first full run misses a gate, do not loosen it. Read the report (it lists the 20 worst sentences with reference and recognised IPA), fix the stage that loses most, and run again. The gates are the result this issue must deliver.\n6. Mode check, only when `parseMarkup` of #50 is exported (else the test is skipped with the reason in its name): speak sentence 1 of each language once whispered and once loud with the markup of #50; report the share of mode spans that come back in `heard.modes` with the same notation and at least 50 % overlap in time. This issue sets no gate of its own for modes: the numbers belong to #70 (sentence mark), #71 (mode labels) and #72 (set `whisper`). Each of them adds its gate to this test when this test exists. For each of the three that is merged already while its gate is missing here, add the gate in this issue with the numbers of that issue's acceptance criteria.\n7. Write the report with `writeReport('roundtrip', markdown, data)`: one table per set (rows: language × tier; columns: the numbers above), then the 20 worst sentences. Copy the report of the full run to `docs/reports/roundtrip.md` and commit it with the run link, the commit hash and the date at the top.\n8. Smoke test `tests/roundtrip-smoke.test.js` (part of `npm test`): sentence 18 of `en`, 2 of `ru` and 2 of `zh`; tier `telephone`, preset `male`, seed 1. Expect `per.rate \u003c= 0.1`, `soundWer.rate === 0` and `languageRight`.\n9. Add the suite and the report to `tests/heavy/README.md` and to `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` (section \"Heavy checks\").\n\n## Tests\n\n- `tests/roundtrip-smoke.test.js`: the three `it` blocks of step 8, named `round trip en`, `round trip ru`, `round trip zh`.\n- `tests/roundtrip-helper.test.js` (fast, stub recogniser passed as `options.recognize`): `counts a homophone as right` (`sea` heard as `see` gives `wer.distance === 1` and `soundWer.distance === 0`); `counts tones` (one wrong tone letter gives `toneErrors.distance === 1`); `measures syllable times` (a result shifted by 20 ms gives a mean of 20 ms).\n- `has 20 sentences per language`: `sentences.json` has four keys with 20 non-empty strings each and no digit.\n- `tests/heavy/roundtrip-sentences.test.js` as described above.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `node --test tests/roundtrip-smoke.test.js` passes in less than 30 s on one core.\n- [ ] `npm run test:heavy -- --suite roundtrip --limit 2` passes locally and writes `reports/heavy/roundtrip.md`.\n- [ ] A run of `Heavy checks` with `suite=roundtrip` on the pull request branch is green: every gate of step 4 holds.
