Contributing to js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template\n\n## Development Workflow\n\nUse Node.js 24 with npm 10.9 or newer for development and release tooling.\nChangesets 3 requires a supported Node.js 22.11, 24, or 26+ runtime.\n\n1. **Fork the repository** and clone your fork\n2. **Create a feature branch**: `git checkout -b feature/my-feature`\n3. **Install dependencies**: `bun install` (or `npm install`)\n4. **Make your changes**\n5. **Run local checks**: `bun run check`\n6. **Create a changeset**: `bun run changeset`\n7. **Commit and push** (pre-commit hooks will run automatically)\n8. **Create a Pull Request**\n\n## Code Standards\n\n### File Size Limits\n\n**Maximum 1500 lines per file** (enforced via ESLint `max-lines` rule and CI `check-file-line-limits` job).\n\nThis benefits both AI and human developers by ensuring files remain readable and maintainable.\n\n### Formatting and Linting\n\nAll code must pass:\n\n```bash\n# Check formatting\nbun run format:check\n\n# Check linting\nbun run lint\n\n# Run all checks\nbun run check\n```\n\nThe pre-commit hook runs automatically, but you can also manually format and fix:\n\n```bash\n# Auto-fix formatting\nbun run format\n\n# Auto-fix lint issues\nbun run lint:fix\n```\n\n### Testing Requirements\n\nTests should:\n\n- Cover critical paths\n- Work across all runtimes (Node.js, Bun, Deno)\n- Use the [test-anywhere](https://github.com/link-foundation/test-anywhere) framework\n\n```bash\n# Run tests\nbun test --timeout 30000\nnpm test\ndeno test -A --parallel\n```\n\nTests that need more than about 10 seconds or a download do not belong in\n`tests/*.test.js`; put them into `tests/heavy/` (see \"Heavy checks\" below).\n\n### Heavy checks\n\nSlow tests (full 3D renders, quality reports against recordings, recognition\nof datasets, round trips, voice copying) live in `tests/heavy/` and are named\n`<suite>-<topic>.test.js`, where the suite is `quality`, `recognition`,\n`roundtrip`, `copy`, `performance`, `gpu` or `lexicon`. `npm test`, `bun test` and\n`deno test` never run them; [tests/heavy/README.md](../tests/heavy/README.md)\ndescribes the folder and its helpers.\n\nThey run in the workflow `Heavy checks`\n([.github/workflows/heavy.yml](../.github/workflows/heavy.yml)), which is only\nstarted by hand:\n\n- in the **Actions** tab: choose **Heavy checks**, then **Run workflow**, pick\n  the branch, the suite, optionally a `ref` (a branch or tag of this\n  repository, or a commit already on `main` or on the branch picked; empty\n  means the branch picked)\n  and a `limit` (largest number of items, such as utterances or files, that\n  each test may process; empty means no limit);\n- from the command line:\n\n  ```bash\n  gh workflow run heavy.yml -f suite=quality -f limit=5\n  # on another branch\n  gh workflow run heavy.yml --ref my-branch -f suite=performance\n  ```\n\nA run started on `main` writes to the cache scope of `main`, so\n[scripts/resolve-heavy-ref.sh](../scripts/resolve-heavy-ref.sh) refuses a\n`ref` that names anything else, such as a commit of a fork; to test a pull\nrequest from a fork, start the workflow on its branch after pushing that\nbranch here.\n\nThe run summary shows one row per test file with its result and wall time,\nfollowed by the reports the tests wrote; the reports are also uploaded as the\nartifact `heavy-<suite>-<run id>` and kept for 30 days. The step has a budget\nof 300 minutes (see [CI-TIMEOUT-BUDGETS.md](CI-TIMEOUT-BUDGETS.md)).\n\nLocally:\n\n```bash\nnpm run test:heavy -- --suite performance\nnpm run test:heavy -- --suite performance --limit 2 --out /tmp/heavy\n```\n\nReports go to `reports/heavy/` (`--out` changes the folder): every test writes\n`<name>.md` and `<name>.json`, and the runner writes `summary.md`. `reports/`\nis never committed. A report that should be kept is copied to `docs/reports/`\nby the issue that owns it.\n\n#### Round-trip recognition\n\nRun `npm run test:heavy -- --suite roundtrip` to measure synthetic speech\nrecognition on a fixed corpus of 80 sentences in English, Russian, Hindi and\nMandarin. The suite tests four presets across nine tiers and reports phone and\ntext errors, lexical tone and stress, syllable timing, language, punctuation,\nspeech modes and recognition speed. For a shorter run, append `--limit 2` to\ncap each language's sentence sample before testing its tiers and presets.\nThe full run produces the [round-trip report](reports/roundtrip.md).\n\n#### Performance tracking\n\n`tests/heavy/performance-tiers.test.js` (issue 31) times every audio tier\nexcept `reference` on the JavaScript and the Rust engine, on one core, and\nwrites `performance-tiers.json`. In CI, or locally with\n`PERFORMANCE_COMPARE=1`, its test `speed rules hold` compares the run with\n[docs/reports/performance-baseline.json](reports/performance-baseline.json)\nthrough [scripts/performance.mjs](../scripts/performance.mjs): a row more than\nthe tolerance (2.0, from the spread of five CI runs) slower than its baseline\nrow (scaled by a calibration loop, so a slower runner is forgiven), a missing\nrow, a Rust row slower than its\nJavaScript row, or a waveguide tier above half of real time fails the run. The\nsame script compares any two reports by hand:\n\n```bash\nnode scripts/performance.mjs compare reports/heavy/performance-tiers.json\nnode scripts/performance.mjs compare new.json --baseline old.json --tolerance 2\n```\n\nThe calibration loop does not follow every machine: a busy developer machine\nrenders slower than its calibration says, so a local comparison with the CI\nbaseline can fail with no change of code. Compare with a baseline of your own\nmachine instead:\n\n```bash\nnode scripts/performance.mjs baseline reports/heavy/performance-tiers.json --dir /tmp/mine\nPERFORMANCE_COMPARE=1 PERFORMANCE_BASELINE=/tmp/mine/performance-baseline.json \\\n  npm run test:heavy -- --suite performance\n```\n\nThe workflow never commits; the files in `docs/reports/` change only in a pull\nrequest, from the artifact of a green run of suite `performance`:\n\n- **Trend.** Every pull request that changes `src/acoustics/`, `src/engine/`\n  or `crates/`, and every minor release, adds its row to\n  [docs/reports/performance.md](reports/performance.md):\n  `node scripts/performance.mjs trend performance-tiers.json` (a second run of\n  the same commit replaces the first).\n- **Baseline.** Replace the baseline only for a wanted change of speed, and\n  give the reason in the pull request:\n  `node scripts/performance.mjs baseline performance-tiers.json`. A row with\n  the status `faster` is the hint that the baseline is out of date.\n\n#### Suite `gpu`\n\nThe files `gpu-*.test.js` run the WebGPU 3D solver, which Node.js and Bun\nlack, so the runner gives them, together with `tests/fdtd-gpu.test.js`, to\n`deno test -A --config deno.heavy.json` after the Node.js files. The suite\nneeds Deno on `PATH`; without it their rows in `summary.md` say\n`skipped (no Deno)`. `deno.heavy.json` has its own import of `test-anywhere`\nand `\"lock\": false`: Deno finds `package.json` only next to `deno.json`, and\nthe lock it would write for this config would replace `deno.lock`.\n\n`REQUIRE_GPU=1` turns a missing adapter into a failure:\n`tests/helpers/gpu.js` throws\n`REQUIRE_GPU=1 but this runtime has no WebGPU adapter` and the runner exits\nwith 1 and prints `suite gpu needs Deno on PATH` when Deno is missing. The\nworkflow sets it for the suites `gpu` and `all`.\n\nOn Linux without a GPU, Deno's WebGPU falls back to Mesa's software OpenGL ES\ndriver; install it with\n\n```bash\nsudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libegl1 libgles2 libegl-mesa0 libgl1-mesa-dri\ndeno run -A scripts/gpu-adapter.mjs   # prints the adapter, or null\nREQUIRE_GPU=1 npm run test:heavy -- --suite gpu\n```\n\nEvery GPU test prints its adapter (`WebGPU adapter: {...}`) and the report\n`gpu-solver.md` names it. A software adapter says nothing about GPU speed.\n\n### Recognition benchmark\n\nRun a short sample locally or dispatch the full recognition suite on one\nGitHub Actions runner core:\n\n```bash\nnode scripts/run-heavy.mjs --suite recognition --limit 5\ngh workflow run heavy.yml -f suite=recognition\n```\n\nThe benchmark uses the first rows of each set in\n[datasets/benchmark.json](../datasets/benchmark.json). Keep fetched audio and\ntranscripts in `.datasets/`. Only the aggregate Markdown report and a JSON\nreport with aggregate counts and rates and per-row IDs and counts go into the\nworkflow artifact. Use the default prefixes for comparisons against the\ncommitted baseline. The recognition workflow has a 90-minute test budget.\n\nTo set or update the baseline, run the full suite on comparable single-core\nhardware:\n\n```bash\nHEAVY_UPDATE_BASELINE=1 node scripts/run-heavy.mjs --suite recognition\n```\n\nOnce all benchmark corpora are measured and pass the floors, this writes\n`tests/heavy/baselines/recognition.json` and\n`docs/reports/recognition-benchmark.md`. Review and commit both files. 'medium' : settings.level;\n  return serial(job.samples, job.sampleRate, settings, level);\n}\n\nexport function recognize(samples, sampleRate, options = {}) {\n  if (options.threads === 'auto' || options.threads > 1) {\n    return recognizeAsync(samples, sampleRate, options);\n  }\n  checkAudio(samples, sampleRate);\n  const settings = recognitionSettings(options);\n  const level = settings.level === 'auto' ? 'medium' : settings.level;\n  const jobs = options.unsplit\n    ? []\n    : pieces(samples, sampleRate, options, settings);\n  return jobs.length\n    ? merge(\n        jobs.map((job) => runPiece(job, settings.kernels)),\n        jobs,\n        settings\n      )\n    : serial(samples, sampleRate, settings, level);\n}\n\nasync function parallelDecode(samples, sampleRate, settings, level, pool) {\n  const { input, rate, options } = decodeInput(\n    samples,\n    sampleRate,\n    settings,\n    level\n  );\n  let decoded = await audioToIpaParallel(\n    input,\n    rate,\n    { ...options, sourceRate: sampleRate, lattice: settings.rescoring },\n    pool\n  );\n  checkNoise(decoded, samples.length / sampleRate);\n  if (settings.rescoring && decoded.ipa) {\n    const preparation = planRescoring(decoded);\n    const scores = await pool.run('rescore', preparation.jobs, scoreJob);\n    decoded = applyRescoring(decoded, preparation, scores, RESCORING_WEIGHT);\n  }\n  return recognizeDecoded(decoded, input, rate, settings, level, 'parallel');\n}\n\nexport async function recognizeAsync(samples, sampleRate, options = {}) {\n  checkAudio(samples, sampleRate);\n  const kernels = options.kernels ?? (await createRecognitionEngine(options));\n  const settings = recognitionSettings({ ...options, kernels });\n  const level = settings.level === 'auto' ? 'medium' : settings.level;\n  const pool = createRecognitionPool({\n    threads: kernels.threads,\n    engine: kernels.name,\n  });\n  try {\n    const workerOptions = { ...options, unsplit: true };\n    delete workerOptions.kernels;\n    const jobs = pieces(samples, sampleRate, workerOptions, settings);\n    if (jobs.length) {\n      const lexicons = pool.size > 1 ? registeredLexicons() : [];\n      const results = await pool.run(\n        'audio',\n        jobs,\n        (job) => runPiece(job, kernels),\n        lexicons.length ? { lexicons } : undefined\n      );\n      return merge(results, jobs, settings);\n    }\n    if (\n      pool.size === 1 ||\n      Object.keys(settings.stages).length ||\n      settings.profile\n    ) {\n      return serial(samples, sampleRate, settings, level);\n    }\n    return await parallelDecode(samples, sampleRate, settings, level, pool);\n  } finally {\n    await pool.close();\n  }\n}\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

At the values the planner writes they give the shape of the vowel and consonant channels; moved, they widen the mouth (`JAW_AREA` = 0.8 per cm, 9 % more F1 of `[ɛ]` for 0.5 cm; time constant 0.02 s, so that a short `[z]` still reaches its gap), lengthen the lips or the pharynx (`stretchSections()`, the velum, the teeth and the noise source keep their distance from the lips) and scale the pharynx ([experiments/issue-40-articulators.txt](../experiments/issue-40-articulators.txt)). In the 3D solver the voxel tract goes on below the glottis by `LARYNX_TRAVEL` = 0.25 of its length and the source plane moves in whole cells with the tract length, so the time step stretches by at most half a cell: `[u]` and `[æ]` differ by 3.6 % in step, 10.8 % before ([experiments/issue-40-fdtd3d.txt](../experiments/issue-40-fdtd3d.txt)). The ratio of nasal to vowel of `[ˈama]` becomes 0.99 and 1.08 at 1 and 0.6 cm cells, against 0.87 and 1.19 before, closer to the 1.09 of the waveguide ([experiments/issue-40-ama-3d.txt](../experiments/issue-40-ama-3d.txt)). `matchVoice` reads the tract length from F1 to F3, which rises with the length where the reading with F4 reverses ([experiments/issue-40-length-feature.txt](../experiments/issue-40-length-feature.txt)). capacity : Math.min(capacity, settings.lag + 1);\n  const path = new Int8Array(capacity).fill(-1);\n  const search =\n    book &&\n    createTractSearch(frames, formants, book, settings, steps, {\n      candidates: track.candidates,\n      history,\n      head,\n      query: options.query,\n    });\n  const smoother = createTractSmoother(track, book, steps, path);\n  const source = createSourceEstimator(frames, pitch, track, batch);\n  const start = frames.startTime;\n\n  function commit(last, end) {\n    const first = track.committed;\n    if (last <= first) {\n      return;\n    }\n    search.trace(first, end, path);\n    smoother.smooth(first, last, end);\n    for (let t = first; t < last; t++) {\n      if (path[t] >= 0) {\n        track.confidence[t] = Math.exp(\n          -track.candidates.cost[t * width + path[t]] / 8\n        );\n      }\n    }\n    source(first, last, end);\n    track.committed = last;\n  }\n\n  const score = createScorer(frames, search, (end) => {\n    if (!batch) {\n      commit(end - settings.lag, end);\n    }\n  });\n\n  return {\n    frames,\n    output: track,\n    track,\n    advance(final = false) {\n      if (start !== frames.startTime || frames.count < track.frameCount) {\n        throw new RangeError(\n          'Create a new inverter after trimming or resetting the frame set'\n        );\n      }\n      advance(final);\n      const end = Math.min(frames.count, pitch.committed, formants.committed);\n      if (final && end !== frames.count) {\n        throw new RangeError(\n          'Final pitch and formant tracks must cover all inversion frames'\n        );\n      }\n      track.frameCount = score(end, final);\n      track.duration = final\n        ? frames.sampleCount / frames.rate\n        : track.frameCount * frames.hop;\n      if (final) {\n        commit(end, end);\n      }\n    },\n    refine() {\n      refineArticulation(frames, track, book, steps, smoother);\n      smoother.smooth(0, track.frameCount, track.frameCount);\n    },\n  };\n}\n\nexport function createArticulationInverter(frames, options = {}) {\n  const {\n    frames: input,\n    track,\n    advance,\n  } = createInverter(frames, options, false);\n  return { frames: input, track, output: track, advance };\n}\n\nfunction renderError(frames, track) {\n  const sampleRate = frames.rate;\n  const rendered = renderPlan(articulationPlan(track), {\n    sampleRate,\n    solver: 'waveguide',\n    engine: 'js',\n    seed: 1,\n  });\n  const observed = frames.samples.subarray(0, frames.sampleCount);\n  return melCepstralDistortion(observed, rendered, sampleRate);\n}\n\nexport function invertArticulation(frames, options = {}) {\n  const inverter = createInverter(frames, options, true);\n  inverter.advance(true);\n  const { track } = inverter;\n  if (options.refine && track.confidence.some((value) => value > 0)) {\n    const baselineError = renderError(frames, track);\n    const copyTract = (arrays) =>\n      Object.fromEntries(\n        CODEBOOK_CHANNELS.map(({ name }) => [name, arrays[name].slice()])\n      );\n    const unrefined = copyTract(track.channels);\n    const unrefinedVariance = copyTract(track.variance);\n    inverter.refine();\n    // The oral objective omits the noisy source and radiation detail of\n    // the renderer. Keep the refinement only if the render-back improves.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Features per word, from the frames of its vowels (`analyzeFrames`, `trackPitch`, `trackFormants`, `inverseFilter`, `mode-features.js`): `alpha` (alpha ratio, dB), `pitch` (median, Hz and semitones re the baseline), `f1` (mean F1 minus the baseline F1 of the same vowel, Hz; `null` without `options.voice`), `voiced` (voiced share of the vowel frames), `h1h2` (corrected for formants, dB), `hnr` (dB), `cpp` (dB), `jitter` (%), `rate` (syllables per second of the word and its two neighbours). `d` before a name below means \"minus the baseline\".\n4. Effort in decibels (inverse of `EFFORT_RULES` of #52): `Etilt = dalpha / 0.2`, `Epitch = dpitch in Hz / 5`, `Ef1 = df1 / 3.5`; `E = 0.6 * Etilt + 0.2 * Epitch + 0.2 * Ef1` (without `f1`: 0.75 and 0.25); `effort = clamp(0.5 + E / 40, 0, 1)`, rounded to the nearest of 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1. `confidence = max(0, 1 - |Etilt - Epitch| / 20)`.\n5. Label per word, first rule that fits (start values; tune with the tests):\n\n   | Rule | Keys | Label |\n   | --- | --- | --- |\n   | `voiced < 0.05` and energy ratio 6 dB above the baseline | `phonation.whisper: 1` | `W` |\n   | median pitch below 70 Hz | `phonation.creaky: 1` | `C` |\n   | `dpitch >= 10` st and `h1h2 >= 8` | `phonation.falsetto: 1` | `F` |\n   | `h1h2 < 0`, `dhnr <= -3`, `jitter >= 3` | `phonation.harsh: 1` | `V!` |\n   | `jitter >= 5`, and `h1h2 < 0` or `dpitch <= -8` st | `phonation.creaky` | `V̰` |\n   | `dh1h2 <= -3` and `dhnr >= -2` | `phonation.tension: 1` | `V͈` |\n   | `dh1h2 >= 1` and (`dcpp <= -1` or `dhnr <= -3`) | `phonation.breathy` | `V̤` |\n   | voiced, `hnr < 10`, `dhnr <= -4` | `phonation.whisper: 0.5` | `Ṿ` |\n   | `dh1h2` between 2 and 5, `dhnr` between -2 and 2 | `phonation.tension: -1` | `V͉` |\n   | `effort` of step 4 is not 0.5 and no row above fits | `effort` | `pp`, `p`, `f`, `ff` |\n   | `rate / baseline rate >= 1.2` (may be added to any row) | `rate: 1.3` | `allegro` |\n   | `rate / baseline rate <= 0.83` (may be added to any row) | `rate: 0.75` | `lento` |\n\n   Degree of breathy and creaky voice: `d = clamp(dh1h2 / 3.2, 0, 1)` (breathy) or `clamp(jitter / 5, 0, 1)` (creaky), rounded to 0.33, 0.67 or 1 and written as `{1V̤`, `{V̤`, `{3V̤`. Use the key names and signs that #54 really has; this table uses those of #50.\n\n6. From words to spans: join neighbouring words with the same label. One word between two words with the same label takes their label. A span shorter than 0.3 s is dropped, except whisper. Inside a span of 4 words or more with a label of effort, fit a line to `E` over time: a change of 8 dB or more gives `crescendo` (rising) or `diminuendo` instead.\n7. Whisper spans: use `findWhisper` of `src/recognition/whisper.js` when that file exists (#72); otherwise the first row of the table.\n8. Emotion, per phrase (words between pauses of 0.2 s or more):\n   1. Vector: pitch level (st), pitch span (95th minus 5th percentile, st), `rate` ratio, `E`, `dh1h2`, `dhnr`; each minus the baseline and divided by its scale: 2 st, 2 st, 0.15, 5 dB, 3 dB, 3 dB.\n   2. Reference vectors: on first use, synthesise the baseline sentence once per emotion name of #55 at intensity 1 with the baseline voice and measure the same vector. No trained model is used.\n   3. `activation` = mean of the first four components divided by 2, cut to -1…1. Always reported when `|activation| >= 0.3`, as `emotion: { arousal: activation }`.\n   4. Name: the nearest reference by Euclidean distance `near`; `next` is the second nearest. Report `emotion.name` only when `near <= 0.6 * (length of the vector)` and `near <= 0.8 * next`; `intensity` = length of the vector divided by the length of the reference, cut to 0…1; `confidence = 1 - near / next`.\n   5. When a name is reported, drop the effort, rate and phonation spans of that phrase which the emotion preset of #55 itself produces (same key, value within one step), so that speaking the result again does not apply them twice. `notation` is `null`.\n9. Sounds, only when #56 is merged: a noise of 0.3 to 0.7 s inside a pause is `⸨inhale⸩`; 3 or more bursts of voice at 4 to 6 per second are `⸨laugh⸩`; a steady `ə`-like vowel longer than 0.2 s next to a pause is `⸨filler⸩`. Add the token to `ipa`, and to `modes` a span `{ start, end, sound, notation, confidence }`.\n10. Write `ipa`: wrap the words of every span that has a label in `{label … label}`, with `formatIpa` of #50. Export `toPlanModes(modes)`: it returns `[{ from, to, mode }]` for `planUtterance(ipa, { modes })`, including the spans without a label.\n11. What cannot be decided is left out. The suite `roundtrip` of the heavy workflow measures how much of the text, the IPA, the syllable times and the language comes back, per audio tier and per preset voice, fails when a threshold is missed, and writes `docs/reports/roundtrip.md`. Three sentences run in every `npm test`.\n\n## Why\n\nRecognition is the simulation in reverse, so the simulator's own speech is the one input for which the right answer is known exactly: text, IPA and the time of every syllable. This is the regression baseline for every later change of the recogniser, and the proof that both directions work at 8000 Hz.\n\n## Current state\n\n- `synthesize(text, options)` returns an object with the keys `lang`, `accent`, `ipa`, `words`, `head`, `plan`, `timeline`, `sampleRate`, `samples` and `duration`. `timeline.words[].syllables[]` holds `ipa`, `stress`, `start`, `end` (seconds) and `text`.\n- Measured on this branch: the three smoke sentences below take 0.11 to 0.27 s each to synthesise at tier `minimal` (22050 Hz, 1.9 to 2.3 s of audio).\n- The 80 sentences were checked with the current text-to-IPA code. They give about 214 s of speech and contain 40 different phone symbols in English, 47 in Russian, 50 in Hindi and 40 in Mandarin, all four Mandarin tones, the half-third tone and the neutral tone, and statements, yes/no questions, question-word questions, exclamations and one-word sentences in each language. There are no digits and no erhua (see #46 and #43).\n- `HEAD_PRESET_NAMES` is `['any', 'male', 'female', 'child']`. Create `tests/helpers/roundtrip.js` exporting `roundTrip(text, options)` with `options = { lang, tier, preset, seed }`. Steps:\n   1. `spoken = synthesize(text, { lang, tier, preset, seed })`.\n   2. `heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level })` with `level = levelForTier(tier)`. Do not pass the language: it must be found.\n   3. Return `{ spoken, heard, seconds }` plus these numbers, computed with `errorRate` and `editDistance` of #18:\n      - `per`: `errorRate(spoken.ipa, heard.ipa, 'phone')`;\n      - `wer` (not for `zh`) and `cer`: `errorRate(text, heard.text, unit)` with `'word'` and `'char'`;\n      - `soundWer`: the same as `wer`, but each word of both texts is first replaced by its IPA from `textToIpa(...).words[].ipa`, so that a word which sounds the same (`sea` and `see`, 他 and 她) is not an error. For `zh` the tokens are the characters;\n      - `toneErrors` (only `zh`): edit distance between the two lists of tones, one entry per syllable (the tone letters in the syllable's IPA, the empty string for the neutral tone);\n      - `stressHits` (only `en`, `ru`): among the reference words with two or more syllables whose recognised word has the same number of syllables, how many have `stress: 1` on the same syllable;\n      - `timeErrors`: pair the reference and recognised syllables through the edit-distance path over syllable IPA; for each pair with equal IPA collect `|start difference|` and `|end difference|` in ms;\n      - `languageRight`: `heard.languages[0].language === lang` after sorting by `share`, largest first;\n      - `sentenceMark`: the last of `. ? !` in `heard.text`, with `।`, `。`, `？`, `！` mapped to their ASCII form, or `null`.\n3. Features per word, from the frames of its vowels (`analyzeFrames`, `trackPitch`, `trackFormants`, `inverseFilter`, `mode-features.js`): `alpha` (alpha ratio, dB), `pitch` (median, Hz and semitones re the baseline), `f1` (mean F1 minus the baseline F1 of the same vowel, Hz; `null` without `options.voice`), `voiced` (voiced share of the vowel frames), `h1h2` (corrected for formants, dB), `hnr` (dB), `cpp` (dB), `jitter` (%), `rate` (syllables per second of the word and its two neighbours). `d` before a name below means \"minus the baseline\".\n4. Effort in decibels (inverse of `EFFORT_RULES` of #52): `Etilt = dalpha / 0.2`, `Epitch = dpitch in Hz / 5`, `Ef1 = df1 / 3.5`; `E = 0.6 * Etilt + 0.2 * Epitch + 0.2 * Ef1` (without `f1`: 0.75 and 0.25); `effort = clamp(0.5 + E / 40, 0, 1)`, rounded to the nearest of 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1. `confidence = max(0, 1 - |Etilt - Epitch| / 20)`.\n5. One word between two words with the same label takes their label. A span shorter than 0.3 s is dropped, except whisper. Inside a span of 4 words or more with a label of effort, fit a line to `E` over time: a change of 8 dB or more gives `crescendo` (rising) or `diminuendo` instead.\n7. [2026-11-22T11:38:46.545Z] [STDERR] ## Abstract
[2026-11-22T11:38:46.549Z] [STDERR] We introduce a novel mechanism for incorporating articulatory dynamics into speech recognition with the theory of task dynamics. This system reranks sentence-level hypotheses by the likelihoods of their hypothetical articulatory realizations which are derived from relationships learned with aligned acoustic/articulatory data. Experiments compare this with two baseline systems, namely an acoustic hidden Markov model and a dynamic Bayes network augmented with discretized representations of the vocal tract. Our system based on task dynamics reduces word-error rates significantly by 10.2% relative to the best baseline models.

[2026-11-22T11:52:35.846Z] [STDERR]  `copyRecording(samples, sampleRate, options)` analyzes mono speech and synthesizes a copy from its recognized phonemes, timing, pitch, loudness, and measured voice modes. It returns the audio, a voice file, the editable score, the recognition result, and acoustic metrics. Pass `voice` or `--voice voice.json` to reuse a fitted voice. Choose a synthesis tier with `tier` or `--tier`. Set one of `impose.durations`, `impose.pitch`, `impose.loudness`, or `impose.modes` to `false` to use the corresponding synthesis defaults. Optional `refine: true` or `--refine` searches for a closer articulation. The JavaScript option `refineBudget` limits its draft renders and defaults to 200.

The copy path estimates a preset from pitch, proposes readings from the pronunciation dictionary, and accepts the synthesis plan only when the newly rendered waveform closely agrees with the input. Other recordings use the voice fitting and recognition path.

Options and defaults: `tier` (as `synthesize`), `seed` (1), `languages` (all), `voice` (skip the fit and use this voice), `impose` (`{ durations: true, pitch: true, loudness: true, modes: true }`), `refine` (`false`), `refineBudget` (200 renders). Returns `{ samples, sampleRate, duration, score, voice, recognition, metrics }`.\n2. Analysis. Call `copyVoice` of #78 (with `options.voice`: only its recogniser). Keep the voice, the `recognize` result and its `modes` (#70, #71). Phoneme times are needed, and the result of `recognize` (#73) has only words and syllables. Add the option `segments` (boolean, default `false`) to `recognize` and `createRecognizer`. With `true` the result gets one extra key, `segments: [{ ipa, start, end, confidence }]` (one entry per phoneme, from `audioToIpa` of #66), in the same way as `nbest` adds `alternatives`. Without the option the result keeps exactly its six keys, so the tests of #73 stay as they are. Document the option in `src/index.d.ts` and in the README section on recognition. `copyVoice` passes `segments: true`.\n3. Plan. `planUtterance(recognition.ipa, { head, language })` with the copied voice, `vibrato: 0` (the measured contour already holds it) and the language with the largest share.\n4. Durations (`warp.js`, `warpPlan(plan, measuredSegments)`). Group the plan segments by IPA token. Build a piecewise linear map from recording time to plan time with one anchor at the start and end of every token; silence between recognised words maps to the pause of the plan, or to a new silent stretch when the plan has none. Make new channels of `ceil(duration * frameRate) + 1` frames and fill each frame by linear interpolation of the plan at the mapped time. Inside a stop keep the release (`kind: 'release'`) at its planned length and stretch the closure. Clamp the stretch of one token to 0.33-3 times and list clamped tokens in `metrics.warnings`. Update `segments[].start` and `.end`.\n5. Pitch. Take f0 from `trackPitch` (#59), resample to the frame rate. Octave check: a frame more than 9 semitones from the median of the voiced frames within ±100 ms is moved by one octave when that brings it within 3 semitones, else it is marked as a gap. Median filter over 5 frames, fill gaps with `interpolateGaps`, smooth with `smoothChannel` (10 ms), write to `channels.f0`. Skip spans that the modes mark as whisper.\n6. Loudness. Level `L(t)` = RMS in dB over 25 ms windows every 5 ms. Render a draft with the `waveguide` solver at 16 kHz. Multiply `channels.loudness` by `10 ** (0.8 * (L_recording - L_draft) / 20)`, factor clamped to 0.25-4, only where both levels are above −40 dB of their maximum. Do this twice. First add a test that doubling `loudness` raises a vowel by 6 ± 1 dB; if it does not, use the measured exponent instead of 20.\n7. Modes. Copy the recognised spans to `plan.modes` (#50) unchanged.\n8. Refinement, only with `refine: true`. Cost = `logSpectralDistance` (#18, dB) between the recording and a waveguide draft at 16 kHz, plus `4 * sum(offset ** 2)` so that gestures stay plausible. For each syllable: (a) blend the channels `height`, `backness`, `rounding` towards the trajectory of `invertArticulation` (#65) with weight 0, 0.5 or 1, keep the best; (b) try offsets of ±0.05 on each of the three channels at the nucleus, keep a change that lowers the cost by 0.05 dB or more; two rounds. Stop after `refineBudget` renders. Cut utterances longer than 5 s at pauses and refine each piece.\n9. Render with `renderPlan` at the requested tier and seed. Pad or trim to the length of the input at the output sample rate.\n10. Score (`score.js`). `toScore(plan, recognition, voice)` returns\n\n    ```json\n    {\n      \"format\": \"voice-simulator/score\",\n      \"version\": 1,\n      \"duration\": 3.42,\n      \"voice\": {},\n      \"words\": [],\n      \"segments\": [{ \"ipa\": \"h\", \"start\": 0.12, \"end\": 0.18 }],\n      \"f0\": { \"rate\": 200, \"values\": [0, 118.2] },\n      \"loudness\": { \"rate\": 200, \"values\": [0, 0.7] },\n      \"modes\": []\n    }\n    ```\n\n    `f0` is in Hz with 0 for unvoiced frames; `words` has the shape of `recognize`. `renderScore(score, options)` rebuilds the plan from a score (steps 3 to 7 with the score as the measurement) and renders it, so an edited IPA symbol, time or pitch value gives new audio.\n\n11. Metrics. `metrics` = `compareRecordings(original, copy)` of #18 plus `timingError` (mean absolute difference in ms between the syllable starts of the score and those found by recognising the copy).\n12. It prints the recognised text and the metrics (`--json` for JSON). Add the line \"Copy only your own voice, a voice you have permission to copy, or a public-domain recording.\" to `--help` and to a README section \"Copying a voice\" that links to \"Not goals\" in `docs/VISION.md`.\n13. Listening tests. Add two test definitions in the format of #20 under `examples/listening-test/`: `copy-abx` (A = original, B = copy, X = one of them, 10 golden recordings) and `copy-similarity` (MUSHRA scale \"same speaker?\": hidden reference = another utterance of the speaker; the copy; the copy rendered with the default voice; another real speaker as low anchor). `scripts/make-copy-stimuli.mjs` writes the stimuli to `reports/copy-stimuli/`. Running them with people is #83.\n14. Heavy suite `copy` and report `docs/reports/copy-synthesis.md` written by `scripts/copy-report.mjs`: one row per golden recording and tier (`medium` and the default tier) with every metric. Store thresholds in `tests/heavy/copy-thresholds.json`; set the cepstral distortion limit to the first measured mean times 1.05. Later pull requests may only lower the numbers in that file.\n\n## Tests\n\n`tests/copy.test.js` (fast, tier `minimal`, 16 kHz):\n\n- `keeps measured durations`: `warpPlan` on the plan of `ˈmama` with every token made 1.5 times longer gives segments 1.5 times longer (±1 frame).\n- `imposes the measured pitch`: a rising 100-150 Hz contour is found again in the copy by `f0Errors` with RMSE below 0.3 semitones.\n- `repairs an octave jump`: 5 frames at double pitch are moved back.\n- `round-trips a score`: `renderScore(toScore(...))` gives the same samples as the copy; raising every `f0` value by 2 semitones raises the measured median pitch by 2 ± 0.2 semitones.\n- `copies a synthetic original`: \"Hello world.\" rendered with preset `female`; phoneme error rate 0, f0 RMSE ≤ 0.3 semitones, `timingError` ≤ 10 ms.\n- `cli copy writes audio and a score`: runs the command on a temporary WAV.\n\n`tests/heavy/copy-golden.test.js` (suite `copy` of #14):\n\n- `copies the golden set`: for every recording, f0 RMSE ≤ 1 semitone on frames voiced in both, voicing error ≤ 10 %, `timingError` ≤ 20 ms, mel cepstral distortion ≤ the value in `copy-thresholds.json`.\n- `refinement helps`: with `refine: true` the mean log-spectral distance is lower than without it on at least 80 % of the recordings.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `node bin/voice-simulator.js copy in.wav -o out.wav --score s.json` writes both files; `--from-score s.json` renders the same samples.\n- [ ] `node --test tests/copy.test.js` passes on Node.js, Bun and Deno.\n- [ ] Heavy suite `copy` passes with the thresholds above and `docs/reports/copy-synthesis.md` is committed with the measured numbers, the commit and the command.\n- [ ] `copyRecording`, `renderScore` and `toScore` are exported and typed.\n- [ ] The two listening-test definitions load in the harness of #20.\n- [ ] The consent sentence is in `--help` and in the README.\n- [ ] `npm run check` and `npm test` pass; a minor changeset is added.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Fitting the voice and recognising: #78. Create `tests/helpers/roundtrip.js` exporting `roundTrip(text, options)` with `options = { lang, tier, preset, seed }`. Steps:\n   1. `spoken = synthesize(text, { lang, tier, preset, seed })`.\n   2. `heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level })` with `level = levelForTier(tier)`. Do not pass the language: it must be found.\n   3. Return `{ spoken, heard, seconds }` plus these numbers, computed with `errorRate` and `editDistance` of #18:\n      - `per`: `errorRate(spoken.ipa, heard.ipa, 'phone')`;\n      - `wer` (not for `zh`) and `cer`: `errorRate(text, heard.text, unit)` with `'word'` and `'char'`;\n      - `soundWer`: the same as `wer`, but each word of both texts is first replaced by its IPA from `textToIpa(...).words[].ipa`, so that a word which sounds the same (`sea` and `see`, 他 and 她) is not an error. For `zh` the tokens are the characters;\n      - `toneErrors` (only `zh`): edit distance between the two lists of tones, one entry per syllable (the tone letters in the syllable's IPA, the empty string for the neutral tone);\n      - `stressHits` (only `en`, `ru`): among the reference words with two or more syllables whose recognised word has the same number of syllables, how many have `stress: 1` on the same syllable;\n      - `timeErrors`: pair the reference and recognised syllables through the edit-distance path over syllable IPA; for each pair with equal IPA collect `|start difference|` and `|end difference|` in ms;\n      - `languageRight`: `heard.languages[0].language === lang` after sorting by `share`, largest first;\n      - `sentenceMark`: the last of `. ? !` in `heard.text`, with `।`, `。`, `？`, `！` mapped to their ASCII form, or `null`.\n3. Create `tests/heavy/roundtrip-sentences.test.js`. Seed 1 everywhere. The answer is a list of spans in `result.modes` and the same ExtIPA/VoQS brace marks in `result.ipa` that the synthesiser reads (`{f … f}`, `{W … W}`, `{V̤ … V̤}`), so that speaking the result again gives the same manner of speech.\n\n## Why\n\nThe issue asks for volume, whisper, emotions and \"all common modes of speech\" for input as well as output. #52 to #55 make the synthesiser speak these modes; each of them lists the measurable signs of its mode. Example:\n\n   ```text\n   { start: 0.4, end: 1.9, from: 1, to: 5, effort: 0.75,\n     notation: 'f', confidence: 0.8 }\n   ```\n\n   `start`, `end` in seconds; `from`, `to` are indexes into `result.words` (`to` exclusive); then only the decided keys of the mode object of #50; `notation` is the brace label or `null` when IPA has none (emotion); `confidence` is 0 to 1.\n\n2. Cache by voice.\n   - Without it: the median of each feature over the utterance. Then only changes inside the utterance and the signs that need no baseline (whisper, creak, falsetto) can be reported. Do not guess the rest.\n3. Features per word, from the frames of its vowels (`analyzeFrames`, `trackPitch`, `trackFormants`, `inverseFilter`, `mode-features.js`): `alpha` (alpha ratio, dB), `pitch` (median, Hz and semitones re the baseline), `f1` (mean F1 minus the baseline F1 of the same vowel, Hz; `null` without `options.voice`), `voiced` (voiced share of the vowel frames), `h1h2` (corrected for formants, dB), `hnr` (dB), `cpp` (dB), `jitter` (%), `rate` (syllables per second of the word and its two neighbours). `d` before a name below means \"minus the baseline\".\n4. Effort in decibels (inverse of `EFFORT_RULES` of #52): `Etilt = dalpha / 0.2`, `Epitch = dpitch in Hz / 5`, `Ef1 = df1 / 3.5`; `E = 0.6 * Etilt + 0.2 * Epitch + 0.2 * Ef1` (without `f1`: 0.75 and 0.25); `effort = clamp(0.5 + E / 40, 0, 1)`, rounded to the nearest of 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1. `confidence = max(0, 1 - |Etilt - Epitch| / 20)`.\n5. Use the key names and signs that #54 really has; this table uses those of #50.\n\n6. From words to spans: join neighbouring words with the same label. One word between two words with the same label takes their label. A span shorter than 0.3 s is dropped, except whisper. Inside a span of 4 words or more with a label of effort, fit a line to `E` over time: a change of 8 dB or more gives `crescendo` (rising) or `diminuendo` instead.\n7. Whisper spans: use `findWhisper` of `src/recognition/whisper.js` when that file exists (#72); otherwise the first row of the table.\n8. Emotion, per phrase (words between pauses of 0.2 s or more):\n   1. Reference vectors: on first use, synthesise the baseline sentence once per emotion name of #55 at intensity 1 with the baseline voice and measure the same vector. No trained model is used.\n   3. `activation` = mean of the first four components divided by 2, cut to -1…1. Always reported when `|activation| >= 0.3`, as `emotion: { arousal: activation }`.\n   4. Name: the nearest reference by Euclidean distance `near`; `next` is the second nearest. Report `emotion.name` only when `near <= 0.6 * (length of the vector)` and `near <= 0.8 * next`; `intensity` = length of the vector divided by the length of the reference, cut to 0…1; `confidence = 1 - near / next`.\n   5. When a name is reported, drop the effort, rate and phonation spans of that phrase which the emotion preset of #55 itself produces (same key, value within one step), so that speaking the result again does not apply them twice. `notation` is `null`.\n9. Sounds, only when #56 is merged: a noise of 0.3 to 0.7 s inside a pause is `⸨inhale⸩`; 3 or more bursts of voice at 4 to 6 per second are `⸨laugh⸩`; a steady `ə`-like vowel longer than 0.2 s next to a pause is `⸨filler⸩`. Add the token to `ipa`, and to `modes` a span `{ start, end, sound, notation, confidence }`.\n10. Write `ipa`: wrap the words of every span that has a label in `{label … label}`, with `formatIpa` of #50. Export `toPlanModes(modes)`: it returns `[{ from, to, mode }]` for `planUtterance(ipa, { modes })`, including the spans without a label.\n11. What cannot be decided is left out. Unlicense. */\nimport { CHANNELS } from '../articulation/plan.js';\nimport { CODEBOOK_CHANNELS, frameEnvelope } from './codebook.js';\nimport { L0 } from './codebook-features.js';\nimport { whisperCodebook } from './whisper-codebook.js';\n\nexport const TRACT_WIDTH = CODEBOOK_CHANNELS.length;\nexport const CLOSURE_CANDIDATES = 32;\n\nexport function tractSteps(voice, frameRate) {\n  return Float64Array.from(\n    CODEBOOK_CHANNELS,\n    ({ name, min, max }) =>\n      -0.5 *\n      (max - min) *\n      Math.expm1(-voice.articulationSpeed / (CHANNELS[name] * frameRate))\n  );\n}\n\nfunction transitionWeights(steps, smoothness) {\n  return Float64Array.from(steps, (step, i) => {\n    const { min, max } = CODEBOOK_CHANNELS[i];\n    return smoothness * ((max - min) / (255 * step)) ** 2;\n  });\n}\n\n/** Squared distance in units of one planner step, on the quantized grid. */\nfunction movement(a, b, table, weights) {\n  let sum = 0;\n  a *= TRACT_WIDTH;\n  b *= TRACT_WIDTH;\n  for (let c = 0; c < TRACT_WIDTH; c++) {\n    const delta = table[a + c] - table[b + c];\n    sum += delta * delta * weights[c];\n  }\n  return sum;\n}\n\nfunction isClosure(table, row) {\n  const i = row * TRACT_WIDTH;\n  const lip = table[i + 5] > 127 && (table[i + 6] * 2) / 255 < 0.05;\n  const tongue = table[i + 7] > 127 && (table[i + 8] * 2) / 255 < 0.05;\n  return lip || tongue;\n}\n\nfunction closureSeeds(book) {\n  const { neutral, vowel, nasalVowel, consonant } = book.stats.rows;\n  const end = neutral + vowel + nasalVowel + consonant;\n  const seeds = [];\n  for (let row = 0; k < 3; k++) {\n    const i = t * 4 + k;\n    const reference = referenceScale * book.formants[row * 8 + k];\n    if (formants.valid[i] && reference > 0) {\n      const delta = scale * formants.frequency[i] - reference;\n      const variance =\n        scale * scale * formants.variance[i] + (0.03 * reference) ** 2;\n      cost += (delta * delta) / variance;\n    }\n  }\n  return weight * cost;\n}\n\nfunction scoreSpeech(\n  t,\n  { frames, formants, book, k, scratch, candidates, query }\n) {\n  const { width, count, index, cost } = candidates;\n  if (query) {\n    query(t, scratch.query);\n  } else {\n    frameEnvelope(frames, t, book, scratch);\n    book.query(scratch.envelope, k, scratch.query);\n  }\n  const start = t * width;\n  let best = -1;\n  for (let j = 0; count[t - 1] : 0;\n      const start = t * width;\n      const slot = (t % history) * width;\n      let best = -1;\n      for (let j = 0; j < count[t]; j++) {\n        let predecessor = -1;\n        let lowest = Infinity;\n        for (let i = 0; i < older; i++) {\n          const score =\n            previous[i] +\n            movement(\n              index[start - width + i],\n              index[start + j],\n              table,\n              weights\n            );\n          if (score < lowest) {\n            lowest = score;\n            predecessor = i;\n          }\n        }\n        back[slot + j] = predecessor;\n        current[j] = cost[start + j] + (predecessor < 0 ? 0 : lowest);\n        if (best < 0 || current[j] < current[best]) {\n          best = j;\n        }\n      }\n      winner[t % history] = best;\n      const baseline = current[best];\n      for (let j = 0; j < count[t]; j++) {\n        current[j] -= baseline;\n      }\n      [previous, current] = [current, previous];\n    },\n    trace(first, end, path) {\n      let j = -1;\n      for (let t = end - 1; t >= first; t--) {\n        const slot = t % history;\n        j = j < 0 ? Requirements of #11 covered: R6, R7, R11, R13, R18 (see the [case study](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-11/README.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\nA fixed list of 80 sentences (20 each for English, Russian, Hindi and Mandarin) is spoken by the simulator and recognised by `recognize`. The suite `roundtrip` of the heavy workflow measures how much of the text, the IPA, the syllable times and the language comes back, per audio tier and per preset voice, fails when a threshold is missed, and writes `docs/reports/roundtrip.md`. Three sentences run in every `npm test`.\n\n## Why\n\nRecognition is the simulation in reverse, so the simulator's own speech is the one input for which the right answer is known exactly: text, IPA and the time of every syllable. This is the regression baseline for every later change of the recogniser, and the proof that both directions work at 8000 Hz.\n\n## Current state\n\n- `synthesize(text, options)` returns an object with the keys `lang`, `accent`, `ipa`, `words`, `head`, `plan`, `timeline`, `sampleRate`, `samples` and `duration`. `timeline.words[].syllables[]` holds `ipa`, `stress`, `start`, `end` (seconds) and `text`.\n- Measured on this branch: the three smoke sentences below take 0.11 to 0.27 s each to synthesise at tier `minimal` (22050 Hz, 1.9 to 2.3 s of audio).\n- The 80 sentences were checked with the current text-to-IPA code. They give about 214 s of speech and contain 40 different phone symbols in English, 47 in Russian, 50 in Hindi and 40 in Mandarin, all four Mandarin tones, the half-third tone and the neutral tone, and statements, yes/no questions, question-word questions, exclamations and one-word sentences in each language. There are no digits and no erhua (see #46 and #43).\n- `HEAD_PRESET_NAMES` is `['any', 'male', 'female', 'child']`. Tiers today: `minimal`, `low`, `medium` (waveguide), `high`, `ultra`, `studio`, `reference` (3D). #26 adds `telephone`, `narrowband` and `wideband`.\n- There is no recogniser, so no round-trip test exists: `ls tests/heavy` and `grep -rn roundtrip tests` find nothing.\n\n## What to do\n\n1. Create `tests/helpers/roundtrip.js` exporting `roundTrip(text, options)` with `options = { lang, tier, preset, seed }`. Steps:\n   1. `spoken = synthesize(text, { lang, tier, preset, seed })`.\n   2. `heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level })` with `level = levelForTier(tier)`. Do not pass the language: it must be found.\n   3. Return `{ spoken, heard, seconds }` plus these numbers, computed with `errorRate` and `editDistance` of #18:\n      - `per`: `errorRate(spoken.ipa, heard.ipa, 'phone')`;\n      - `wer` (not for `zh`) and `cer`: `errorRate(text, heard.text, unit)` with `'word'` and `'char'`;\n      - `soundWer`: the same as `wer`, but each word of both texts is first replaced by its IPA from `textToIpa(...).words[].ipa`, so that a word which sounds the same (`sea` and `see`, 他 and 她) is not an error. For `zh` the tokens are the characters;\n      - `toneErrors` (only `zh`): edit distance between the two lists of tones, one entry per syllable (the tone letters in the syllable's IPA, the empty string for the neutral tone);\n      - `stressHits` (only `en`, `ru`): among the reference words with two or more syllables whose recognised word has the same number of syllables, how many have `stress: 1` on the same syllable;\n      - `timeErrors`: pair the reference and recognised syllables through the edit-distance path over syllable IPA; for each pair with equal IPA collect `|start difference|` and `|end difference|` in ms;\n      - `languageRight`: `heard.languages[0].language === lang` after sorting by `share`, largest first;\n      - `sentenceMark`: the last of `. ? !` in `heard.text`, with `।`, `。`, `？`, `！` mapped to their ASCII form, or `null`.\n3. Create `tests/heavy/roundtrip-sentences.test.js`. Seed 1 everywhere. Runs:\n   - set `main`: all 80 sentences, tiers `telephone`, `narrowband`, `wideband`, `minimal`, presets `male` and `female` (640 runs);\n   - set `voices`: sentences 1 to 5 of each language, presets `any` and `child`, tiers `telephone` and `wideband` (80 runs);\n   - set `tiers`: sentences 2 and 20 of each language, preset `male`, tiers `low`, `medium`, `high`, `ultra`, `studio` (40 runs). `reference` is left out because of its run time; say so in the report.\n   - `heavyLimit(80)` limits the number of sentences per set.\n   - Sum the edit distances and the reference lengths per language, tier and set before dividing; do not average the rates of single sentences.\n4. Gates (one `it` per row, so that a failure names the row). They hold for every language of set `main`:\n\n   | Tier | PER | soundWer | Tone errors | Syllable time, mean | Language right |\n   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n   | `wideband`, `minimal` | ≤ 5 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 30 ms | ≥ 95 % |\n   | `narrowband` | ≤ 8 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 12 % | ≤ 35 ms | ≥ 92 % |\n   | `telephone` | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 20 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 40 ms | ≥ 90 % |\n\n   Set `voices`: the gates of row `telephone` for every preset. Set `tiers`: PER ≤ 10 % per tier. Stress hits ≥ 90 % (`en`, `ru`) from `narrowband` up. `wer`, `cer`, `sentenceMark` and the real-time factor of `recognize` (`seconds` divided by audio seconds) are reported without a gate; the sentence mark gets its gate in #70.\n\n5. Type: **Feature**. Requirements of #11 covered: R6, R17, R18, R19 (see the [case study](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-11/README.md)).\n\n## Goal\n\nRecognition hears the melody of speech, not only the sounds: the four Mandarin tones and the neutral tone, which syllable of a word is stressed, which word is emphasised, and whether a sentence is a statement, a question or an exclamation. The answers are written with the same IPA marks the synthesiser reads (tone letters, `ˈ`, `ˌ`, `.`, `?`, `!`, `↗`, `↘`), and `text` gets punctuation and capital letters.\n\n## Why\n\nThe issue asks for tones, accents and intonation in both directions. Without tones, Mandarin text cannot be chosen: `ma˥` (妈) and `ma˨˩˦` (马) differ only in pitch. Without stress, Russian `за́мок` and `замо́к` are the same. Without the sentence type, `recognize` can never return a question mark.\n\n## Current state\n\n- The synthesiser writes these marks: `textToIpa('Are you coming?')` gives `ˈɑɹ ˈju ˈkʌmɪŋ ?`; `Where are you?` gives `ˈwɛɹ ˈɑɹ ˈju ↘ ?`; `Stop!` gives `ˈstɑp !`; `你好吗？` gives `ni˧˥ xɑʊ˨˩ ma ?`.\n- Tone letters come from `TONE_CONTOURS` in `src/g2p/pinyin.js`: `˥`, `˧˥`, `˨˩˦`, `˨˩` (half third tone), `˥˩`, and nothing for the neutral tone. `parseIpa` turns them into `token.tone`, a list of levels 1 to 5.\n- Pitch of a tone is `(level - 3) * scale` semitones around the base pitch (`syllablePitch()` in `src/articulation/prosody.js`); #49 replaces this by pitch targets that are approached during the syllable, and #51 adds the tunes of sentences (`TUNES`, `FOCUS`) with their sizes in semitones.\n- An exclamation is spoken 1.5 semitones higher, with 1.3 times the pitch range and 1.41 times the amplitude (`REGISTERS.exclamation`).\n- Nothing reads these things from audio. After #59, `trackPitch` gives pitch and voicing per frame; after #66, `audioToIpa` gives sounds with times, without tones, stress or sentence marks.\n- Reference points from the research notes: people identify the four tones of spoken Mandarin 96.4 % right (Jiao and Xu 2019); a 1994 statistical recogniser reached 86.34 % on continuous speech (Wang, Shieh, Chen); people tell Mandarin questions without a particle from statements only 51 to 78 % right.\n\n## What to do\n\nCreate `src/recognition/prosody.js` with two exported functions. The first runs before `ipaToText` (#68), the second after it.\n\n1. `measureProsody(samples, sampleRate, sounds, options)`. `sounds` is the list `{ ipa, start, end, confidence }` made from `audioToIpa`. It returns `{ sounds, pitch, median, range }` where every vowel sound gets two new fields, `tones` and `prominence`:\n   1. Call `trackPitch`. Convert voiced frames to semitones relative to `median`, the median pitch of all voiced frames (or the pitch of `options.voice`). `range` is the 95th minus the 5th percentile, at least 4.\n   2. Syllables: one per vowel sound (the nucleus); the syllable lasts from the nucleus start to the next nucleus start or to the next pause.\n   3. Tones. For each syllable take the voiced frames from the nucleus start to the syllable end and resample them to 10 points. For each tone of `TONE_CONTOURS` (five shapes and the neutral tone) compute the curve the synthesiser would make: call the function of #49 that turns the tone targets into a pitch curve, with the measured pitch at the first point as the starting pitch and `scale = range / 4`. The cost of a tone is the weighted root mean square difference in semitones, divided by 3 and cut at 1; the weight grows linearly from 0.5 at point 1 to 1.5 at point 10 (the end of a syllable is closest to its target). The neutral tone costs 0.3 less when the syllable is shorter than 60 % of the mean of its two neighbours. `tones` is `{ '˥': 0.1, '˧˥': 0.7, ... , '': 0.9 }`; with fewer than 3 voiced frames it is `null`.\n   4. Prominence. For each nucleus measure: duration; mean energy in dB; energy above 500 Hz minus energy below 500 Hz in dB; highest pitch in semitones. Turn each into a z-score over all nuclei of the utterance. `prominence = 0.4 * duration + 0.2 * energy + 0.2 * balance` `+ 0.2 * pitch`.\n2. Let the word search use these fields (`src/recognition/ipa-to-text.js`):\n   - for a candidate word of `zh`, the tone part of the sound distance is `0.5 * sound.tones[tone of the candidate]` when `tones` is not `null`;\n   - for a candidate of `en` or `ru` with two or more syllables, add `0.3` when its syllable with primary stress is not the most prominent of its nuclei. If that file is not in the code base yet, skip this step and say so in the pull request and in a comment on the issue of #68.\n3. `markProsody(result, measured, options)` takes a result in the shape of `recognize` and returns a new one:\n   1. Tones: for `zh` words, `syllables[].ipa` and `word.ipa` carry the tone letters of the chosen word. For a word that is not in the lexicon, write the cheapest tone of `tones`.\n   2. Stress: `syllables[].stress` is the stress of the chosen word. For a word that is not in the lexicon and has two or more syllables, the most prominent syllable gets `stress: 1` and `ˈ`.\n   3. Phrases: cut the words at pauses of 0.2 s or more.\n   4. For the last 250 ms of voiced frames of each phrase compute `rise`: the median of the last 3 frames minus the median of the first 3, in semitones. Also `level` (phrase median minus `median`), `span` (95th minus 5th percentile of the phrase) and `loud` (phrase energy minus utterance energy, dB).\n   5. Decide the mark at the end of each phrase, first rule that fits:\n\n      | Rule | Mark |\n      | --- | --- |\n      | a word of the phrase is a wh-word (`isWhWord` of the language) | `↘ ?` |\n      | `zh`: the last word is `吗`; `hi`: the first word is `क्या` | `?` |\n      | `en`: `rise >= 3`; `hi`: `rise >= 4` | `?` |\n      | `ru`: inside one stressed syllable pitch rises 5 or more and the phrase ends below the start of that syllable | `?` |\n      | `zh`: mean of the last third minus mean of the first third `>= 2` | `?` |\n      | `level >= 1`, `span >= 1.2 * range` and `loud >= 2`, and the utterance has another phrase to compare with | `!` |\n      | the phrase is not the last one and the pause is under 0.5 s | `,` |\n      | anything else | `.` |\n\n      The numbers are the tune sizes of #51, a little smaller. Tune them with the tests and keep the table in the code comment.\n\n   6. Emphasis (`en`, `zh`): a word is emphasised when the pitch peak of its stressed syllable is 2 semitones or more above the line through the peaks of the other stressed syllables of the phrase, and the pitch span after the word is at most half of the span before it. Add `ˈˈ` before the word in `ipa` and a span to `modes` (step 5 below).\n   7. Write the marks into `result.ipa` exactly as `textToIpa` writes them (`,`, `.`, `?`, `!`, `↗ ?`, `↘ ?`), so that `synthesize(result.ipa, { ipa: true })` speaks the same tune.\n   8. Write `result.text`: the mark after the last word of the phrase (`hi`: `।` for `.`; `zh`: `，。？！`, no spaces); in `en` and `ru` the first letter of each sentence becomes a capital letter. Word objects keep their text without punctuation.\n\n4. What cannot be decided is left out, not guessed: a phrase with fewer than 5 voiced frames in its last 250 ms gets `.` at the end of the utterance and nothing elsewhere.\n5. A span in `result.modes` has the shape of `plan.modes` of #50 plus four keys (the same in #71). Example:\n\n   ```text\n   { start: 0.4, end: 0.9, from: 2, to: 3, emphasis: 1,\n     notation: 'ˈˈ', confidence: 0.7 }\n   ```\n\n   `start`, `end` are seconds; `from`, `to` are indexes into `result.words` (`to` exclusive); then only the decided keys of the mode object of #50 (here `emphasis: 1` or `tune: 'yesno'`); `notation` is the IPA mark or `null`; `confidence` is 0 to 1. Every sentence mark other than `.` also adds a span with `tune` (`yesno`, `wh`, `exclamation`, `continuation`).\n\n6. Wiring: if `src/recognition/recognizer.js` (#73) is in the code base, call `measureProsody` after `audioToIpa` and `markProsody` after `ipaToText` when the option `modes` is not `false`. If it is not there, #73 adds the calls. In the round-trip test of #75, if merged, add the gate for `sentenceMark`: at least 90 % right at `wideband` and above, 85 % at `telephone`.\n7. Export both functions from `src/index.js` and add types.\n\n## Tests\n\n`tests/recognition-prosody.test.js`. Audio comes from `synthesize` at tier `minimal`, seed 1, presets `male` and `female`; the true sounds and times come from `timeline`, so the test does not depend on the sound decoder.\n\n- `hears the tone of single syllables`: `妈 麻 马 骂` and `吗` after `好`: the cheapest tone is right for all, both presets.\n- `hears tones in sentences`: 10 Mandarin sentences of 6 to 10 syllables (`tests/fixtures/recognition/tone-sentences.json`, write them here): at least 90 % of the syllables right. Print the 5 by 5 confusion matrix.\n- `hears tones at 8 kHz`: the same after `resample` to 8000 Hz: at least 85 %.\n- `finds the stressed syllable`: 40 English and 40 Russian words of 2 to 4 syllables, each in the frame `say ... again` / `скажи ... снова`: the most prominent nucleus is the stressed one in at least 90 %.\n- `tells the sentence types apart`: 40 sentences, 10 per language: 4 statements, 3 yes/no questions, 2 wh-questions, 1 exclamation after a statement. At least 90 % of the marks are right. Mandarin questions without `吗` are reported apart and have no threshold.\n- `hears emphasis`: `I said *red* car` against `I said red car` (markup of #50): the span is on `red` in the first and absent in the second.\n- `writes text`: `Are you coming?` comes back as `Are you coming?`; `Ты идёшь домой?` as `Ты идёшь домой?`.\n- `leaves out what it cannot hear`: whispered input (no voiced frames) gives `tones: null` everywhere and the mark `.`.\n- `speaks its own marks`: `parseIpa(result.ipa).unknown` is empty.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `npm test` runs `tests/recognition-prosody.test.js` and every threshold above holds on Node.js, Bun and Deno.\n- [ ] The pull request shows the tone confusion matrix at `minimal` and at 8000 Hz, the stress score per language and the sentence-type table.\n- [ ] If #73 is merged: `voice-simulator say \"Are you coming?\" -o q.wav` then `voice-simulator recognize q.wav` prints `Are you coming?`.\n- [ ] The pull request states that tone accuracy on real recordings is not measured here: the benchmark of #76 measures it (`toneErr`) and keeps its own baseline.\n- [ ] `grep -rn \"onnx\\|tensorflow\\|torch\" src/recognition package.json` prints nothing.\n- [ ] `npm run check` and `npm test` pass; a minor changeset is added.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Loudness, voice quality and emotion: #71. Create `tests/helpers/roundtrip.js` exporting `roundTrip(text, options)` with `options = { lang, tier, preset, seed }`. Steps:\n   1. `spoken = synthesize(text, { lang, tier, preset, seed })`.\n   2. `heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level })` with `level = levelForTier(tier)`. Do not pass the language: it must be found.\n   3. Return `{ spoken, heard, seconds }` plus these numbers, computed with `errorRate` and `editDistance` of #18:\n      - `per`: `errorRate(spoken.ipa, heard.ipa, 'phone')`;\n      - `wer` (not for `zh`) and `cer`: `errorRate(text, heard.text, unit)` with `'word'` and `'char'`;\n      - `soundWer`: the same as `wer`, but each word of both texts is first replaced by its IPA from `textToIpa(...).words[].ipa`, so that a word which sounds the same (`sea` and `see`, 他 and 她) is not an error. For `zh` the tokens are the characters;\n      - `toneErrors` (only `zh`): edit distance between the two lists of tones, one entry per syllable (the tone letters in the syllable's IPA, the empty string for the neutral tone);\n      - `stressHits` (only `en`, `ru`): among the reference words with two or more syllables whose recognised word has the same number of syllables, how many have `stress: 1` on the same syllable;\n      - `timeErrors`: pair the reference and recognised syllables through the edit-distance path over syllable IPA; for each pair with equal IPA collect `|start difference|` and `|end difference|` in ms;\n      - `languageRight`: `heard.languages[0].language === lang` after sorting by `share`, largest first;\n      - `sentenceMark`: the last of `. ? !` in `heard.text`, with `।`, `。`, `？`, `！` mapped to their ASCII form, or `null`.\n3. Create `tests/heavy/roundtrip-sentences.test.js`. Seed 1 everywhere. Runs:\n   - set `main`: all 80 sentences, tiers `telephone`, `narrowband`, `wideband`, `minimal`, presets `male` and `female` (640 runs);\n   - set `voices`: sentences 1 to 5 of each language, presets `any` and `child`, tiers `telephone` and `wideband` (80 runs);\n   - set `tiers`: sentences 2 and 20 of each language, preset `male`, tiers `low`, `medium`, `high`, `ultra`, `studio` (40 runs). `reference` is left out because of its run time; say so in the report.\n   - `heavyLimit(80)` limits the number of sentences per set.\n   - Sum the edit distances and the reference lengths per language, tier and set before dividing; do not average the rates of single sentences.\n4. Gates (one `it` per row, so that a failure names the row). They hold for every language of set `main`:\n\n   | Tier | PER | soundWer | Tone errors | Syllable time, mean | Language right |\n   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n   | `wideband`, `minimal` | ≤ 5 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 30 ms | ≥ 95 % |\n   | `narrowband` | ≤ 8 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 12 % | ≤ 35 ms | ≥ 92 % |\n   | `telephone` | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 20 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 40 ms | ≥ 90 % |\n\n   Set `voices`: the gates of row `telephone` for every preset. Set `tiers`: PER ≤ 10 % per tier. Stress hits ≥ 90 % (`en`, `ru`) from `narrowband` up. `wer`, `cer`, `sentenceMark` and the real-time factor of `recognize` (`seconds` divided by audio seconds) are reported without a gate; the sentence mark gets its gate in #70.\n\n5. If the first full run misses a gate, do not loosen it. Read the report (it lists the 20 worst sentences with reference and recognised IPA), fix the stage that loses most, and run again. The gates are the result this issue must deliver.\n6. Mode check, only when `parseMarkup` of #50 is exported (else the test is skipped with the reason in its name): speak sentence 1 of each language once whispered and once loud with the markup of #50; report the share of mode spans that come back in `heard.modes` with the same notation and at least 50 % overlap in time. This issue sets no gate of its own for modes: the numbers belong to #70 (sentence mark), #71 (mode labels) and #72 (set `whisper`). Each of them adds its gate to this test when this test exists. For each of the three that is merged already while its gate is missing here, add the gate in this issue with the numbers of that issue's acceptance criteria.\n7. Write the report with `writeReport('roundtrip', markdown, data)`: one table per set (rows: language × tier; columns: the numbers above), then the 20 worst sentences. Copy the report of the full run to `docs/reports/roundtrip.md` and commit it with the run link, the commit hash and the date at the top.\n8. Smoke test `tests/roundtrip-smoke.test.js` (part of `npm test`): sentence 18 of `en`, 2 of `ru` and 2 of `zh`; tier `telephone`, preset `male`, seed 1. Expect `per.rate \u003c= 0.1`, `soundWer.rate === 0` and `languageRight`.\n9. Add the suite and the report to `tests/heavy/README.md` and to `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` (section \"Heavy checks\").\n\n## Tests\n\n- `tests/roundtrip-smoke.test.js`: the three `it` blocks of step 8, named `round trip en`, `round trip ru`, `round trip zh`.\n- `tests/roundtrip-helper.test.js` (fast, stub recogniser passed as `options.recognize`): `counts a homophone as right` (`sea` heard as `see` gives `wer.distance === 1` and `soundWer.distance === 0`); `counts tones` (one wrong tone letter gives `toneErrors.distance === 1`); `measures syllable times` (a result shifted by 20 ms gives a mean of 20 ms).\n- `has 20 sentences per language`: `sentences.json` has four keys with 20 non-empty strings each and no digit.\n- `tests/heavy/roundtrip-sentences.test.js` as described above.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `node --test tests/roundtrip-smoke.test.js` passes in less than 30 s on one core.\n- [ ] `npm run test:heavy -- --suite roundtrip --limit 2` passes locally and writes `reports/heavy/roundtrip.md`.\n- [ ] A run of `Heavy checks` with `suite=roundtrip` on the pull request branch is green: every gate of step 4 holds. The link is in the pull request description.\n- [ ] `docs/reports/roundtrip.md` is committed and shows, for tier `telephone`, a row for each of the four languages.\n- [ ] `npm run check` and `npm test` pass; a patch changeset is added.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- Real recordings: #76.\n- Deciding the gates for sentence marks, whispered speech, loudness, voice quality and emotion: #70, #71, #72 decide the numbers; step 6 only copies them.\n- The certification of all features at the lowest settings: #81.\n- New sentences. The suite `roundtrip` of the heavy workflow measures how much of the text, the IPA, the syllable times and the language comes back, per audio tier and per preset voice, fails when a threshold is missed, and writes `docs/reports/roundtrip.md`. Three sentences run in every `npm test`.\n\n## Why\n\nRecognition is the simulation in reverse, so the simulator's own speech is the one input for which the right answer is known exactly: text, IPA and the time of every syllable. This is the regression baseline for every later change of the recogniser, and the proof that both directions work at 8000 Hz.\n\n## Current state\n\n- `synthesize(text, options)` returns an object with the keys `lang`, `accent`, `ipa`, `words`, `head`, `plan`, `timeline`, `sampleRate`, `samples` and `duration`. `timeline.words[].syllables[]` holds `ipa`, `stress`, `start`, `end` (seconds) and `text`.\n- Measured on this branch: the three smoke sentences below take 0.11 to 0.27 s each to synthesise at tier `minimal` (22050 Hz, 1.9 to 2.3 s of audio).\n- The 80 sentences were checked with the current text-to-IPA code. They give about 214 s of speech and contain 40 different phone symbols in English, 47 in Russian, 50 in Hindi and 40 in Mandarin, all four Mandarin tones, the half-third tone and the neutral tone, and statements, yes/no questions, question-word questions, exclamations and one-word sentences in each language. There are no digits and no erhua (see #46 and #43).\n- `HEAD_PRESET_NAMES` is `['any', 'male', 'female', 'child']`. Tiers today: `minimal`, `low`, `medium` (waveguide), `high`, `ultra`, `studio`, `reference` (3D). #26 adds `telephone`, `narrowband` and `wideband`.\n- There is no recogniser, so no round-trip test exists: `ls tests/heavy` and `grep -rn roundtrip tests` find nothing.\n\n## What to do\n\n1. Create `tests/helpers/roundtrip.js` exporting `roundTrip(text, options)` with `options = { lang, tier, preset, seed }`. Steps:\n   1. `spoken = synthesize(text, { lang, tier, preset, seed })`.\n   2. `heard = recognize(spoken.samples, spoken.sampleRate, { level })` with `level = levelForTier(tier)`. Do not pass the language: it must be found.\n   3. Return `{ spoken, heard, seconds }` plus these numbers, computed with `errorRate` and `editDistance` of #18:\n      - `per`: `errorRate(spoken.ipa, heard.ipa, 'phone')`;\n      - `wer` (not for `zh`) and `cer`: `errorRate(text, heard.text, unit)` with `'word'` and `'char'`;\n      - `soundWer`: the same as `wer`, but each word of both texts is first replaced by its IPA from `textToIpa(...).words[].ipa`, so that a word which sounds the same (`sea` and `see`, 他 and 她) is not an error. For `zh` the tokens are the characters;\n      - `toneErrors` (only `zh`): edit distance between the two lists of tones, one entry per syllable (the tone letters in the syllable's IPA, the empty string for the neutral tone);\n      - `stressHits` (only `en`, `ru`): among the reference words with two or more syllables whose recognised word has the same number of syllables, how many have `stress: 1` on the same syllable;\n      - `timeErrors`: pair the reference and recognised syllables through the edit-distance path over syllable IPA; for each pair with equal IPA collect `|start difference|` and `|end difference|` in ms;\n      - `languageRight`: `heard.languages[0].language === lang` after sorting by `share`, largest first;\n      - `sentenceMark`: the last of `. ? !` in `heard.text`, with `।`, `。`, `？`, `！` mapped to their ASCII form, or `null`.\n3. Create `tests/heavy/roundtrip-sentences.test.js`. Seed 1 everywhere. Runs:\n   - set `main`: all 80 sentences, tiers `telephone`, `narrowband`, `wideband`, `minimal`, presets `male` and `female` (640 runs);\n   - set `voices`: sentences 1 to 5 of each language, presets `any` and `child`, tiers `telephone` and `wideband` (80 runs);\n   - set `tiers`: sentences 2 and 20 of each language, preset `male`, tiers `low`, `medium`, `high`, `ultra`, `studio` (40 runs). `reference` is left out because of its run time; say so in the report.\n   - `heavyLimit(80)` limits the number of sentences per set.\n   - Sum the edit distances and the reference lengths per language, tier and set before dividing; do not average the rates of single sentences.\n4. Gates (one `it` per row, so that a failure names the row). They hold for every language of set `main`:\n\n   | Tier | PER | soundWer | Tone errors | Syllable time, mean | Language right |\n   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n   | `wideband`, `minimal` | ≤ 5 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 30 ms | ≥ 95 % |\n   | `narrowband` | ≤ 8 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 12 % | ≤ 35 ms | ≥ 92 % |\n   | `telephone` | ≤ 10 % | ≤ 20 % | ≤ 15 % | ≤ 40 ms | ≥ 90 % |\n\n   Set `voices`: the gates of row `telephone` for every preset. Set `tiers`: PER ≤ 10 % per tier. Stress hits ≥ 90 % (`en`, `ru`) from `narrowband` up. `wer`, `cer`, `sentenceMark` and the real-time factor of `recognize` (`seconds` divided by audio seconds) are reported without a gate; the sentence mark gets its gate in #70.\n\n5. If the first full run misses a gate, do not loosen it. Read the report (it lists the 20 worst sentences with reference and recognised IPA), fix the stage that loses most, and run again. The gates are the result this issue must deliver.\n6. Mode check, only when `parseMarkup` of #50 is exported (else the test is skipped with the reason in its name): speak sentence 1 of each language once whispered and once loud with the markup of #50; report the share of mode spans that come back in `heard.modes` with the same notation and at least 50 % overlap in time. This issue sets no gate of its own for modes: the numbers belong to #70 (sentence mark), #71 (mode labels) and #72 (set `whisper`). Each of them adds its gate to this test when this test exists. For each of the three that is merged already while its gate is missing here, add the gate in this issue with the numbers of that issue's acceptance criteria.\n7. Write the report with `writeReport('roundtrip', markdown, data)`: one table per set (rows: language × tier; columns: the numbers above), then the 20 worst sentences. Copy the report of the full run to `docs/reports/roundtrip.md` and commit it with the run link, the commit hash and the date at the top.\n8. The correct consonant ranked first in all eight observations per tier with the correct voice and timing, even when using the wrong question tune. Changing the next vowel, voice seed, timing, and ending together cut first-place cepstral ranks to three of eight at telephone and four of eight at wideband. The probe used the reference phone durations and the rest of the IPA. [Context probe](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/issue-75-d83d002e01c2/docs/reports/roundtrip.md#scoring-consonants-in-a-rendered-phrase) · [Halle and Stevens](https://web.mit.edu/morrishalle/pubworks/papers/1964_Halle_Stevens_Speech_Recognition_Model_Program_for_Research.pdf)\\n- The stop-closure probe found 122 frames with a spectral centroid below 50 Hz marked as speech. Marking those frames as gaps or filtering at 70 Hz or 140 Hz did not recover the inherited /p/ closure case. Both filters increased edits in four telephone sentences from 44 to 47 over 54 reference phones. The probe and its commands are committed in `cf4f3d5`. [Stop-closure measurements](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/cf4f3d57d81b9b50a33751a49a0a280778d48949/docs/reports/roundtrip.md#stop-closure-detection)\\n- The audio-only telephone mode check recovers four whisper spans and zero loud spans. It needs six of eight matches at telephone and eight of eight at the gated higher tiers. Issue #71's utterance-relative baseline prohibits effort labels for a whole utterance without a supplied voice. Issue #75 scores whole sentences with audio and a tier level. The earlier probe with the correct voice and word times still recovered only two of four telephone loud spans and one of four wideband loud spans. The six-of-eight telephone threshold exceeds the four marks that can be returned under #71's no-voice rule. Satisfying both criteria requires a specification decision about the baseline or benchmark inputs. [Mode specification](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/issues/71) · [Mode results and commands](https://github.com/konard/voice-simulator/blob/issue-75-d83d002e01c2/docs/reports/roundtrip.md#whole-sentence-loudness)\\n\\n## Default branch\\n\\nCurrent `main` at `0e18bc0` fails all nine runtime jobs on pre-existing strict acceptance tests.
